chapters.title: Chapter 1: The Second Failure
paragraphs: [ Awakening Failed.]
The middle-aged woman’s voice echoed through the hall; quiet, flat, and emotionless, as if those few words couldn’t possibly crush someone’s future.
The young man standing in front of the purple sphere froze for a few seconds.
His fingers were still on the clear surface of the sphere, and the weak purple light passed through the gaps between his fingers.
It was like he was in shock, or for some reason his ears couldn’t process what he had just heard. Or at least the news was so painful that his brain preferred to pretend it hadn’t heard it.
Then he let out a long sigh, his shoulders dropped, and he stepped aside without a word.
Whispers immediately rose in the hall.
"That was his second time, right?"
"Yeah... I heard his father Awakened as a C-rank with a two-star class."
"What bad luck... If he could have gotten a two-star class like his father, he could have lived the rest of his life without worrying about money."
The boy lowered his head and walked through the crowd; just like the dozens of others who had walked the same path during the past hour.
The secondary awakening hall of the National Academy was always like this.
Stuffy and heavy, full of hopes that were slowly being extinguished.
Unlike the main hall, which was for geniuses and newly awakened students, this was the place for those who had been rejected by the world once... but still weren’t ready to give up.
On both sides of the hall were rows of metal chairs. Young people with anxious faces, families who had fallen silent, and looks trapped between hope and fear.
In the middle of the hall, a huge purple sphere sat on a silver-colored platform. The sphere was filled with mana, and an amazing amount of this magical energy radiated from its surface.
Of course, it was this mana that made the awakening process possible. A person can only experience the awakening process when their body comes into contact with a very large amount of mana.
The test administrator took a quick look at her list.
"Next."
A girl with short pink hair stepped forward. She paused for a moment before placing her palm on the sphere, as if she was afraid of failing again.
But if she failed, what then? Would her future be destroyed?
A few seconds of silence filled the hall, and then a faint blue light glowed inside the sphere.
The girl’s eyes went wide.
The sphere suddenly became brighter, and glowing lines formed on its surface.
[Awakening Successful.]
[Class Awakened]
[Class: Mage (2 star)]
The crowd reacted immediately.
"She did it!"
"What’s her rank?"
"At least 1 Star or higher, it seems."
An unbelieving smile appeared on the girl’s face. Her hand was shaking. For many people, this moment was the border between two lives.
A normal life and the life of an Awakened.

"Congratulations on your awakening. You have obtained a two-star Mage class. You can see information about your talent in your panel," the middle-aged woman explained lazily, then gestured for the girl to step aside.
"Thank you so much!!" The pink-haired girl bowed happily and excitedly, then went toward her family.
Lian watched that scene from the end of the hall in silence.
His hands were in the pockets of his black jacket, and he was leaning against the cold wall. His appearance looked calmer than he really was.
But only he knew how heavy his heartbeat had become.
Two hundred and fifty years had passed since the day the gates opened. Since the day the world’s sky changed, and since the day monsters crawled out of dark cracks and swallowed cities.
In those days, humanity was pushed to the brink of destruction, until "The Will" appeared.
No one knew exactly what it was. A god? A system? The will of the world?
But that unknown thing was what gave awakening to humans. The power that allowed them to resist the monsters.
And since then, everything had changed.
Power was no longer just power. It was identity, it was status, and it was worth.
And those who failed to become an awakened were almost always pushed to the margins.

Although their country was more or less in a better situation, because of that disaster, many countries collapsed, hundreds of millions of people were killed, and even now, large parts of the world are unsafe and dangerous.
"Hey, do you see that guy?"
The whispering of two people near Lian grew louder.
"Which one?"
"The one over there... in the black jacket."
A few looks turned toward him.
"Wait..."
One of the boys’ eyes widened a little.
"Isn’t that Lian Vonhelm?"
There was a short silence, and then the whispers grew louder.
"Damn... it’s him."
"The only son of the Vonhelm family whose awakening failed?"
"I thought it was a rumor."
"I heard that even after his failure, he didn’t give up and trained for two years."
"Well, apparently he still hasn’t accepted that he’s a normal person."
Lian didn’t react. Not because he was used to it, but because he no longer had the energy to care.
The Vonhelm family was not a small name. They were incredibly well-known both nationally and globally.
And precisely because of that, Lian’s failure stood out even more.
The first awakening process happens at age 16, and each person can only go through the awakening process twice in their life. If the first fails, you can always try a second time.
But almost 99% of people who fail the first time will also fail the second time, and there is no third time, because a normal human body cannot handle the shock of mana three times.
And he had failed to become an Awakened. He was considered a stain on their family name.
The woman in charge, without paying attention to the whispers, read the next name.
"Lian Vonhelm."
The hall went quiet for a moment. Lian pulled away from the wall and walked toward the platform.
His somewhat tall height made him easy to see even in a crowd.
His black hair had fallen slightly over his forehead, and his eyes were... darker than they should be for an eighteen-year-old.
Many looks followed him.
Some curious, some mocking, and some just waiting for failure. In the past, he was seen as a little celebrity with a great future.
But failing the awakening process had turned all that admiration from back then into mockery. Mockery that almost seemed born from jealousy.
Lian stood in front of the sphere. Its purple surface pulsed in silence.
This was his last chance.
After eighteen, you were no longer allowed to apply for a second awakening.
Meaning if he failed today, it was over.
"Put your hand on the sphere," the woman in charge said impatiently.
Lian breathed slowly and placed his palm on the cold surface of the sphere.
At that moment, light exploded.
The entire hall was flooded with purple brightness. The crowd stepped back in shock.
The sphere began to shake. Glowing lines moved across its surface at a crazy speed.
For the first time, the woman in charge’s eyes widened a little.
Even Lian froze for a moment.
His heart pounded hard. After two years... maybe?
But then the notifications appeared.
[Awakening Failed.]
The light suddenly flickered.
[Error! ERROR! Error 44##]
[Error! Error!]
[Subject Not Registered Within The System.]
Silence. Several full seconds. No one said a word. Lian stared motionless at the floating words.
They were familiar. Exactly the same messages and the same errors. The same thing he had seen two years ago, and back then they had just said it was a problem with the device.
"...Did the device malfunction?" The woman in charge frowned and looked at the sphere a few times. This sphere was one of the best of its kind and could even handle the pressure of a five-star class.
So what was going on?
But she was too lazy to care. Then she shrugged.
"Awakening failed. Next."
As if nothing special had happened, the whispers started again.
"Huh? What was that Error?"
"Doesn’t matter. It ended in fail anyway."
"The Vonhelm family should really be ashamed."
"What an insult to that name."
"Now I understand why his fiancée left him..."
"That girl got a three-star class! How could she be with a nobody?"
Lian slowly lifted his hand from the sphere.
A strange feeling twisted inside his chest. It wasn’t anger or sadness. It was just... emptiness.
The last small hope had gone out. All this time, part of him had still been hopeful.
Hopeful that maybe the second time would be different. Maybe those errors meant something else.
Maybe there was finally a place for him in this world.
But now it was really over. He had no talent. He had no awakening.
And from tomorrow, he would just be an ordinary Analyzer at the academy. A normal person, in a world that no longer had a place for normal people.
Lian stepped down from the platform without a word. The sound of whispers still flowed behind him.
But he didn’t care anymore. He just wanted to get out of that hall.
Just as he reached the exit, his phone vibrated. Lian glanced at the screen.
A familiar name appeared on the screen. He answered the call.
"Are you finally done?" A boy’s voice came from the other end.
Lian was silent for a moment.
"Yeah." Then he said quietly.
"Good. I’m waiting for you in front of the academy entrance."
The call ended. Lian stared at the dark phone screen for a few seconds, then opened the hall door and went out.

chapters.title: Chapter 2: The Ruined Realms
paragraphs: The air outside the hall was cooler than Lian expected.
The metal doors closed behind him, and the heavy noise of the hall disappeared in an instant.
For a few seconds he just stood there; his hands in his pockets, his gaze fixed on the wide grounds of the National Academy.
The white and silver colored buildings shone under the evening light. Stone paths, neat gardens, training towers, and students moving around in black and blue uniforms.
A place where the future of the country’s Awakened was built, and a place he had practically no connection to.
But luckily, the job of an Analyzer did not require you to be an Awakened. Anyone could become an Analyzer, and he had one of the highest scores in this field.
"You finally came."
Lian turned his head.
A boy with dark brown hair was sitting on the railings by the stairs, holding a cold drink bottle. His face was calm, and his usual half-mocking smile was there.
Kain Mercer, his childhood friend, and one of the few people who still treated him like a normal person.
Kain tossed the second bottle toward him. Lian caught it without effort.
"So?"
"People still love watching others fail." Lian opened the bottle and took a sip.
"At least the device didn’t explode this time." Kain laughed. During Lian’s first awakening attempt, the sphere had exploded. Of course, everyone thought it was because the sphere had a problem.
"That’s a big improvement." Lian gave him a dry look.
Kain jumped down from the railing and locked his hands behind his back.
"Well, let’s take a walk around before the ceremony starts. You still haven’t seen half the academy."
Lian didn’t object. The two entered the academy’s main path.
The hallways of the National Academy looked more like a military facility than a school.
Holographic screens on the walls showed student rankings, and logos of famous guilds appeared on advertisement banners.
<BLACK FLAG Guild>
<Astral Union Recruitment>
<Valen Corporation Talent Program>
A few students were fighting in the training area. One of them blew up a metal dummy with his flaming fist, and cheers from those around grew loud.
Lian turned his gaze away without interest.
"Does it still get on your nerves?" Kain had noticed his short look.
"No." His answer was quick, too quick.
Kain said nothing. Even though they were childhood friends, he really didn’t know what was going on in Lian’s mind.
When they reached the central building, more people were seen.
Most students were moving toward the assembly hall, where the Student Council President and his Vice President were going to give a speech for the new students.
"I heard the President himself is coming this year. Seems like the Tenth Realm thing is pretty serious." Kain said as he put his hands into his uniform pockets.
"People say that every time, but if we’re lucky, this could be the last one." Lian shrugged.
They entered the huge hall.
Long rows of seats continued up near the main platform, and white light shone in through the glass ceiling.
Lian and Kain sat in the middle rows. At that moment, Lian’s gaze fixed on a girl in the first row.
Long light brown hair, a calm face, and a neat academy uniform.
Elena Hartwell.
His ex-girlfriend.
His girlfriend, or, more accurately, his ex-fiancée, who unfortunately or fortunately tore up their engagement contract and called off the engagement.
She believed that the two of them no longer belonged to the same world, and that marrying him would only hold back her future progress.
Next to her sat a tall boy with dark gray hair. The special uniform for top students had a four-star gold badge on his shoulder.
Roderick Ashn.
"After you two broke up, she got into a relationship with Roderick." Kain followed Lian’s gaze and let out a short sigh.
Lian said nothing.
"That guy’s a monster. He got a four-star class. They say several top-rank guilds have already sent him offers." Kain continued.
"And Elena has a three-star class. Although it’s not as rare as four-star... she’s still considered one of the best."
Lian was quiet for a few seconds.
"The new realm comes tonight, right?" he then said quietly.
Kain understood that he had purposely changed the subject and played along.
"Yeah." His voice was more serious this time.
"The Tenth Realm."
Even those around them were talking about the same thing.
Tonight, the sky would change again.
Two hundred and fifty years ago, the first realm had entered Earth’s dimensional orbit. At first, people thought it was something like a new planet or moon.
But they soon realized they were wrong. Those were worlds. Ruined realms that appeared in the sky like moons.
And through gates connected to those realms, monsters had entered Earth.
According to realm specialists, those worlds once had advanced civilizations.
Cities, empires, civilizations that were now just ruins full of monsters.
No one knew where those creatures had come from, only that they had destroyed everything.
Even now, each realm was like a game-like world, at least for the Awakened. The difference was, if you got killed there, you really died.
"So far nine realms have appeared, and humanity has cleared all nine." Kain looked at the glass ceiling of the hall.
"They all think the tenth is the last." Lian said quietly.
"They hope." Actually, this wasn’t just an empty claim. There were reasons and theories behind it.
Kain paused, then gave him a side look.
"But the scary part is always the first night."
Lian said nothing. There was no need. Every child in the world knew the story of the first night. The night a new realm appeared, twenty-five thousand people would vanish randomly.
From all over the world, old, young, Awakened, normal. There was no rule. They would be summoned directly to the new realm.
Like sacrifices. And almost no one ever came back alive.
"Do you think you’ll get summoned tonight?" Kain suddenly laughed.
"I don’t think I’m that unlucky." Lian gave a short laugh too.
At that moment, the noise in the hall quieted down. Several people appeared on the main platform.
The Student Council President stood in the center. A handsome boy in a formal white uniform with the golden Student Council badge on his chest.
But Lian’s attention did not stay on him.
Instead, it fixed on the tall girl standing next to him. Long black hair, a cold face, and icy eyes.
Seraphina.
His childhood friend, and now the Vice President of the Student Council.
Their eyes met for a brief moment, but what Lian saw in that look was only coldness and anger.
"She’s still angry at you, huh?" Kain laughed quietly.
"Apparently." Lian sighed.
"Well, what did you expect?" Kain shrugged.
Lian didn’t answer.
The speech began, but he barely listened to any of it.
His mind was too tired to care about hopeful words about the future, honor, and the new generation.
After the ceremony ended, the crowd slowly started leaving the hall.
Lian and Kain also headed toward the exit, but just before reaching the doors, someone blocked their way.
"Haha... Lian? Is that you?" Roderick Ashn stood in front of them with a smile on his face.
Elena was nowhere to be seen. Either she had already left the hall or had gone somewhere else.
"How many people do you think have a face as handsome as mine?" Lian gave him a short look and said quietly.
"I didn’t think I’d see you again after high school. And it seems you’re still the same self-obsessed jerk." Roderick laughed.
"Well... what are you doing here? Did you become an Awakened?"
He paused for a few seconds, then laughed himself.
"Though I doubt it."
Lian didn’t react.
Roderick’s gaze went down and fixed on the name tag on Lian’s chest.
Lian Vonhelm
"Oh? You still kept that family name?" His eyebrow rose a little.
Just as he was about to continue, a boy hurried toward him.
"Mr. Ashn, the Student Council President wants to see you."
Roderick clicked his tongue against his teeth, and before leaving, he got a little closer to Lian.
His voice lowered.
"You know... trash like you doesn’t deserve that family name." His smile deepened.
"So you better throw it away before people make fun of you because of it."
Then he straightened up.
"See you later."
And left.
A few seconds of silence remained between Lian and Kain.
"What did he tell you?" Kain finally asked.
"Nothing." Lian sighed
That night, after dinner, the dorms were quieter than ever. Everyone was waiting for the Tenth Realm to appear.
"You really don’t want to see it?" Kain stood by the window.
He and Lian shared a dorm. Their dorm was like a modern one, with two normal beds, a bathroom, and a closet for their clothes.
"No." Lian was lying on his bed with his eyes closed.
"What a buzzkill. Come on, it’s the Tenth Realm after all." Kain laughed.
"It’s just one more star added to the sky. Nothing special." Lian said without opening his eyes.
Kain mumbled under his breath.
But Lian was no longer listening. Today had been long. Academy registration, the awakening test, and then the speech.
And unlike the Awakened, his body was still that of a normal person. Fatigue came to him much sooner.
He fell asleep quietly in the darkness. He hoped that at least unlike the day, he could have a restful sleep.
Time passed slowly, and when he opened his eyes again, a strong stench filled his nose.
Something heavy was pressing down on his body. Breathing was hard.
Lian moved his hand with a frown. A warm, thick liquid spread on his skin.
Blood!
His eyes suddenly opened wide. A reddish darkness covered everything around him.
He struggled and pulled himself forward, and finally his head came out from under something.
And then his body froze. He was trapped in the middle of a mountain of monster corpses. Thousands of carcasses piled on top of each other!
Some were huge, some were torn apart. The smell of blood and death filled the entire space.
The sky above him was red. No sun was seen, no moon either. Just red darkness.
"...I’m not really that unlucky, right?" Lian’s lips moved quietly.
At that moment, a glowing screen appeared in front of his eyes.
[You Have Been Selected As One Of The 25,000 Sacrifices]
[Welcome To The Ruined Realm]

Long rows of seats continued up near the main platform, and white light shone in through the glass ceiling.
Lian and Kain sat in the middle rows.
At that moment, Lian’s gaze fixed on a girl in the first row.
Long light brown hair, a calm face, and a neat academy uniform.
Elena Hartwell.
His ex-girlfriend.
His girlfriend, or, more accurately, his ex-fiancée, who unfortunately or fortunately tore up their engagement contract and called off the engagement.
She believed that the two of them no longer belonged to the same world, and that marrying him would only hold back her future progress.
Next to her sat a tall boy with dark gray hair.
The special uniform for top students had a four-star gold badge on his shoulder.
Roderick Ashn.
"After you two broke up, she got into a relationship with Roderick." Kain followed Lian’s gaze and let out a short sigh.
Lian said nothing.
"That guy’s a monster.
He got a four-star class.
They say several top-rank guilds have already sent him offers." Kain continued.
"And Elena has a three-star class.
Although it’s not as rare as four-star... she’s still considered one of the best."
Lian was quiet for a few seconds.
"The new realm comes tonight, right?" he then said quietly.
Kain understood that he had purposely changed the subject and played along.
"Yeah." His voice was more serious this time.
"The Tenth Realm."
Even those around them were talking about the same thing.
Tonight, the sky would change again.
Two hundred and fifty years ago, the first realm had entered Earth’s dimensional orbit.
At first, people thought it was something like a new planet or moon.
But they soon realized they were wrong.
Those were worlds.
Ruined realms that appeared in the sky like moons.
And through gates connected to those realms, monsters had entered Earth.
According to realm specialists, those worlds once had advanced civilizations.
Cities, empires, civilizations that were now just ruins full of monsters.
No one knew where those creatures had come from, only that they had destroyed everything.
Even now, each realm was like a game-like world, at least for the Awakened.
The difference was, if you got killed there, you really died.
"So far nine realms have appeared, and humanity has cleared all nine." Kain looked at the glass ceiling of the hall.
"They all think the tenth is the last." Lian said quietly.
"They hope." Actually, this wasn’t just an empty claim.
There were reasons and theories behind it.
Kain paused, then gave him a side look.
"But the scary part is always the first night."
Lian said nothing.
There was no need.
Every child in the world knew the story of the first night.
The night a new realm appeared, twenty-five thousand people would vanish randomly.
From all over the world, old, young, Awakened, normal.
There was no rule.
They would be summoned directly to the new realm.
Like sacrifices.
And almost no one ever came back alive.
"Do you think you’ll get summoned tonight?" Kain suddenly laughed.
"I don’t think I’m that unlucky." Lian gave a short laugh too.
At that moment, the noise in the hall quieted down.
Several people appeared on the main platform.
The Student Council President stood in the center.
A handsome boy in a formal white uniform with the golden Student Council badge on his chest.
But Lian’s attention did not stay on him.
Instead, it fixed on the tall girl standing next to him.
Long black hair, a cold face, and icy eyes.
Seraphina.
His childhood friend, and now the Vice President of the Student Council.
Their eyes met for a brief moment, but what Lian saw in that look was only coldness and anger.
"She’s still angry at you, huh?" Kain laughed quietly.
"Apparently." Lian sighed.
"Well, what did you expect?" Kain shrugged.
Lian didn’t answer.
The speech began, but he barely listened to any of it.
His mind was too tired to care about hopeful words about the future, honor, and the new generation.
After the ceremony ended, the crowd slowly started leaving the hall.
Lian and Kain also headed toward the exit, but just before reaching the doors, someone blocked their way.
"Haha...
Lian?
Is that you?" Roderick Ashn stood in front of them with a smile on his face.
Elena was nowhere to be seen.
Either she had already left the hall or had gone somewhere else.
"How many people do you think have a face as handsome as mine?" Lian gave him a short look and said quietly.
"I didn’t think I’d see you again after high school.
And it seems you’re still the same self-obsessed jerk." Roderick laughed.
"Well... what are you doing here?
Did you become an Awakened?"
He paused for a few seconds, then laughed himself.
"Though I doubt it."
Lian didn’t react.
Roderick’s gaze went down and fixed on the name tag on Lian’s chest.
Lian Vonhelm
"Oh?
You still kept that family name?" His eyebrow rose a little.
Just as he was about to continue, a boy hurried toward him.
"Mr.
Ashn, the Student Council President wants to see you."
Roderick clicked his tongue against his teeth, and before leaving, he got a little closer to Lian.
His voice lowered.
"You know... trash like you doesn’t deserve that family name." His smile deepened.
"So you better throw it away before people make fun of you because of it."
Then he straightened up.
"See you later."
And left.
A few seconds of silence remained between Lian and Kain.
"What did he tell you?" Kain finally asked.
"Nothing." Lian sighed
That night, after dinner, the dorms were quieter than ever.
Everyone was waiting for the Tenth Realm to appear.
"You really don’t want to see it?" Kain stood by the window.
He and Lian shared a dorm.
Their dorm was like a modern one, with two normal beds, a bathroom, and a closet for their clothes.
"No." Lian was lying on his bed with his eyes closed.
"What a buzzkill.
Come on, it’s the Tenth Realm after all." Kain laughed.
"It’s just one more star added to the sky.
Nothing special." Lian said without opening his eyes.
Kain mumbled under his breath.
But Lian was no longer listening.
Today had been long.
Academy registration, the awakening test, and then the speech.
And unlike the Awakened, his body was still that of a normal person.
Fatigue came to him much sooner.
He fell asleep quietly in the darkness.
He hoped that at least unlike the day, he could have a restful sleep.
Time passed slowly, and when he opened his eyes again, a strong stench filled his nose.
Something heavy was pressing down on his body.
Breathing was hard.
Lian moved his hand with a frown.
A warm, thick liquid spread on his skin.
Blood!
His eyes suddenly opened wide.
A reddish darkness covered everything around him.
He struggled and pulled himself forward, and finally his head came out from under something.
And then his body froze.
He was trapped in the middle of a mountain of monster corpses.
Thousands of carcasses piled on top of each other!
Some were huge, some were torn apart.
The smell of blood and death filled the entire space.
The sky above him was red.
No sun was seen, no moon either.
Just red darkness.
"...I’m not really that unlucky, right?" Lian’s lips moved quietly.
At that moment, a glowing screen appeared in front of his eyes.
[You Have Been Selected As One Of The 25,000 Sacrifices]
[Welcome To The Ruined Realm]

chapters.title: Chapter 3: Unluckier than I thought
paragraphs: The first thing Lian felt was the smell of blood.
Not the normal smell of blood, but a smell that was thick, rotten, and heavy, as if it was crawling straight into his lungs.
Breathing was hard.
Something heavy was pressing down on his body, and every time he tried to move, he felt soft, slimy flesh crushing under his hands.
His eyes slowly opened. A reddish darkness covered everything around him.
For a few seconds, his mind was still stuck between sleep and reality. But soon the sticky coldness of a liquid that slid across his face removed whatever was left of his sleep.
Lian raised his hand.
Blood.
His whole hand was blood.
He frowned and struggled to move his body. Something like a bone broke under his foot, and the sound of it cracking echoed in the darkness.
His heartbeat got a little faster. He pushed himself forward with more force, and suddenly his head came out from inside a heavy pile.
Cold, smelly air hit his face, and then his body froze.
Around him... was a mountain of corpses.
Thousands of carcasses piled on top of each other. Some were huge, some were half torn apart, some so big that it was hard to even tell their original shape.
Dead eyes, broken horns, and teeth as big as a human forearm.
A narrow river of blood flowed between the corpses and passed by his feet. The blood looked mostly dry.
For a few seconds he just stared. Even his mind could not fully understand the scale of what he was seeing.
Then he slowly crawled out from among the corpses. Every step he took was followed by the sound of flesh crushing or bones breaking.
Lian finally stood on somewhat flatter ground and took a deep breath.
But that was the wrong move. The stench went straight into his throat, and he had to turn his face away.
The sky above him was red. No sun was seen, no moon either. Just a huge layer of dark red clouds moving slowly, as if the sky itself was alive.
And worse than anything, there was no sound. No wind, no insect, no bird. Just the dripping of blood.
Lian was quiet for a few seconds, then the glowing screen appeared in front of him again.
[You Have Been Selected As One Of The 25,000 Sacrifices]
[Welcome To The Ruined Realm]
"...Damn it." His eyes narrowed.
So he really had been summoned.
One of those twenty-five thousand people. The same sacrifices who almost never came back alive.
"Did I get cursed without knowing it?" He sighed. With all the bad luck he had experienced, he didn’t think he would be unlucky enough to be summoned to these ruins!
It’s not that no one can come back alive from the first summoning. It’s just that it’s very hard. Very, very hard. Especially for a normal person like him. Completely impossible.
Lian slowly let out his breath and tried to organize his mind. Panicking would not help.
If he was going to survive, he first had to understand his situation. His gaze scanned the area again.
He was at the bottom of a huge valley.
Walls of black stone rose from both sides, and a faint red mist flowed between them. Huge bones stuck out from the walls, as if gigantic creatures had once been buried inside this place.
"So this is one of the ruined realms..." Lian said quietly to himself.
According to public information, each realm was a destroyed world. Worlds that once had civilizations.
They had cities. They had life. And now they were just ruins full of monsters. No one knew exactly where those monsters came from.
Only that after they appeared, every world had turned into hell.
Lian took his gaze off the sky and looked around again. The most important thing now was to find the "key."
The only way out of the realm.
Keys were usually in specific places. For example, in mountain areas they were always at the top of the highest peak. Or in war zones, in the deepest part of the forest.
But here there was nothing. Just mountains of corpses and blood. A lot of blood.
"This is not normal..." Lian’s frown got deeper.
Even for a newly appeared realm, this amount of carcasses was unusual.
It was as if a huge war had happened right here.
Or, his gaze slowly moved over the broken bones.
...This place was the feeding ground of something.
An uncomfortable pressure twisted inside his chest. Without realizing it, he slowly moved away from the mountain of corpses.
The farther he got, the more he could see the valley’s true shape.
The ground was covered in cracked black stones, and trails of blood flowed between them like red veins. In some places, broken weapons could be seen among the carcasses.
Swords.
Spears.
Pieces of armor.
Lian paused. So other humans had died here too. But there were no human corpses or human blood.
His gaze fell on a corner of the valley in the distance. A huge bone was stuck in a rock, which had caused the rock to crack and its base to become loose.
He looked around. It seemed that if that rock fell, it could also damage the rest of the valley walls.
"This might be the territory of a powerful monster," he whispered to himself. He felt his guess was right, because the monster blood didn’t look very old.
And that led to only one conclusion. He had to get out of here as soon as possible and go somewhere safe.
But was there anywhere safe in these ruins?
His gaze suddenly fixed on something. A narrow path could be seen between the valley walls. A winding stone route that went upward.
The only exit he had seen so far. His heartbeat calmed down a little. At least this place was not completely closed off.
Lian took a few steps toward the path.
But at that moment, a sound came.
Tak.
The sound of something heavy hitting stone.
His body immediately froze. A few seconds of complete silence passed.
Then again.
Tak.
This time closer.
And then he heard heavy, rough breathing. Something was coming down the path.
Lian slowly raised his head.
At first, only a huge shadow was seen in the red mist. Then a large claw placed itself on the stone.
Blood dripped from its dark fur. And then... that thing came fully out of the mist.
The monster looked like a wolf, but only in the most basic shape.
Its body was the size of an elephant. Huge muscles moved under its black, blood-soaked fur. Large, twisted horns like those of a deer stuck out from its head.
Its whole body was covered in wounds. Marks from deep sword cuts and torn flesh. Part of its side looked like it had been ripped off.
But despite its condition, it was still alive. The monster’s bloody eyes fixed on Lian.
And at that moment, a deep instinct inside Lian screamed.
Death.
If he ran, he would die.
If he fought, he would die.
Even if he didn’t move, he would still die.
He looked at that creature. At the monster that looked like it had come out of a nightmare.
The monster slowly pulled back its lips.
A row of long, curved teeth, like those of prehistoric tigers, was revealed. Blood dripped from its fangs.
And then it looked at its new prey with hunger.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Battle Without Victory
paragraphs: The monster suddenly smiled. A smile like it was thanking for seeing a free meal.
That scene was so unnatural that for a moment, even Lian’s brain could not react.
Blood dripped from the creature’s huge fangs and fell onto the black stones below the valley.
Its breaths were heavy and uneven. Every time its chest rose, a muffled sound like bones crushing could be heard from inside its body.
But despite all those wounds, it was still alive. And it could still tear him apart.
Lian did not move. His black eyes moved across the monster’s body.
Its left leg was limping.
Its side had a deep tear. Its neck had three sword wound marks. Heavy bleeding. And more important than anything, the speed of its breathing.
"This thing... should be dead." Even if this monster did not die right now, it did not have much life left in it. At most, it would die in a few hours.
What could have brought this monster to such a state? Based on the sword marks, it was clearly the work of a sword user. But someone from this world’s possible inhabitants?
Or one of the 25,000 summoned?
The monster suddenly let out a deep growl from its throat. The valley shook. And then it moved. It only took a moment.
Its huge body jumped toward Lian like a bloody shadow. Lian’s eyes widened, and he threw himself to the side.
BOOM!
Where he had been standing exploded. Black stones were thrown in all directions.
The shockwave dragged Lian’s body across the ground.
"Damn it...!" He barely kept his balance and ran without looking back.
The sound of the monster’s heavy claws echoed behind him.
TAK!
TAK!
TAK!
Every step of that creature shook the valley.
Lian moved through the mountain of corpses. Several times he almost slipped on blood and flesh.
The stench filled everything. The sound of the monster’s breaths got closer every moment.
Suddenly he saw something by his foot. A broken sword. Without thinking, he picked it up and turned. At that same moment, the monster jumped out of the red mist.
Lian threw the broken blade toward the creature’s eye. The monster moved its head a little. The blade did not even enter its eye. It just broke on the bone next to its face.
But that moment was enough. Lian threw himself behind a pile of carcasses.
BOOM!
The monster crashed straight into the mountain of corpses. A wave of flesh and blood sprayed into the air.
Lian, breathing heavily, crouched behind a huge carcass. His heart was pounding like crazy. He had no chance in a direct fight.
None. Even the monster being wounded did not change the truth.
He was just a normal person. No awakening. No mana. No power. If he took even one direct hit, he would die.
The monster’s angry growl sounded again. And then...
Silence.
Lian frowned. Why wasn’t it attacking? A drop of blood ran down from his forehead. His eyes slowly scanned the area.
And at that moment, he realized the monster was searching by smell. Its bloody eyes moved unsteadily. Its pupils had no focus.
"Its eyesight is weak..." It had probably lost too much blood. That had affected its full ability and its senses.
"If that’s the case... maybe I can test him." Remembering a spot in this valley, an idea came to his mind.
But he was not sure if it would work or not.
Lian slowly moved back. Then suddenly he threw a large piece of bone to the other side.
TAK!
The monster immediately turned and attacked toward the sound. The ground shook. Lian used the chance and ran.
His eyes wildly scanned the area. He was clearly looking for a place. A place where he could find a way to kill that thing... that monster.
And then he saw it. Part of the valley wall was cracked.
A huge bone was stuck between the rocks. The entire upper part looked unstable.
Lian’s eyes narrowed.
"There it is."
The monster’s roar echoed behind him. The creature had realized it had been tricked. Lian ran straight toward the wall.
The sound of the monster’s claws got closer and closer. Their distance was less than ten meters.
Five meters.
Three meters.
He could feel the creature’s hot breath on the back of his neck. Just before reaching it, Lian threw himself to the ground.
And the monster jumped.
BOOOM!
Its whole huge body hit the cracked wall.
For one second, nothing happened.
Then the sound of breaking came.
CRAAACK—
The monster’s bloody eyes widened a little. And then the whole wall collapsed. Huge stones fell down. The giant bone was freed and fell from above like a white spear.
The monster let out an angry roar and tried to move back. But it was too late.
The bone went straight through its side. Black blood sprayed out like an explosion.
But at that same moment, the monster’s claw swung forward. With all the strength it had left, it pulled itself forward. And something hot entered Lian’s body.
His eyes shook. For a moment, he did not even feel the pain. Then he looked down.
The monster’s broken horn had gone straight through the middle of his chest. Blood spilled from his mouth.
His body fell to the ground. Breathing suddenly became hard. Very hard.
The monster staggered a few steps. The sound of its bones cracking echoed in the valley.
Its bloody eyes were still locked on Lian. As if even while dying, it wanted to make sure its prey died with it.
Then it finally fell.
BOOM.
Lian lay on the ground. Warm blood spread under his body. His breaths were short and broken.
His eyes slowly became blurry.
".So this is how I die..." He gave a weak laugh.
Honestly? It was a ridiculous end.
His whole life, he had been rejected by the world. And now he was going to die like a nameless sacrifice inside a forgotten realm.
Worse than that, his death would not matter to anyone. Well, except maybe his best friend.
"But maybe this is not bad either..." he whispered with a weak voice.
Before dying, at least he had killed a monster. Yes, with trickery and a plan. And more importantly, the monster itself was almost dead. But still, he had managed to kill a monster.
This could count as a somewhat good ending.
But suddenly a strange pulse twisted inside his chest.
THUMP.
THUMP.
THUMP.
Lian’s eyes shook. An unnatural heat was entering his body from the blood around him.
No... it was being pulled. All the monster’s blood. All the essence scattered in the air. Everything was being pulled toward his body.
And then glowing screens appeared.
[Ruined Heart Activated]
[Beginning Third Awakening Attempt]
Lian’s body shook.
A wild pain passed through the depths of his existence.
[Awakening Failed]
[Subject Not Registered Within The System]
Blood spilled from his mouth.
But the messages did not stop.
[Fourth Attempt Initiated]
His heartbeat became stronger. A sound like chains breaking echoed inside his body.
He felt like his bones were being crushed. Like his soul was being torn apart.
This pain was thousands of times worse than his chest being pierced. Hundreds of thousands of times worse than any pain he had ever experienced.
It was as if his body, or whatever was deep inside him, was forcing him to become an Awakened.
[Ruined Heart Activated]
The entire valley shook for a moment.
And then
[Awakening Successful]

No power.
If he took even one direct hit, he would die.
The monster’s angry growl sounded again.
And then...
Silence.
Lian frowned.
Why wasn’t it attacking?
A drop of blood ran down from his forehead.
His eyes slowly scanned the area.
And at that moment, he realized the monster was searching by smell.
Its bloody eyes moved unsteadily.
Its pupils had no focus.
"Its eyesight is weak..." It had probably lost too much blood.
That had affected its full ability and its senses.
"If that’s the case... maybe I can test him." Remembering a spot in this valley, an idea came to his mind.
But he was not sure if it would work or not.
Lian slowly moved back.
Then suddenly he threw a large piece of bone to the other side.
TAK!
The monster immediately turned and attacked toward the sound.
The ground shook.
Lian used the chance and ran.
His eyes wildly scanned the area.
He was clearly looking for a place.
A place where he could find a way to kill that thing... that monster.
And then he saw it.
Part of the valley wall was cracked.
A huge bone was stuck between the rocks.
The entire upper part looked unstable.
Lian’s eyes narrowed.
"There it is."
The monster’s roar echoed behind him.
The creature had realized it had been tricked.
Lian ran straight toward the wall.
The sound of the monster’s claws got closer and closer.
Their distance was less than ten meters.
Five meters.
Three meters.
He could feel the creature’s hot breath on the back of his neck.
Just before reaching it, Lian threw himself to the ground.
And the monster jumped.
BOOOM!
Its whole huge body hit the cracked wall.
For one second, nothing happened.
Then the sound of breaking came.
CRAAACK—
The monster’s bloody eyes widened a little.
And then the whole wall collapsed.
Huge stones fell down.
The giant bone was freed and fell from above like a white spear.
The monster let out an angry roar and tried to move back.
But it was too late.
The bone went straight through its side.
Black blood sprayed out like an explosion.
But at that same moment, the monster’s claw swung forward.
With all the strength it had left, it pulled itself forward.
And something hot entered Lian’s body.
His eyes shook.
For a moment, he did not even feel the pain.
Then he looked down.
The monster’s broken horn had gone straight through the middle of his chest.
Blood spilled from his mouth.
His body fell to the ground.
Breathing suddenly became hard.
Very hard.
The monster staggered a few steps.
The sound of its bones cracking echoed in the valley.
Its bloody eyes were still locked on Lian.
As if even while dying, it wanted to make sure its prey died with it.
Then it finally fell.
BOOM.
Lian lay on the ground.
Warm blood spread under his body.
His breaths were short and broken.
His eyes slowly became blurry.
".So this is how I die..." He gave a weak laugh.
Honestly?
It was a ridiculous end.
His whole life, he had been rejected by the world.
And now he was going to die like a nameless sacrifice inside a forgotten realm.
Worse than that, his death would not matter to anyone.
Well, except maybe his best friend.
"But maybe this is not bad either..." he whispered with a weak voice.
Before dying, at least he had killed a monster.
Yes, with trickery and a plan.
And more importantly, the monster itself was almost dead.
But still, he had managed to kill a monster.
This could count as a somewhat good ending.
But suddenly a strange pulse twisted inside his chest.
THUMP.
THUMP.
THUMP.
Lian’s eyes shook.
An unnatural heat was entering his body from the blood around him.
No... it was being pulled.
All the monster’s blood.
All the essence scattered in the air.
Everything was being pulled toward his body.
And then glowing screens appeared.
[Ruined Heart Activated]
[Beginning Third Awakening Attempt]
Lian’s body shook.
A wild pain passed through the depths of his existence.
[Awakening Failed]
[Subject Not Registered Within The System]
Blood spilled from his mouth.
But the messages did not stop.
[Fourth Attempt Initiated]
His heartbeat became stronger.
A sound like chains breaking echoed inside his body.
He felt like his bones were being crushed.
Like his soul was being torn apart.
This pain was thousands of times worse than his chest being pierced.
Hundreds of thousands of times worse than any pain he had ever experienced.
It was as if his body, or whatever was deep inside him, was forcing him to become an Awakened.
[Ruined Heart Activated]
The entire valley shook for a moment.
And then
[Awakening Successful]

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Class: Monster
paragraphs: All Lian could feel was blood.
Its metallic and hot taste filled his throat, and every breath hurt like a rusty blade being pushed into his lungs.
His eyes were half open, watching the red sky above the valley.
His body no longer moved.
The monster’s broken horn was still stuck through the middle of his chest, and blood was slowly leaking from around the wound.
A bit farther away, the huge fallen body of the wolf lay motionless. A creature that even in death looked terrifying.
Lian gave a weak, dry laugh.
"...This is ridiculous."
He had actually survived. He had managed to kill that monster. And now he was dying.
THUMP.
THUMP.
Suddenly a heavy pulse twisted inside his body. Lian’s eyes shook. An unnatural heat came out from inside the monster’s corpse.
No... it was being pulled. Strings of red light like living veins came out of the wolf’s body and entered Lian’s chest.
At that moment, glowing screens appeared in front of his eyes.
[You Have Killed A Level 10 Fallen Wolf]
[Level Increased]
[Level Increased]
[Level Increased]
[Level Increased]
Lian’s eyes widened a little.
"Four levels...?"
But the notifications did not stop.
[You Are The First Individual To Slay A Fallen Wolf Within The Newly Opened Ruined Realm]
[Title Acquired: Wolf Slayer]
Suddenly a wave of heat spread through his whole body. The broken horn that had pierced his chest slowly turned to ash and disappeared, as if it had never been there.
Lian held his breath. The wound was not closing, but it was healing.
He forced his hand onto the ground and sat up. His body still hurt, but that feeling of certain death was no longer there.
He breathed slowly and tried to calm himself, having practically returned from a state of death to life.
His eyes stayed fixed on the floating panel in disbelief.
"...I really awakened?" His voice was quiet and rough.
This should not be possible. Every human only had one chance at awakening. At best, people were allowed a second attempt.
But even that second attempt was risky. A normal person’s body should not be exposed to the huge amount of mana needed for the awakening process. If it was, it could explode.
But a third attempt?
A fourth?
Lian had never even heard of such a thing. No body in the world was strong enough to endure and make that possible.
So how had it become possible for him?
He frowned.
If this news spread, there would be a huge uproar. Guilds, governments, research centers, all of them would go crazy chasing after him.
And honestly, that was the last thing he wanted. He did not have the energy for that kind of trouble.
Lian slowly let out his breath and looked toward the fallen wolf’s corpse.
Now that he was calmer, he could feel the presence of that monster better. The pressure of its existence was heavy even after death.
"Level ten Fallen Wolf..."
Monsters were not only classified by level. Their bloodline, overall ability, and talents also differed.
There were five main ranks: Normal, Fallen, Unholy, Demon, and Supreme.
A Fallen monster at the same level was far stronger than a Normal type. It could perhaps defeat dozens of Normal monsters at the same level.
And now that Lian thought about it, that creature had almost destroyed him even while dying. In fact, it had succeeded. If he had not suddenly become an Awakened, he would be dead right now.
His gaze fixed on the huge wounds on the wolf’s body. Cut marks that had even split its bones.
A deeper frown appeared on his face.
"What could have wounded it this badly...?"
He was not really the reason that monster was killed. He had only landed the last hit. If that wolf had been healthy, Lian would not have even had a chance to run.
So what could almost kill a Fallen wolf? A much more powerful monster? But the sword wound marks said something else.
But something else bothered him more.
"...Why only four levels?"
As far as he knew, killing a level ten Fallen monster should raise a newly awakened person to at least level eight or nine.
Unless...his eyes narrowed a little.
"I need more Exp for each level?"
And if that was true, it only meant one thing. His class was of a high rank.
Lian quickly opened his status panel. A moment later, his pupils shook.
[Name: Lian Vorhelm]
[Level: 4]
[Race: Human]
[Bloodline: Human]
[Class: Monster]
[Talent: Dormant Monster]
[Innate Skills: Bloodlust, Butcher, Glutton]
[Skill: Wolf Speed]
[Stats: click to see]
[Fragments: 5/100]
[Titles: Wolf Slayer]
Lian stared for a few seconds. Then he read the line about his class again.
Class: Monster
"...What?" His voice came out clearer than before.
A monster class? Since when did such a class exist? In all of recorded human history, there were only six main classes.
Warrior, Assassin, Mage, Archer, Priest, and Summoner.
Every Awakened fell under one of these six classes. There were no exceptions.
But the truth was right in front of his eyes. He had a class outside the known system.
And even stranger, there were no stars next to it. Class rank was determined by the number of stars.
A one-star class was the weakest possible and could only evolve once.
While five-star classes could evolve every twenty levels and evolve a total of five times.
The difference between them was terrifying.
One-star classes only absorbed ten percent of a monster’s Exp and had very low mana compatibility, around ten percent.
But five-star classes? After killing a monster, they absorbed fifty percent Exp and had fifty percent mana compatibility, plus monster-like stat growth.
They were the true geniuses of the world.
But his class had no rank. What did this mean? Could his class not evolve even once? Or did it have no limits on evolution?
Unfortunately, he did not have enough information. To be more precise, he had no information to base any reasoning on.
Maybe by looking at his innate skills he could understand better.
Lian slowly tapped on his first innate skill.
[Bloodlust: While even the greatest geniuses can only absorb up to 50% of a monster’s EXP after killing it, you absorb 100%.]
His eyes widened a little.
One hundred percent? He absorbed all of a monster’s Exp? Even five-star classes only got half of it.
He immediately tapped on the second skill.
[Butcher: While all Awakened gain Stat Points only after leveling up, you permanently obtain 1% of a monster’s Stats after every kill.]
This time even his breath stopped for a moment. One percent of every stat from each monster? This was insane.
One percent might seem small, but normally the only way to increase power was leveling up and receiving stat points.
And the amount depended completely on class quality. Between levels 1 and 10, one-star classes got only 1 stat point per level up.
Five-star classes got 5 stat points. After that, between levels 10 and 20, one-star classes got 10 stat points per level up, and five-star classes got 50 stat points.
And after level 20, when Awakened could go through their first evolution, the stat points they got per level varied based on their class evolution.
But him? He could directly steal stats from monsters. Even if his level stayed low, eventually his stats would become monstrous.
Like being level 5 but having the stats of a level 20 Awakened.
"...This is a monsterous class." Lian whispered quietly to himself.
Just like the monsters themselves.
And then his gaze fixed on the last skill.
[Glutton: Whenever you kill a monster possessing a Skill or Talent, you have a chance to randomly devour one of them.]
He was quiet for a few seconds, then slowly scrolled the panel down. In the Skill section, something new was seen.
[Wolf Speed]
So he really had devoured one of that wolf’s skills. His heart beat slowly but heavily.
The powers of this class were not normal. This looked more like something a monster should have, not a human.
But just as he was about to open his new skill, his body froze.
He felt something... a heavy and cold presence, far more terrifying than the Fallen wolf, behind him.
Lian slowly turned his head.
And then a quiet voice echoed in the silence of the valley.
"Were you the one who killed my prey?"

chapters.title: Chapter 6: The Golden Mountain
paragraphs: The presence behind him was heavy. Not like the Fallen Wolf, and not like any monster. It was something calmer, but at the same time more dangerous.
Lian turned slowly, and then for a moment his eyebrows pulled together a little.
A girl was standing there.
Her height was almost the same as his, maybe a little shorter. She wore light armor of a dark silver color, parts of it covered in dried blood.
A short, torn cape hung from her shoulder. A long sword was in her right hand. A sword that still had fresh blood dripping from its edge.
But what made the space around her feel colder was her face.
She was too young. She looked the same age as Lian, maybe even one or two years younger. And that made her more terrifying.
Because there was only one truth. This girl, according to her own words, was the one who had brought the Fallen Wolf to the edge of death.
The girl’s cold eyes fell on the huge wolf corpse.
Then her gaze slowly moved over the fallen rocks, the huge bone stuck in the monster’s body, and finally the hole on Lian’s clothes.
A cold, emotionless light shone in her pupils for a moment.
Lian frowned, and his body unconsciously tightened a little. He was sure the girl was extremely powerful. But he was not afraid. If needed, he would fight.
He had not had the chance to check his new stats yet. But according to the Butcher skill’s description, he should have absorbed one percent of that wolf’s power.
And if that monster really was a level ten Fallen Wolf, his current stats should not be weak.
The girl was quiet for a few seconds. Then the cold light in her eyes slowly faded.
"Whatever." Then she turned and started walking away from there, as if she really did not care.
Lian was surprised for a moment. He had not expected such a reaction. This girl was either too confident, or she did not consider him a threat at all.
He did not know if he should be happy or unhappy about this situation. But he also preferred not to get into a fight at this point.
Seeing that the girl was really leaving the valley, he suddenly said,
"Wait."
The girl stopped.
"What is the environment like up there? Mountainous or forest?" Lian asked without moving from his spot.
"A mountain range in the middle of a forest." The girl thought for a moment and finally decided to answer.
’So it counts as mountainous,’ Lian thought to himself, and felt a little relieved. Finding keys in mountainous areas was easier than in forests.
"Up there, on your way, did you see a mountain with a golden peak?"
"Why?"
Lian blinked. Really? He did not expect someone not to know what a golden mountain meant.
Even high school students knew that. Or at least... they should know.
For a moment he wondered if the girl was pretending not to know. The problem was that this was not something that needed to be hidden.
But when his gaze fell on her calm profile, he realized, no, she really did not know. And this was strange.
Very strange.
"For the key." Lian finally said.
The girl turned her head a little.
"Key? A key for what?"
This time Lian was really surprised. From her tone, it was clear she was not lying. Had this girl lived her whole life in a cave?
"The key to exit the realm."
A few seconds of silence passed.
"So we don’t have to kill all the monsters to leave?" The girl’s face was still cold, but surprise could be felt in her tone.
Lian stared at her.
And the girl continued.
"I thought all the monsters in this world had to be killed for the exit to open."
"No, that is really not necessary."
The girl was quiet for a few moments.
"That is easier." Then she said very quietly.
Lian really did not know how to react. Where had this girl come from? She did not even know the most basic information about the realms.
But instead, she could slaughter a Fallen Wolf to the edge of death.
"So you did not see a golden mountain?"
"No." The girl thought a little and answered.
And then after a short pause, she continued.
"But I saw a very tall mountain. Much bigger than the others."

Lian’s eyes lit up a little. That was probably it. According to public information, keys usually appeared in places with the highest energy concentration. And in ruined realms, that place was often the highest point.
"Which direction?"
The girl, without a word, pointed her hand toward the north of the valley. Lian held the direction for a few seconds, then nodded.
"Thanks."
"And I did not want to kill that monster. It attacked me, and I almost died." Then he paused for a moment and said,
The girl finally turned and looked directly at him.
"I noticed." Her gaze fixed on Lian’s torn clothes. More precisely... on the hole in the middle of his chest.
"The middle of your clothes has a hole, but your body does not look like that." Her voice was quiet and completely calm.
"That wolf should have pierced your body.
Lian said nothing.
"That is why I did not kill you." The girl then completed her sentence, and with cold eyes continued,
"Otherwise, because you took my prey, you would have had to die."
A few seconds of silence passed.
And then Lian laughed. It was a short laugh, but not from mockery. It was from the sudden understanding that this girl was not stupid. She just did not know a lot of things.
But instead, her ability to analyze was terrifying. With only a few looks, she had understood almost everything that had happened.
Lian nodded.
"Have a good journey."
Then he went toward the wolf corpse. After all, this was not just a normal monster. It was a Fallen Wolf. Even its skin could be extremely valuable.
Lian sat next to the corpse and started removing the valuable parts of the monster’s body.
Claws, teeth, bones, and finally its thick, bloody skin.
The more he worked, the more he realized the insane value of that monster. If he could take these things to the real world, he would become rich!
After some time, he finally put his hand on the corpse. The space around the corpse pulsed for a moment.
And the huge wolf body disappeared into the Storage Space. One of the basic abilities of all Awakened. A dimensional space given to them by the system.
Lian took a quiet breath and turned. But then he paused. The girl was still standing there. She had not left.
"...Can I help you?" A slight frown appeared on his face.
The girl looked at him in silence.
"Do you have a question?"
Again silence.
"I thought you wanted to go." Lian spoke again.
The girl said nothing for a few seconds. As if she was not sure how to say what she wanted. And this, for the first time, made her look a little like her actual age.
But only for a short moment.
"You are going to go toward that key, right?" She finally said.
"Yes."
"Then I am coming with you." The girl nodded and added. Her tone was more of an order than a request.
As if she was saying, do not even think about refusing.

"So we don’t have to kill all the monsters to leave?" The girl’s face was still cold, but surprise could be felt in her tone.
Lian stared at her.
And the girl continued.
"I thought all the monsters in this world had to be killed for the exit to open."
"No, that is really not necessary."
The girl was quiet for a few moments.
"That is easier." Then she said very quietly.
Lian really did not know how to react.
Where had this girl come from?
She did not even know the most basic information about the realms.
But instead, she could slaughter a Fallen Wolf to the edge of death.
"So you did not see a golden mountain?"
"No." The girl thought a little and answered.
And then after a short pause, she continued.
"But I saw a very tall mountain.
Much bigger than the others."
Lian’s eyes lit up a little.
That was probably it.
According to public information, keys usually appeared in places with the highest energy concentration.
And in ruined realms, that place was often the highest point.
"Which direction?"
The girl, without a word, pointed her hand toward the north of the valley.
Lian held the direction for a few seconds, then nodded.
"Thanks."
"And I did not want to kill that monster.
It attacked me, and I almost died." Then he paused for a moment and said,
The girl finally turned and looked directly at him.
"I noticed." Her gaze fixed on Lian’s torn clothes.
More precisely... on the hole in the middle of his chest.
"The middle of your clothes has a hole, but your body does not look like that." Her voice was quiet and completely calm.
"That wolf should have pierced your body.
Lian said nothing.
"That is why I did not kill you." The girl then completed her sentence, and with cold eyes continued,
"Otherwise, because you took my prey, you would have had to die."
A few seconds of silence passed.
And then Lian laughed.
It was a short laugh, but not from mockery.
It was from the sudden understanding that this girl was not stupid.
She just did not know a lot of things.
But instead, her ability to analyze was terrifying.
With only a few looks, she had understood almost everything that had happened.
Lian nodded.
"Have a good journey."
Then he went toward the wolf corpse.
After all, this was not just a normal monster.
It was a Fallen Wolf.
Even its skin could be extremely valuable.
Lian sat next to the corpse and started removing the valuable parts of the monster’s body.
Claws, teeth, bones, and finally its thick, bloody skin.
The more he worked, the more he realized the insane value of that monster.
If he could take these things to the real world, he would become rich!
After some time, he finally put his hand on the corpse.
The space around the corpse pulsed for a moment.
And the huge wolf body disappeared into the Storage Space.
One of the basic abilities of all Awakened.
A dimensional space given to them by the system.
Lian took a quiet breath and turned.
But then he paused.
The girl was still standing there.
She had not left.
"...Can I help you?" A slight frown appeared on his face.
The girl looked at him in silence.
"Do you have a question?"
Again silence.
"I thought you wanted to go." Lian spoke again.
The girl said nothing for a few seconds.
As if she was not sure how to say what she wanted.
And this, for the first time, made her look a little like her actual age.
But only for a short moment.
"You are going to go toward that key, right?" She finally said.
"Yes."
"Then I am coming with you." The girl nodded and added.
Her tone was more of an order than a request.
As if she was saying, do not even think about refusing.

chapters.title: Chapter 7: Out of the Valley
paragraphs: A cold wind passed through the black trees of the forest.
Lian quietly jumped down from a large tree root and looked around. They had been out of the valley for about an hour now.
Or at least what could be called "out."
The valley was still visible behind them. A huge crack in the middle of dark mountains, like the mouth of a giant monster that had opened inside the ruined realm.
And now they had entered the forest. A forest that was unnaturally quiet.
The trees were huge. Black twisted trunks, some of them as tall as small towers. Their leaves were a color between gray and dark red, and a faint mist moved between them.
There was no sound of birds. No insects. No sign of normal life. Which was, fortunately, a good thing.
He was still not sure if they were in a safe place or not. They could be in an area with no monsters. No dangerous monsters. Or actually, an area with very dangerous monsters.
But with the information he had as an Analyzer student, he could argue that their environment was not that dangerous.
That Fallen Wolf was level 10. All the monster corpses in the valley had been hunted by that wolf. Except, of course, for those extremely huge bones.

And since there was no other wolf in that area, it meant the wolf lived alone and was not part of any pack. On the other hand, he doubted a level 10 Fallen Wolf would dare to hunt in these forests without worry if it knew there was a monster stronger than itself.
This meant he did not need to worry about monsters stronger than that Fallen Wolf. Even though he trusted this reasoning, it might not apply to this entire strange mountain range covered by a forest.
"This world really feels dead..." Lian let out his breath slowly.
"It is." The girl next to him answered without looking.

Lian glanced at her. Since they had left the valley, the girl had walked almost the entire way in silence. Her long sword was still in her hand, and even though her body was covered in blood, her steps were calm and completely balanced.
As if she did not get tired. Or maybe the concept of tiredness did not matter to her.
He had been uncertain about accepting this girl’s offer at first, but he had decided it could be a good idea. Especially since she seemed to be a powerful Awakened.
A few seconds of silence passed between them.
"Do you have a name?" Lian finally said.
"Seris."
A short and cold name. It suited her strangely.
"Lian." He introduced himself as well. But only his first name. Because his family name might be recognized.
Seris just said a quiet "Hmm" and fell silent again.
Lian sighed. This was probably the strangest companionship he could imagine.
But at least he was sure the girl did not intend to kill him.
While moving through the trees, he finally had a chance to open his status panel again.
[Strength: 13]
[Soul: 5]
[Speed: 20]
[Mana: 3]
[Resistance: 25]
[Stat Points: 61]
His eyes narrowed a little. He looked carefully at his stats. He had seen charts before that showed the normal range for stats.
And his stats were completely within the normal range. No problems. Except for Mana. His Mana was terrible. The normal range for Mana was 5 to 7.
And then his gaze fell on the Stat Points.
61 points!
The total of all his current stats was 66. And he had gotten 61 stat points. In a way, he could almost double the total of his stats.
If he put all of them into Strength, his physical power would become four or five times stronger. And he could increase his Mana up to 20 times.
"The total stats of that Fallen Wolf must have been significant." But he could not tell exactly how much.

Because aside from receiving one percent of the monster’s total stats as stat points due to the Butcher innate skill, he had also gained four levels. He should have received stat points for those level increases too.
But because his class was an anomaly, he did not know how many stat points he got per level up.
’I need to pay attention to this,’ he thought to himself.
But what should he do with these stat points?
Right now, he did not have enough information. Depending on the situation he found himself in, he might have specific needs for the points. For now, keeping them was more logical.
Then his gaze fell on his new skill.
[Wolf Speed]
He tapped on its description.
[Wolf Speed]
[Rank: Common (+)]
[Temporarily increases movement speed by 30 points. Your instincts sharpen while active.]
The skill was strong. Actually, very strong. If he had had it while running from the Fallen Wolf, he might not have been wounded at all. With such a skill, hunting monsters would be easier.
Especially if he faced monsters that were slow and big. He could use this as an advantage.
Lian closed the panel. But at that moment, he noticed Seris was looking at him.
"What?"
"When you walk, sometimes you frown for no reason. Is there a problem?"
"I was thinking."
"Hmm." And then she looked forward again.
Lian really did not know how to talk to this girl. But did he really have to spend this whole journey in this strange way?
A few minutes later, he broke the silence.
"How did you wound that wolf so badly?"
"I hit it with my sword.
"A few times." Seris continued without changing her expression.
Lian just stared at her for a few seconds. Then he sighed.
"Right. That was the wrong question."
For the first time, he felt that maybe the girl was not purposely being dry and strange. Maybe she really thought this way. Maybe silence really was the best option.
Suddenly Seris stopped. Her movement was so sudden that Lian stopped immediately.
The girl’s eyes narrowed. Her hand gripped the handle of her sword tighter.
Lian frowned.
"What is it?"
"A sound." Seris said quietly.
Lian listened. At first he heard nothing. But a few seconds later...
Tak.
Tak.
Tak.
The ground shook. Very lightly, but it really happened. Lian’s eyes narrowed a little. The sound of a tree breaking came from a distance.
And then a sharp smell of blood and rotten flesh spread in the air. The mist between the trees slowly moved aside, and something came out of the darkness.
A monster.

Its body looked like a bear, but much larger. Almost the size of a huge polar bear. Its fur was a mix of black and dark purple. Two curved horns like a mammoth’s tusks stuck out from the sides of its head.
Its claws...
Lian frowned unconsciously.
Those things looked more like blades than claws. Each one as long as a short sword.
The monster’s red eyes locked onto them. A heavy growl came from its throat.
But before Lian could say anything, a second monster came out from between the trees.
Then a third.
Fourth.
Fifth.
Sixth.
And finally... a seventh!
Seven pairs of bloody eyes opened in the darkness of the forest.
Seris slowly raised her sword. And Lian, while his gaze moved between those huge monsters, had only one thought in his mind.
"You have to be kidding me..."

chapters.title: Chapter 8: The First Battle
paragraphs: Seven pairs of bloody eyes were staring at them in the darkness of the forest, and the air around suddenly felt heavier and harder to breathe.
The sound of those creatures breathing echoed among the trees, and their eyes showed their desire to slaughter both of them and eat them.
But unlike what might be expected, Lian did not feel fear. Not because he was stronger than them.
But because after facing that Fallen Wolf, these monsters no longer had that unimaginable terror they would have had before.
His gaze fixed on one of the bears.
[Corrupted Mammoth Bear]
[Level 7]
[Rank: Normal]
Lian slowly let out his breath. So his guess was right. That Fallen Wolf really was the top monster of this area.
Otherwise, having seven level seven monsters near its territory would not make sense. If that wolf were alive, these bears would not even dare to come close to its territory.
These monsters had probably realized something had happened to that wolf and came to check, and ran into the two of them on the way.
Compared to that Fallen Wolf, these seven monsters were like insects. They would need at least twenty or thirty more to match that wolf.
At that moment, a movement next to him caught his attention. Lian turned his head, and for the first time since he had met Seris, he felt that something in her face had changed.
The girl’s eyes were shining. But surprisingly, not from anger and not from fear. From excitement. Pure excitement, like a child who had found a new toy.
Or a hunter who had finally found valuable prey.
Seris did not even look at Lian. She raised her sword, and then like an arrow released from a bow, she charged toward the bears.
BOOM!
The ground under her foot cracked. One of the bears did not even have time to react.
The silver sword shone like lightning in the air, and a line of blood sprayed through the forest.
Lian blinked.
"This girl is really crazy..." But he immediately smiled.
Actually, this was better for him. As long as Seris kept the monsters busy, he could also handle one or two of them and increase his power even more than before.
After all, he needed experience, and more importantly, Stat Points.
But this also made him think again about how powerful this girl really was. Maybe he could figure it out in this fight.
Two giant bears roared and turned toward him. The ground shook under their massive claws.
Lian quickly opened his status panel. With his current power, he had no chance against these monsters. So it was time to increase his stats a little.
[Strength: 13]
[Spirit: 5]
[Speed: 20]
[Mana: 3]
[Resistance: 25]
[Stat Points: 61]
He did not hesitate even for a moment. He put thirty points directly into Strength. Right now he was facing monsters whose advantage was raw power.
And since he had no offensive skills and no weapon, the best option was physical strength.
[Strength: 13 --> 43]
At that moment, a wave of heat exploded inside his body. The muscles in his arms tightened. The veins in his neck swelled. His bones made sounds.
Raw power flowed through his whole body. For the first time since entering this realm, he felt strong.
The first bear suddenly let out a loud roar, and then slammed its massive claw down at him.
BOOM!
The ground exploded. A cloud of dirt and rock was thrown into the air. Lian barely pulled himself aside.
But the shockwave still pushed him back several meters. His eyes widened a little.
"Damn it..." His power had increased, but these monsters were no joke either.
The second bear attacked from the right. Its huge horns charged straight toward Lian’s chest. Lian raised his fist.
BOOM!
The impact made his arm go numb. He stepped back, and the bear only stepped back one step as well.
Lian frowned. Even with forty-three Strength, his power was only barely equal to one of these monsters.
If two attacked at the same time, things would get bad. So it was time.
[Wolf Speed Activated]
[Duration: 10 Minutes]
The world suddenly changed. He could hear the heartbeat of the bears. Their movements seemed slower. He could feel the wind on his skin.
And more importantly, his body felt lighter. Much lighter. So light that it felt like he could not feel his weight at all.
A smile appeared on his face. He put five points into Strength.
[Strength: 43 --> 48]
The first bear attacked again. But this time, Lian could see its movement. Before the claw came down, he moved past the monster and slammed his fist into the bear’s side.
BOOM!
The sound of breaking bones echoed in the forest. The bear let out a painful roar, but it was not dead yet.
The second bear attacked from behind. Lian jumped onto a tree trunk and pulled himself aside at the last moment.
The monster’s huge horns got stuck inside the tree. That created an opportunity for him. Lian immediately used it.
He landed on the monster’s head and slammed both his fists with all his strength onto its skull.
CRAAACK!
The skull cracked. Purple blood sprayed around. The monster staggered a few steps and then fell.
[You Have Killed A Corrupted Mammoth Bear]
Lian did not have a chance to breathe. The first bear attacked again. But now it was alone. And more importantly, it was wounded.
Lian’s smile deepened. Killing this one would not be that hard. A few minutes later, the last roar echoed in the forest.
And the bear’s huge body fell to the ground. Blood dripped from Lian’s fists. His breaths were heavy, but he was still standing.
[You Have Killed A Corrupted Mammoth Bear]
[Level Increased]
[Congratulations! You have reached level 5!]
[Butcher Activated]
[3 stat points gained]
[3 stat points gained]
[Glutton Activated]
[Skill Successfully Devoured]
[Skill Acquired: Iron Hide]
Lian’s eyes shone. He had leveled up, and he had gained 6 more stat points. And more importantly, a new skill from his first real fight.
He looked at his stat points.
[Stat Points: 42]
"I used 35 points, so my points should have gone down to 26. Then I gained 6 points from killing two monsters, so I should have 32 stat points. But I have 42?"
"Right... and I also leveled up once. So each level up gives me 10 stat points?" He now understood how many points he got per level up.
A slight smile appeared on his face. He got twice as many stat points per level as five-star classes!
He could not imagine how people would react if this news spread in the world... It would probably be crazy, right?
But he knew this could also be dangerous for his life.
Then he pushed his thoughts aside. He wanted to take a look at his new skill. But before he could read its description...
BOOM!
A massive explosion echoed from deeper in the forest. Lian raised his head.
And then he was completely quiet for a few moments. Not too far away... the body of one of the giant bears was cut in half.
Blood was raining down on the trees. And standing in that blood was a girl with a silver sword.
Calm, emotionless, and completely unharmed. Around her, four monster corpses lay on the ground.
"What level is this girl exactly?"
