But before he could read its description...
BOOM!
A massive explosion echoed from deeper in the forest.
Lian raised his head.
And then he was completely quiet for a few moments.
Not too far away... the body of one of the giant bears was cut in half.
Blood was raining down on the trees.
And standing in that blood was a girl with a silver sword.
Calm, emotionless, and completely unharmed.
Around her, four monster corpses lay on the ground.
"What level is this girl exactly?"

chapters.title: Chapter 9: We Have a Problem
paragraphs: When the last bear fell and the forest went silent again, Lian expected to finally have a chance to breathe.
This was the first real fight he had ever had with monsters in his life. Of course, the Fallen Wolf existed, but that could not really be called a fight.
Defeating it was a combination of luck, intelligence, and using the environment correctly. And more importantly, that monster was already near death.
And his fight with these bears was won with his own raw power.
But at that moment, a sound came from a distance. A sound like breaking rocks, and after that, a short scream.
"Kyaaaaa! Help!!!"
It was a human scream.
Lian unconsciously raised his head. Before he could say anything, Seris, who was cleaning blood from her sword, turned her head toward the sound.
She listened for a few seconds.
"Let’s go see." Then she said.

And without waiting for an answer, she started moving. Lian just sighed and followed behind her. He still had a few minutes left on his skill and was able to move quickly toward the source of the sound.
After traveling a few hundred meters, the further they went, the more signs of battle appeared.
Trees were broken. Traces of blood could be seen on the ground. Some of the thick tree trunks looked like they had been crushed in half by something huge.
About ten minutes later, they reached an open space in the middle of the forest.
And at that moment, Lian stopped. In the center of that open space, a giant monster was standing.
A creature that looked like a massive monkey with black skin and bones sticking out of its body. Its height was over four meters.
Its arms were so big that each swing could crush a human. But what caught Lian’s attention was not the monster itself.
It was three people.
Two girls and one boy. All three were lying on the ground. Their condition was terrible.
One of the girls was wounded in her side, and her clothes were completely soaked in blood. The second girl had a broken arm and her face was very pale.
But the worst condition belonged to the boy. Part of his armor was completely crushed, and the deep mark of a claw could be seen on his chest.
He was breathing with difficulty, and yet he was still trying to put himself in front of the two girls.
As if even in that state, he wanted to protect them.
Lian frowned. If they had arrived a few minutes later, all three would have died.
But before he could do anything, Seris moved past him.
"I’ll kill the monster." And she walked straight toward the giant creature.
No plan. No questions. She just went.
The monster roared, and the ground shook. A moment later, the fight began.
But Lian did not even keep his eyes on that scene. He quickly went to the three injured people.
When he got closer, he realized the situation was even worse than he thought.
The boy was almost unconscious, and his breathing had become irregular. One of the girls tried to say something, but her voice sounded more like a whisper.
Lian knelt down.
"Calm down. There is no danger right now."
The girl looked at him with hesitation, but then her gaze went toward Seris. At that moment, a massive explosion echoed through the forest.
BOOM!
Several tree trunks were thrown into the air, and the ground under them shook. The girl’s eyes widened a little.
"That... is she with you?"
Lian looked at the fight. Seris was fighting the four-meter-tall monster and was worryingly winning.
"I think so, I guess."
"You think?"
"I am not very sure either."
For a moment, silence fell between them. A few minutes later, the sound of the fight stopped.
And that meant the fight was over. The monster was dead, naturally.
A little later, Seris disappeared, apparently to look around, and Lian busied himself helping the injured.
Actually, he had gotten the water from her before, after they left the valley. That girl was completely prepared to be summoned into a ruined realm and had many things in her storage space.
After giving them some water and letting them catch their breath, they were finally able to talk.
"I am Aria." The girl with the least injuries said quietly.
She pointed to the girl next to her.
"That is Alisa."
Then she looked at the boy.
"And he is Ryan."
Ryan moved his head with difficulty. It was clear that speaking was painful for him.
Lian introduced himself.
"Are you also among the summoned ones? What happened that you got trapped here?" He then asked.
"Yes... When we woke up... we were right here." Aria was quiet for a few seconds and then answered.
"Right here?"
"Not exactly here. A few hundred meters away. We thought maybe if we got out of this area, we would reach a safe place." The girl nodded.
"But we were wrong." Ryan, the wounded boy, suddenly added with difficulty.
"That monster found us." He then added.
Lian said nothing. It made sense. They had just entered the realm. They had no information. Their chance of survival was almost zero.
He had not had a chance to look at that monster’s stats, but it was probably a level 8 or 9 monster. And looking at these three, he could tell the two girls were not even Awakened.
That meant only the boy was Awakened. And looking at his young face, he was not much older than Lian. So it was normal that he could not match this monster.
If Seris had not decided to follow that sound today, all three would probably have been dead within a few more minutes.
At that moment, the sound of footsteps was heard from behind them. Everyone turned their heads.
Seris had returned. Her sword was still stained with the monster’s blood. But something in her behavior made Lian frown immediately.
The girl’s eyes were scanning the area. And for the first time since he had met her, there was no trace of her usual indifference in her gaze.
"Sorry to interrupt your conversation."
"What’s wrong?" Lian felt something bad.
Seris fixed her gaze into the dark depths of the forest and then said quietly.
"I think we have a problem."
"What problem?"
"We are surrounded." Seris answered without taking her eyes off the trees.
A heavy silence fell. And at that moment, from the darkness of the forest, dozens of pairs of red eyes lit up, one after another.

chapters.title: Chapter 10: The Endless Bears
paragraphs: Seris was staring into the darkness between the trees. Her cold eyes were slowly scanning the area.
This was the first time since Lian had met her that the girl actually looked cautious.
And an unpleasant feeling formed inside Lian’s chest. If even Seris was reacting like this, it meant the situation was really bad.
"We are surrounded." Those words were still hanging in the air.
Lian quickly stood up from his spot and looked around. At first he saw nothing. But a few seconds later, a branch broke in the darkness.
Then another one.
And another one.
A heavy roar came from deep in the forest.
Then a second roar and a third. The sound of heavy footsteps began to get closer.
The ground under their feet was shaking. Lian’s face slowly became serious.
"These sounds..." And then he saw them.
In the darkness of the forest, a pair of red eyes. Then a second pair, a third pair, a fourth pair. The eyes appeared one after another.
Until almost the entire forest around them was filled.
Aria’s face went pale. Alisa held her breath without meaning to. Even Ryan’s face turned white from fear.
From between the trees, the first monster came out.
Corrupted Mammoth Bear.
Then the second one.
Third.
Fourth.

And then their number became so many that Lian stopped counting. Dozens of bears had surrounded the entire open space. And each of them was at least level 7. Among them, level 8 and 9 could also be seen.
"Is this number normal?" Seris frowned. And yes, it was a real frown. She asked.
"No, unless there is a very large group of them. And even then, this number is too many. But I can guess why so many of them are coming this way." Lian thought for a moment and then answered.
These bear monsters probably lived somewhere nearby. But until today, because of that Fallen Wolf, they did not dare to come close to this area to hunt.
No matter how many they are, they are still normal rank monsters. The hierarchy among monsters is very important. They would not dare to provoke a Fallen monster.
But now that they had probably realized the thing they were afraid of was dead, they wanted to use the chance and take over this entire area.
The situation was much worse than he had imagined. No matter how powerful the two of them were, facing this many was practically impossible.
Lian looked around. An open space with trees in every direction. No high ground, no rocks, no narrow paths. Practically the worst possible battlefield.
They had no environmental advantage. Besides... his gaze fell on the three wounded people. All three could barely stand. Helping them was impossible. Their presence was an extra burden.
This fight would only be between him and Seris and those monsters.
"This will be a hard fight." Lian looked at Seris.
The girl just nodded. Then she raised her sword. At that moment, all the bears roared.
And the attack began.
BOOM!
The ground shook. Dozens of huge bodies jumped forward at the same time. Like a wave of flesh and bone that wanted to crush everything.
Lian immediately opened his panel. He still had three minutes left of Wolf Speed.
[Stat Points: 42]
Without any hesitation, he made his decision. He put thirty points into Strength, five points into Speed, and the rest into Resistance.
[Strength: 48 --> 78]
[Resistance: 25 --> 32]
At that moment, a wave of heat exploded inside his body. His muscles tightened. His bones made sounds. A wild power flowed through his being.
But it was not over yet. His gaze fell on his new skill.
[Iron Hide]
[Rank: Common (+)]
[When activated, Resistance increases by 100%.]
[Duration: 5 Minutes]
[Cooldown: 30 Minutes]
"Activate." He clicked on the activation option. This skill could help a lot in this situation.
[Iron Hide Activated]
A strange feeling spread through his whole body. It was as if his skin had become thicker. As if an invisible layer of steel had been placed under his flesh.
With this skill, he now had resistance equal to 64 points. Fighting these bears should be easier and with less trouble.
At that moment, the first bear reached him. Its huge claw came down.
BOOM!
The hit struck Lian directly on the shoulder. But unlike expected, he only stepped back a few steps.
It hurt, but no bones broke.
"It works." His eyes shone. His resistance was working better than he thought. If he had not activated this skill and increased his resistance, that attack could have crushed his shoulder.
Then he slammed his fist into the bear’s stomach. The sound of cracking bones echoed. The bear let out a painful roar, but it was still alive.
Another monster attacked from the right. Lian dodged with the help of Wolf Speed. The world around him seemed slower. And that difference was everything.
He was beating the bears one by one with his fists. Blood was pouring from the monsters’ bodies. They were falling to the ground one after another.
Though the bears also managed to hit him and cause significant wounds.
The forest had become a battlefield.
On the other side, Seris looked more like a monster than a human. Every time her sword moved, blood spread in the air.
One bear, two bears, three bears, four bears. The monsters were falling one after another.
But for every monster that died, two more took its place.
Time passed. Blood gathered on the ground. Corpses were scattered everywhere.
System notifications kept appearing in front of Lian’s eyes.
[You Have Killed A Corrupted Mammoth Bear]
[You Have Killed A Corrupted Mammoth Bear]
[You Have Killed A Corrupted Mammoth Bear]
[Your level has increased]
But despite all these notifications, the number of enemies did not go down. Slowly, Lian’s breaths became heavy.
His arms hurt. His fists were bloody. Most of the blood belonged to the monsters, but his own blood could also be seen among it.
Iron Hide had saved his life many times.
But even that had limits. On the other side, even Seris was breathing hard. Her sword was still deadly, but she no longer had her initial speed.
A bear managed to drag its claw across her shoulder, blood flowed on the girl’s light armor.
She was wounded. The girl who had been slaughtering monsters like they were insects was slowly showing weakness.
Finally, more time passed. The number of corpses increased. Until a short silence appeared in the middle of the battle.
Lian looked around, breathing heavily. Corpses were everywhere. Seven bears had been killed by him. Eleven bears had been killed by Seris.
Nineteen monsters were dead. But Lian’s color had drained. Seris could no longer continue.
More than twenty bears still remained. More than twenty! As if there was no end to them. And at that moment, another notification appeared that made the situation even worse.
[Iron Hide Deactivated]
[Cooldown: 30 minutes ]
Lian’s eyes widened. He felt the world suddenly become heavy. The sense of safety he had gotten used to was gone. His chest rose and fell. Breathing had become hard.
Wolf Speed had run out a long time ago. Now with this one gone too, he had lost a significant part of his power.
On the other side, Seris knelt down. She pushed her sword into the ground to keep her balance. This was the first time Lian had seen her in such a state.
Tired, exhausted, and near her limit. Blood was flowing from the corner of the girl’s mouth.
But her eyes were still locked on the enemies. Lian spat a mouthful of blood onto the ground.
"Damn it... where did these come from?" He then mumbled under his breath.
There was no answer.
But as if the bears had heard him, all the remaining monsters raised their heads.
And they roared at the same time. Their roar shook the forest. The ground trembled.
Aria and Alisa’s faces went pale. Ryan looked at the wave of monsters with despair. Until now, it had been unbelievable to them that these two had managed to fight this many monsters.
But now they had also fallen.
And then all the remaining monsters attacked at the same time. Dozens of huge bodies charged toward the group through the blood and corpses.
Death was approaching like a powerful wave.
Lian raised his bloody fists. Seris raised her sword one last time. And the wave of mammoth bears rushed toward them with crazy speed.

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Too Good to Be True
paragraphs: While the monsters were charging toward them, Lian quickly looked at his stat points. He still had this winning card and could continue fighting by increasing his stats again.
[Stat Points: 41]
He had leveled up twice and reached level 7. He had gotten 20 points from that.

From the seven monsters he had killed, two were level 8 and each gave him 3 stat points. The other five monsters were level 7 and each gave him also 3 stat points and that brought his total to 41 stat points.
Using these, he should be able to increase his resistance and speed by a significant amount. He did not think he needed to increase his strength because it was already very high.
In addition, he did not obtain a new skill after killing one of those Level 8 monsters.
Overall, he realized that killing the Level 7 or 8 Mammoth Bears did not grant him any skills. Obviously, this was because they were ordinary low-level monsters.
Such monsters usually have only one or two skills at most, and those skills are generally just racial traits shared by all members of the species.

He had already obtained the Iron Hide skill from killing one of them before. That meant they didn’t possess any other worthwhile skills besides that one, and they didn’t display any additional skills during this battle either.
But before he could do that, suddenly a rain of arrows covered the sky.
The sound of shooting echoed in the air. Fast, one after another, non-stop. As if the forest itself had turned into a weapon.
The mammoth bears were still charging, but the first wave collapsed before reaching their target. Their huge bodies fell to the ground one after another, mixing dirt and blood together.
For a moment, Lian just watched. Not the bears, but the direction of the arrows. The accuracy... the coordination... this was not amateur work.
Were there other Awakened here? But what were the chances that several archers had all been summoned to the same spot in the ruined realm?
The chance of something like that was less than one percent!
So what was happening here? Who shot these arrows? A very powerful archer?
Even Seris did not lower her sword. She just watched.

From between the trees, seven or eight people came out. They wore light armor, made of leather and handmade. Their bodies were strong and built for hunting and survival. Like people who had done only one thing for years: stay alive.
"Easy... we are not enemies." One of them stepped forward and raised his hand.
Lian frowned a little, but the frown quickly disappeared. These people did not give him the feeling of Awakened. In fact, they did not give him the feeling that they were from his world at all.
Seris did not react either. She just lowered her sword a little. Not completely.
The man who stepped forward looked at the group. At the wounded ones, at Lian, and especially at Seris. Then at the bear corpses.
"You must be good fighters to have killed this many mammoth bears." The man said with admiration.
"When you are trying to survive, it is natural to fight with everything you have."
A few of the group smiled briefly. But not as a joke. It looked more like agreement.
"We are guards from a nearby village. We heard the sound of fighting. We came to check." Another person stepped forward and said.
This sentence worried Lian more than the previous attack. Village guards in a ruined realm? In a place that should only have monsters?
It was not that there were no natives in the previous ruined realms. But their numbers were very low. And the chance of meeting them by chance was extremely low.
But that did not make him show hostility right away. After all, this was a ruined realm. It could be completely different from the previous ones that humans had cleared.
One of the natives looked at the wounded. Ryan was still half-conscious. Aria and Alisa were breathing with difficulty.
"These three are badly wounded. We need to take them to the village." He then said.
Lian wanted to refuse. His instinct was screaming that this was wrong. He really did not want to go to the village with these natives. Besides, everything looked too good.
"Please... help us..." But before he could speak, Ryan said in a weak voice.
That one sentence was enough to make Lian stay quiet. Seris did not take her eyes off the natives either. But in the end, neither of them agreed.
They just had no choice. The two of them were also wounded and tired. They needed to rest.
Maybe that village was safe. A good place to rest.
The natives picked up the wounded. Light and fast, as if their weight meant nothing to them.
They started moving. They left the open area and went back into the forest. The trees around them became denser.
The path was clear. The two of them followed the natives quietly. Time passed slowly. Without facing any trouble, they got closer to their destination.
On the way, no monsters attacked them. No strange things happened. This made Lian think that maybe he was being too guarded against these people. But he did not like that thought.
With every step forward, the air became heavier. Breathing became harder. And the further they went, the colder the air became.
So cold that even Lian, with his resistance higher than a normal person, felt it clearly.
But before he could think too much about it, his gaze went forward. Between the branches, something was seen.
A mountain range. And in the middle of it, a peak that was higher than all the others. Shining and golden! As if it was producing its own light.
Lian stopped for a moment. Something clicked in his mind. The key!
That mountain itself was the same mountain where the key should be. The same mountain that could be his way out of this ruined realm.
’So this is why breathing gets harder the closer we get. Near the golden mountain, the energy is very dense and intense. Breathing in such a place is hard.’
The natives walked slowly ahead. No fear, no hurry. Besides, breathing did not look hard for them at all. They seemed to breathe without any problem.
Maybe they were just used to it.
After some time, the trees moved back. The ground opened up. Finally, a village appeared. But it was exactly at the base of the golden mountain, a little above ground level.
Houses made of wood and stone. Weak light and smoke rose from a few spots.
Its appearance was simple, exactly like a normal village with no problems.
Lian quietly looked at Seris. Seris looked back at him and neither spoke.
But both of them had, very "coincidentally," reached the place they were looking for.
But was that coincidence really a coincidence?

chapters.title: Chapter 12: The Mountain God?
paragraphs: The village was more normal up close than Lian had expected.
The houses were made of stone and wood. Not so poor that they looked like a camp, and not so advanced that it could be called a real city.
Smoke rose from the chimneys. Yellow lights were on behind the windows. And for the first time since entering this realm, Lian smelled cooked food.
But what caught his attention more than anything was the silence.
The moment the guards entered the village, people came out of their houses one after another. Old men, women, children. Practically everyone stared at them.
No one said anything. No one smiled. No one came forward. They just looked.
Lian felt like he had entered a zoo and he was the animal being shown for the first time.
Even a child holding a wooden doll stood still and stared at him.
"We found outsiders!" Then one of the guards shouted.
As if a spell had been broken, the people suddenly started whispering. Quiet voices rose from all sides.
"Are they really outsiders?"
"They are so young..."
"But where did they come from?..."
"Why are they wounded?..."
Lian frowned. These people seemed like they had not seen any new person for a long time. Or at least very rarely. At that moment, the crowd moved aside.
But this was not that strange. After all, in ruined realms, it is very rare for civilizations or intelligent humans or races to exist.
An old man stepped forward from among the people. He was about sixty years old. White hair and a simple robe. But something in his gaze made it impossible to see him as a normal old man.
His eyes were too sharp. Too alert. As if he did not miss the smallest detail.
The guards immediately lowered their heads. Even the village people fell silent.
The old man smiled.
"Welcome to our village." His voice was calm and warm, but Lian did not feel comfortable for some reason.
"I am Aldric. The elder of the village."
"Do not worry. You can stay as our guests for as long as you want."
"Thank you very much. I am Lian." Lian thanked him but was still cautious.
He had many questions. Too many. What is this village? Who are these people? How have they survived in a ruined realm?
But before he could ask anything, Aldric looked at Aria, Alisa, and Ryan. His face became serious.
"The wounded must be treated first. After that, we will have plenty of time to talk."
Lian was quiet for a few moments. Finally, he nodded. It was logical. For now, nothing was more important than staying alive.
The village’s treatment center was a stone building in the center. Inside, it smelled of medicinal plants. Shelves full of bottles and various medicines could be seen.
Aria and Alisa almost passed out the moment they entered. Ryan was not in better condition. His face was pale, and he was breathing with difficulty.
Several healers immediately took them. In contrast, Lian and Seris were in much better condition.
Their wounds were shallower. Mostly fatigue and bruises. After cleaning the wounds and bandaging a few cuts, their treatment was almost done.
The main healer was a girl around fifteen or sixteen years old. She had light golden hair, green eyes, and a smile that, unlike many of the village people, looked real.
"You were very lucky. How did you survive such a wound? And where is the wound?"
Lian looked at her. She was pointing to the large hole visible on his torn clothes.
"I wonder the same thing. And that wound has healed." Lian gave a small smile.
The girl laughed. Her voice was calm. For the first time since arriving at the village, Lian felt like he was talking to a normal person.
So he decided to gather some information.
"Your village is big."
"It used to be bigger." The girl sighed while organizing the medicines and said.
"Monsters?" Lian noticed. His tone had changed.
"What else could it be besides those damned monsters?" The girl thought for a moment and nodded.
"Move your arm. Let me see if it hurts." And she immediately changed the subject.
Lian’s eyes narrowed a little. He had gotten his answer.
A while later, his gaze went out the window. The golden mountain could still be seen. Even from this distance, it had a strange shine. As if it was really made of gold.
"What is up there?"
"The Mountain God." The girl answered almost without thinking.
"The Mountain God?" Lian raised an eyebrow and asked. This answer was strange and unclear to him. What is the Mountain God?
Could a monster be living up there? If that was the case, it could become a problem.
"Yes, he protects us." The girl gave a sweet and innocent smile and said.
"When the world was destroyed, when the monsters destroyed everything, the Mountain God saved the remaining people. That is why our ancestors settled here."
"To live under his protection." It was clear that this girl truly believed what she said.
Lian stayed quiet. The story sounded like an old legend. But in this world, many legends had truth to them. So he could not completely reject it.
But this itself could become a problem. If something was up there on the path to the key, or worse, protecting the key, it would be a big headache for them.
He had heard that powerful monsters might live in places where keys are located. Because around the keys, energy is at its most dense. For monsters, that is like paradise.
"Has anyone ever seen the Mountain God?" Then an important question came to his mind, and he asked.
For the first time, the girl was quiet. It took a few seconds. Then she smiled. But this time, her smile was a little different. It seemed somewhat fake.
"Of course not. No human is allowed to go to the peak. That is the god’s territory."
"And if someone goes?" Lian asked with curiosity.
The girl looked at the window. At the golden mountain. And immediately, devotion, faith, and belief appeared in her eyes.
"Those who went... never came back." She then said quietly.

chapters.title: Chapter 13: The Healing Room
paragraphs: A few hours had passed since they arrived at the treatment center. For the first time since entering the ruined realm, Lian had been able to close his eyes without worrying about a sudden monster attack.
Of course, he was not really sleeping. His mind was too busy. The golden mountain and that Mountain God that no one had ever seen, which might be a powerful monster.
But the question was, how powerful? More powerful than the level 10 Fallen Wolf? If not, then there was no problem. Because with his and Seris’s power, they would be fine.
But if it was stronger than a level 10 Fallen Wolf, it could become a problem.
Then he got up and sat on the wooden bed. He looked at his wounds. Most of the cuts had closed. Even the bruises on his arms had mostly faded.

It was as if his body was recovering at an unnatural speed. Of course, for an Awakened, this was normal. Physical power includes recovery speed, senses, and even intelligence. And he had increased his physical power by 3 to 4 times.
So it was normal that his body’s healing speed had also increased.
At that moment, a groan came from the other beds. Lian turned his head. One of the twin girls had slowly opened her eyes.
It took a few seconds for her to understand where she was. Then her sister also woke up.
And a few moments later, Ryan also opened his eyes. He took a deep breath, as if he had just come out of a long nightmare.
Seris, who had been sitting on a chair by the window the whole time, just glanced at them.
"You finally woke up."
"I didn’t think I would still be alive." The more talkative girl gave a small smile.
"Me neither." Her sister also nodded.
"I think we all feel the same." Ryan also gave a tired smile.
A few moments of silence passed.
Then Aria’s gaze suddenly became serious. She looked toward Lian and Seris.
"By the way, thank you."
"If you hadn’t come, we would be dead by now. Thank you so much." Alisa also sighed and nodded. She thanked him too.
"I owe you as well." Ryan also raised his gaze.
Seris, without changing her expression, just nodded and fell silent again. Her behavior made everyone feel awkward for a few seconds.
"No problem. We were not far from dying ourselves." Lian smiled and tried to warm up the atmosphere again.
"At least we are alive now. And thank you too, Ryan!" The atmosphere in the room calmed down a little. Aria laughed.
"I didn’t do anything. Actually, I caused more trouble." Ryan smiled.
"I thought you were together from the beginning." Lian suddenly added.
"You mean me and my sister, or Ryan?"
"Ryan."
"No. When we woke up, only me and my sister were together. I don’t know why. Maybe we got lucky." Aria continued.
"Then we started moving and tried to figure out where we were. That’s when we found Ryan. Actually, he found us."
"Before we could figure out exactly where we were, what had happened, and get to know each other better, just a few minutes later, that monster appeared."
Remembering that scene, the faces of both sisters paled a little.
"That thing was nothing like the monsters we had read about in books."
"Ryan could have run away, but he didn’t. He stayed to save us." Aria looked at Ryan with gratitude.
Ryan said nothing. He looked embarrassed or awkward.
"So we have to thank you. If you weren’t there, we would have been killed before those two arrived."
"Well, I’m glad you survived. And it was my duty to do that." Ryan also sighed and nodded.
Lian looked at them carefully. There was no problem in their behavior or speech. Aria was talkative. Alisa seemed quieter and more introverted. Ryan seemed like a shy boy.
He did not get a bad feeling from them. He just did not know why he did not feel good when all three of them were present.
Lian decided not to push for now. Instead, he turned his gaze back to the two sisters.
"How old are you?"
"We just turned sixteen."
"Really? Haven’t you awakened yet? Or did you fail the awakening?"
"Our awakening ceremony was next week." Aria answered without hesitation.
Lian sighed. For these two girls, surviving in this ruined realm was even worse than for him a few hours ago, when he was not yet an Awakened.
At least he had a lot of information about ruined realms. But these two girls did not seem to know much. They did not have much information about ruined realms.

"All our lives, we were waiting for the awakening ceremony. Then exactly one week before it, we ended up here. I think we are the unluckiest people in the world." Aria sighed in frustration and puffed out her cheeks.
"Don’t worry. I am sure there are people more unlucky than you. In fact, right now as we speak, thousands of people who were summoned to this realm have already died." Lian tried to comfort them.
But his comfort was not very successful. It made the atmosphere suffocating and cold again.

For every human killed in the ruined realm, ten level 1 monsters can enter Earth. If an Awakened is killed, depending on their level, even more powerful monsters can enter Earth and cause killing and chaos.
Right now, as they spoke, thousands of portals might have opened all over their world, and monsters might be attacking.
But luckily, the guilds and governments were on alert. They should be able to prevent most of the casualties.
"I didn’t expect to be summoned here either. When I woke up, I was in the middle of the forest." Ryan stepped forward when he saw the atmosphere and tried to calm it again.
"At first I thought I was dreaming. Then I saw one of those bears."
"And you defeated it?" Lian asked with curiosity. The mammoth bears were not strong for him, but they were still notable monsters.
"There was only one. It was hard, but not impossible." Ryan shrugged.
"Then I sensed the presence of those two and went toward them."

And he stopped talking right there. Exactly as Lian expected. He gave no extra explanation. He said no personal information. He made no mention of his past. As if he had drawn an invisible border around himself.
Time passed slowly. The talk moved from monsters to different cities. To the awakening ceremony. To life before the ruined realm. To things they wanted to do if they got back alive.
Aria did most of the talking. In fact, 99 percent of the talking was done by her. Lian, Alisa, Seris, and Ryan spoke very little.
Except for Alisa and Seris, who really did not seem like talkative people. But Ryan seemed like he just preferred not to say anything about himself.
At that moment, a knock on the door was heard. Everyone fell silent.
The door opened. Mira, the same girl who had been taking care of them, entered the room. The young village girl had her usual smile on her face.
But this time, she seemed a little excited. Her gaze moved across the group.
"Luckily, you all look much better. Your wounds are healing well too."
"The village elder sent me."
Lian frowned slightly.
"For what?"
"He wants to see you." She kept her smile. Her gaze moved past Lian.
To Seris. To Ryan. And then to the twin sisters.
"He wants to see all five of you."

I don’t know why.
Maybe we got lucky." Aria continued.
"Then we started moving and tried to figure out where we were.
That’s when we found Ryan.
Actually, he found us."
"Before we could figure out exactly where we were, what had happened, and get to know each other better, just a few minutes later, that monster appeared."
Remembering that scene, the faces of both sisters paled a little.
"That thing was nothing like the monsters we had read about in books."
"Ryan could have run away, but he didn’t.
He stayed to save us." Aria looked at Ryan with gratitude.
Ryan said nothing.
He looked embarrassed or awkward.
"So we have to thank you.
If you weren’t there, we would have been killed before those two arrived."
"Well, I’m glad you survived.
And it was my duty to do that." Ryan also sighed and nodded.
Lian looked at them carefully.
There was no problem in their behavior or speech.
Aria was talkative.
Alisa seemed quieter and more introverted.
Ryan seemed like a shy boy.
He did not get a bad feeling from them.
He just did not know why he did not feel good when all three of them were present.
Lian decided not to push for now.
Instead, he turned his gaze back to the two sisters.
"How old are you?"
"We just turned sixteen."
"Really?
Haven’t you awakened yet?
Or did you fail the awakening?"
"Our awakening ceremony was next week." Aria answered without hesitation.
Lian sighed.
For these two girls, surviving in this ruined realm was even worse than for him a few hours ago, when he was not yet an Awakened.
At least he had a lot of information about ruined realms.
But these two girls did not seem to know much.
They did not have much information about ruined realms.
"All our lives, we were waiting for the awakening ceremony.
Then exactly one week before it, we ended up here.
I think we are the unluckiest people in the world." Aria sighed in frustration and puffed out her cheeks.
"Don’t worry.
I am sure there are people more unlucky than you.
In fact, right now as we speak, thousands of people who were summoned to this realm have already died." Lian tried to comfort them.
But his comfort was not very successful.
It made the atmosphere suffocating and cold again.
For every human killed in the ruined realm, ten level 1 monsters can enter Earth.
If an Awakened is killed, depending on their level, even more powerful monsters can enter Earth and cause killing and chaos.
Right now, as they spoke, thousands of portals might have opened all over their world, and monsters might be attacking.
But luckily, the guilds and governments were on alert.
They should be able to prevent most of the casualties.
"I didn’t expect to be summoned here either.
When I woke up, I was in the middle of the forest." Ryan stepped forward when he saw the atmosphere and tried to calm it again.
"At first I thought I was dreaming.
Then I saw one of those bears."
"And you defeated it?" Lian asked with curiosity.
The mammoth bears were not strong for him, but they were still notable monsters.
"There was only one.
It was hard, but not impossible." Ryan shrugged.
"Then I sensed the presence of those two and went toward them."
And he stopped talking right there.
Exactly as Lian expected.
He gave no extra explanation.
He said no personal information.
He made no mention of his past.
As if he had drawn an invisible border around himself.
Time passed slowly.
The talk moved from monsters to different cities.
To the awakening ceremony.
To life before the ruined realm.
To things they wanted to do if they got back alive.
Aria did most of the talking.
In fact, 99 percent of the talking was done by her.
Lian, Alisa, Seris, and Ryan spoke very little.
Except for Alisa and Seris, who really did not seem like talkative people.
But Ryan seemed like he just preferred not to say anything about himself.
At that moment, a knock on the door was heard.
Everyone fell silent.
The door opened.
Mira, the same girl who had been taking care of them, entered the room.
The young village girl had her usual smile on her face.
But this time, she seemed a little excited.
Her gaze moved across the group.
"Luckily, you all look much better.
Your wounds are healing well too."
"The village elder sent me."
Lian frowned slightly.
"For what?"
"He wants to see you." She kept her smile.
Her gaze moved past Lian.
To Seris.
To Ryan.
And then to the twin sisters.
"He wants to see all five of you."

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Questions and Lies
paragraphs: "The village elder is waiting for you."
Lian got up from the bed. His wounds were almost closed. On the other side of the room, Seris also stood up.

Ryan and the twin sisters had not fully healed yet, but at least they could walk. Their injuries had been extremely severe. Especially since the twins were not even Awakened. Their bodies were completely like normal people.
So they did not have the self-healing power and recovery speed of Awakened.
Mira took them out of the building. The air outside was strangely cold.
Even though no snow could be seen, their breaths came out of their mouths as white steam.
Lian raised his head. The golden peak was still there, right above the village, like a golden sun planted in the heart of the earth.
The more he looked at it, the worse he felt for some reason. As if something from up there was watching them.
An unpleasant feeling went up his spine.
He turned his gaze away.
"I am thinking too much." But even he did not believe that. He looked at Seris, and seeing that the girl was completely calm, he pushed his thoughts aside for now.
The village elder’s house was in the center of the settlement. A two-story building made of dark wood. Not grand, but not poor either. As if it belonged to a modest rich person.
When they entered, the first thing that caught Lian’s attention was the walls. Monster skins, huge horns, and skulls some of which were larger than a human body.
And among all of them, there were several paintings. Paintings of the same golden mountain. As if he had created a small temple in his house with those paintings.
Lian unconsciously paused. All those paintings showed only one thing.
The mountain.
"Come in." The old man’s voice came.
The village elder was sitting behind a wooden table. He had a kind face. His eyes were too calm, like the surface of a lake before a storm.
Mira stood respectfully by the wall.
"I am glad you are feeling better." The old man smiled.
"Thanks to your help." Lian thanked him.
"No. It was the Mountain God’s grace." The old man laughed and then said quietly.
Lian sat down without saying anything. Aldric started asking questions.
About their wounds, about the mammoth bear attack, and about how they had survived.
Everything seemed normal. He did not ask any overly personal questions that would make the atmosphere uncomfortable.
Lian and Aria both answered the elder’s questions as much as they could.
After a few minutes, finally the main question came.
"Which region are you from?"
The room went silent. Lian noticed the twin sisters had become a little hesitant. Seris was looking at them with confusion.
Even he did not know how to answer this question. It was natural. How could they answer? They were not from this world at all.
"We are from distant regions." Before anyone could say anything, Lian smiled. He could not let Aria answer this question.
That girl was too honest. He preferred to be cautious for now.
"We got separated from each other after the monster attacks and wandered for a while."
The old man looked at him for a few seconds. Just a few seconds. But those few seconds were enough for Lian to notice something.
He was not convinced. But he did not say anything to ruin the atmosphere. He just slowly nodded.
"I understand."
The conversation continued.
"Sir, do monsters attack this area too?" Aria asked with a little worry. Being surrounded by that many monsters and attacked had given her a kind of fear and trauma.
Even though this village had its own guards, how could they resist a large number of monsters?
"Haha, young lady, there is no need to worry. This place is under the protection of the Mountain God. With his presence, monsters never dare to attack." Aldric answered with a smile.
"Oh, that is good. So our place is completely safe." Aria’s eyes shone with determination and happiness. She looked at her sister.
Alisa also smiled. It was clear she was relieved too. Ryan did not react much. And Seris... was she upset?
’I think she might have a battle-love syndrome,’ Lian chuckled to himself. Then, seeing an opportunity, he finally brought up what had been on his mind from the beginning.
"Does the Mountain God really exist?"
Suddenly, his question caused a sudden silence in the room. Even Mira raised her head and looked at him with a little worry. Her eyes seemed to be saying, why did you ask that?
Lian could guess why. After all, such a question would be considered blasphemous and insulting.
The old man slowly turned toward the window. Toward the golden peak. He gave it a long, meaningful look. His eyes filled with faith and devotion.
"Of course." His answer was quick and sure.
"Our village has been here for many generations. Our ancestors considered this mountain sacred. The Mountain God protects us.
"That is why monsters rarely come near this area. And whenever they do, they suddenly run away."
Lian listened quietly. But suddenly, something caught his attention. Fear. For a very short moment, fear appeared in the old man’s eyes.
Just a moment. But it was there. As if he himself was afraid of the being he worshipped.
"Then why does no one go to the peak?" Lian asked quietly.
This time, the silence was even heavier. The air in the room felt colder. Mira looked down.
The twin sisters looked at each other. It was clear they were confused about why he was asking these questions. Questions that might upset the people who saved them?
Aria, especially, seemed a little annoyed at Lian for this.
"Because humans should not enter the territory of the gods." The old man smiled, but his smile was dry.
That was it... But it did not answer the question. Not at all. Lian realized that this old man had given exactly the same answer as Mira.
"But why did you suddenly become curious about the Mountain God?"
"Well, in the place where we live—" Lian started to answer, but Aria suddenly interrupted, afraid that his words might upset the village elder more.
"We just wanted to thank the Mountain God whose people saved us."
"In any case, you are still wounded. And the paths outside the village are dangerous. How about you stay here for a few days?"
"When you feel better, you can make whatever decision you want."
The twin sisters agreed almost immediately. Ryan had no objection either. Seris just shrugged. It did not matter to her.
But Lian thought for a moment. Actually, he only pretended to think. Because his answer was already clear. He had no intention of leaving this place.
The key was on that mountain. And this village was the closest point to his destination.
"Agreed."
"Then you are our guests for as long as you want." The old man smiled.
A few minutes later, the meeting ended. After saying goodbye, they left the elder’s house. The sky had become darker. The red light of the sky looked dimmer than before.
As they were leaving, Lian unconsciously looked toward the peak. And at that moment, he stopped.

His eyes narrowed. Something was there. For the first time, he noticed it. On the mountainside, among the rocks, there was a narrow, old stone path. It went straight upward, continuing almost to the peak.
Lian’s heart skipped a beat. How had he not seen it before?
He stared at the path for a few seconds. A cold wind came down from the mountain.
Lian did not take his gaze off the path. Only one question formed in his mind. If no one goes to the peak... then for whom was that path made?

chapters.title: Chapter 15: The Forbidden Houses
paragraphs: The next morning, Lian slowly woke up. For a few moments, he even forgot where he was.
The mattress under him was soft. The smell of fresh bread was in the air. Everything seemed too normal.
Too calm. And that was exactly what bothered him. Nothing in a ruined realm should be this normal.
"I think I am being too paranoid." He sighed and slowly got up.
Until a few days ago, he never thought he would spend a whole day and night in a ruined realm. At least he should be thankful that he had managed to sleep on a bed.
Out of the 25,000 summoned people, God knows how many were still alive and able to sleep. Many of them were probably already dead.
He went to the window. His gaze fell on the golden mountain. That huge mountain was still there.

Right in the center of the horizon. Its golden peak was shining under the light. Luckily, they were not far from the only way out of this hell. As long as they could get that key, all of them could leave this realm.
A moment later, the door opened and Seris entered. Her silver hair was a little messy. Her sword was on her waist as usual.
"The key is there." The girl suddenly said without any introduction.
"I think so too." Lian smiled and nodded.
Seris stood by the window. She had been awake for hours. Actually, she had not slept well at all last night. She had been waiting for Lian to wake up.
"Do we tell the others?"
"Not for now." Lian was quiet for a few seconds, then shook his head.
"Those two sisters cannot help us reach the peak. And about Ryan... I don’t know. At least until we are sure ourselves and really find out if there is something else up there besides the key."
"Whatever you want. It doesn’t matter to me." Seris shrugged.
"I want to try to get more information about this Mountain God and the mountain." Lian added.
"Do you think there is a monster up there?"

"Maybe. I doubt the villagers are lying about this Mountain God. And if even one percent of what they say is true, and the other monsters are afraid of it, then it could be a strong monster. Maybe Fallen, or even higher."
Seris stayed quiet and said nothing. After that, both went to have breakfast.
A few hours later, the village was much more alive. Children were playing on the dirt streets. Women were carrying water. Men were repairing houses, working in shops, or doing other jobs.
If someone did not know where they were, they would never imagine this was in the heart of a ruined realm.
In the house they had been given, the condition of the two sisters and Ryan had improved a lot.
Aria was sitting by the window. Ryan was on a wooden chair across from her.
Every now and then they talked. Sometimes they even laughed.
"If you keep this up, maybe when we get back, we will have to throw a wedding party for you." Lian went near them and said with a smile.
Aria’s face immediately turned red. Ryan smiled. But Alisa did not look very happy. As if she was upset that someone was getting too close to her sister... or she simply did not care.
For the first time since entering this realm, the atmosphere had become a little light.

"Lian, I really didn’t mean to interrupt your conversation last night, but I felt like the village elder was getting upset. So I want to apologize." Aria said after her face returned to normal. She stood up.
"I understand. No need to worry. I am not upset." Lian smiled and made it clear he really did not care.
"Thank God." Aria sighed and sat back down. She had been worried that he might be upset because of her behavior last night.
Time passed slowly. Lian went out with Mira to walk around the village. Last night on the way back from the elder’s house, he had asked this girl to show him the village today if she could.
The village girl had her usual kind smile on her face.
She was carrying several baskets of vegetables. Lian had taken one of them to help.
"Are you sure you don’t need to rest? You were wounded."
"I am fine. Don’t worry. I have experienced worse." Lian answered.
The girl laughed sweetly. Her face might not be as beautiful as those models, but her innocence could melt any ice.
"Have you ever left the village?"
"No." Mira shook her head and answered.
"Never?"
"No."
"Really?"
"Most of the villagers are like this. Our life is here. We have no need to go outside. Besides, out there is dangerous."
"I understand. Out there can be really dangerous. You must really thank the Mountain God for protecting this place."
"We thank the Mountain God from the bottom of our hearts. We are always grateful to him." Mira said with a smile and a thankful tone.
"How do you worship this Mountain God? Does it have a temple? Or special ceremonies?"
"What are those? We just thank him in our hearts." The girl asked with confusion.
Lian was a little surprised. They call that being a god, but they have not built a temple for it. Nor do they have special ceremonies for worship? This was a bit beyond what he expected.
It was not that this made him suspicious or anything. After all, this was a different world. Cultures can be different.
But before he could say anything else, something suddenly caught his attention. They had been walking for a while. They had almost reached the end of the village.
And at the end of the village, far from the other houses, several ruined buildings could be seen.
Decayed houses, broken windows, collapsed roofs. As if no one had lived there for years.
Besides that, the area was blocked off to prevent others from entering.
But something was wrong about that area. The air around it seemed heavier. Colder. Quieter. And for some reason, Lian smelled blood from there!
After increasing his physical power several times, his senses, including his sense of smell, had become much stronger. He was sure he was not wrong.
"What is that place?"
A moment later... for the first time since he had met Mira, the girl’s face lost its color.
Her smile disappeared. Her eyes trembled a little.
"Nothing. Just some old houses. Entering there is forbidden. Only the village elder is allowed to go in." Her answer was too quick.
"By the way, do you want to try some fresh bread later?" Mira immediately changed the subject and also changed their path.
Lian said nothing. But he registered those houses in his mind. He would definitely visit that place later.
Then Mira took him away from there and they returned to the center of the village. The girl then said goodbye, saying she had to go home to do her family’s work.
Lian returned to their accommodation. Seris was sitting on one of the chairs, her hand under her chin. She was completely bored.
"I am going hunting."
"Just like that?" Lian laughed.
"Yes."
"I am bored."
It made sense. In this realm, only power mattered. Every minute wasted could later cost them their lives.
And besides, this girl loved fighting.

"I am coming too." Lian thought for a moment and then said. He also wanted to become stronger. The stronger he was, the more security he would feel and the more confidence he would have to face threats.
Seris nodded. Then she looked at the others to hear their thoughts.
"We can’t come. I still can’t walk properly." Aria said sarcastically.
"I prefer to stay here." Ryan also waved his hand.
A few minutes later, Lian and Seris headed toward the village exit. The streets were quiet. A cold wind blew between the houses.
But the closer they got to the gate... a strange feeling formed in Lian’s chest.
When only a few meters remained to the exit, suddenly two guards stepped forward.
They blocked the way.
"Is there a problem?" Lian stopped and frowned.
He received no answer. At that moment, two more guards appeared from the left. Then three more from the right.
Then several people behind them. Within a few seconds... they were surrounded.
Seris quietly put her hand on the handle of her sword. Her eyes turned cold.
The air suddenly became heavy. Lian looked around. At least thirty people.
Maybe more. All armed. All silent. All staring at them. Then one of them left the area. It was not clear where he went.
A few minutes later, the sound of slow footsteps was heard. The village elder came out from among the crowd.
It was clear that the guard had gone to inform the village elder.
But something was different. His usual smile was gone.
"Mr. Aldric, is there a problem that we cannot go out to train and hunt?"
"Sorry, but outside is dangerous. For your safety, it is better if you stay inside the village."
"Is that a suggestion or a threat?" Lian asked with a calm tone but with an indifferent and cold look.
"It is a recommendation." The village elder answered in his own way.
At that moment, Lian noticed something. Something that made his spine freeze.
A very bad feeling formed in his heart. Maybe... they had been wrong from the beginning.
Maybe... they were not guests of this village. They were its prisoners.
He just hoped his guess was wrong.

She had been worried that he might be upset because of her behavior last night.
Time passed slowly.
Lian went out with Mira to walk around the village.
Last night on the way back from the elder’s house, he had asked this girl to show him the village today if she could.
The village girl had her usual kind smile on her face.
She was carrying several baskets of vegetables.
Lian had taken one of them to help.
"Are you sure you don’t need to rest?
You were wounded."
"I am fine.
Don’t worry.
I have experienced worse." Lian answered.
The girl laughed sweetly.
Her face might not be as beautiful as those models, but her innocence could melt any ice.
"Have you ever left the village?"
"No." Mira shook her head and answered.
"Never?"
"No."
"Really?"
"Most of the villagers are like this.
Our life is here.
We have no need to go outside.
Besides, out there is dangerous."
"I understand.
Out there can be really dangerous.
You must really thank the Mountain God for protecting this place."
"We thank the Mountain God from the bottom of our hearts.
We are always grateful to him." Mira said with a smile and a thankful tone.
"How do you worship this Mountain God?
Does it have a temple?
Or special ceremonies?"
"What are those?
We just thank him in our hearts." The girl asked with confusion.
Lian was a little surprised.
They call that being a god, but they have not built a temple for it.
Nor do they have special ceremonies for worship?
This was a bit beyond what he expected.
It was not that this made him suspicious or anything.
After all, this was a different world.
Cultures can be different.
But before he could say anything else, something suddenly caught his attention.
They had been walking for a while.
They had almost reached the end of the village.
And at the end of the village, far from the other houses, several ruined buildings could be seen.
Decayed houses, broken windows, collapsed roofs.
As if no one had lived there for years.
Besides that, the area was blocked off to prevent others from entering.
But something was wrong about that area.
The air around it seemed heavier.
Colder.
Quieter.
And for some reason, Lian smelled blood from there!
After increasing his physical power several times, his senses, including his sense of smell, had become much stronger.
He was sure he was not wrong.
"What is that place?"
A moment later... for the first time since he had met Mira, the girl’s face lost its color.
Her smile disappeared.
Her eyes trembled a little.
"Nothing.
Just some old houses.
Entering there is forbidden.
Only the village elder is allowed to go in." Her answer was too quick.
"By the way, do you want to try some fresh bread later?" Mira immediately changed the subject and also changed their path.
Lian said nothing.
But he registered those houses in his mind.
He would definitely visit that place later.
Then Mira took him away from there and they returned to the center of the village.
The girl then said goodbye, saying she had to go home to do her family’s work.
Lian returned to their accommodation.
Seris was sitting on one of the chairs, her hand under her chin.
She was completely bored.
"I am going hunting."
"Just like that?" Lian laughed.
"Yes."
"I am bored."
It made sense.
In this realm, only power mattered.
Every minute wasted could later cost them their lives.
And besides, this girl loved fighting.
"I am coming too." Lian thought for a moment and then said.
He also wanted to become stronger.
The stronger he was, the more security he would feel and the more confidence he would have to face threats.
Seris nodded.
Then she looked at the others to hear their thoughts.
"We can’t come.
I still can’t walk properly." Aria said sarcastically.
"I prefer to stay here." Ryan also waved his hand.
A few minutes later, Lian and Seris headed toward the village exit.
The streets were quiet.
A cold wind blew between the houses.
But the closer they got to the gate... a strange feeling formed in Lian’s chest.
When only a few meters remained to the exit, suddenly two guards stepped forward.
They blocked the way.
"Is there a problem?" Lian stopped and frowned.
He received no answer.
At that moment, two more guards appeared from the left.
Then three more from the right.
Then several people behind them.
Within a few seconds... they were surrounded.
Seris quietly put her hand on the handle of her sword.
Her eyes turned cold.
The air suddenly became heavy.
Lian looked around.
At least thirty people.
Maybe more.
All armed.
All silent.
All staring at them.
Then one of them left the area.
It was not clear where he went.
A few minutes later, the sound of slow footsteps was heard.
The village elder came out from among the crowd.
It was clear that the guard had gone to inform the village elder.
But something was different.
His usual smile was gone.
"Mr.
Aldric, is there a problem that we cannot go out to train and hunt?"
"Sorry, but outside is dangerous.
For your safety, it is better if you stay inside the village."
"Is that a suggestion or a threat?" Lian asked with a calm tone but with an indifferent and cold look.
"It is a recommendation." The village elder answered in his own way.
At that moment, Lian noticed something.
Something that made his spine freeze.
A very bad feeling formed in his heart.
Maybe... they had been wrong from the beginning.
Maybe... they were not guests of this village.
They were its prisoners.
He just hoped his guess was wrong.

chapters.title: Chapter 16: A Mage
paragraphs: A cold wind passed through the trees around the village, making a sound like a quiet moan that spread through the mountain space.
Lian and Seris stood in front of the village’s wooden gate, while several village guards blocked the way.
The atmosphere was calm. But this calm felt more like the silence before a storm. Seris’s eyes were completely cold. At any moment, she might attack the ones who had surrounded them.
Aldric, the village elder, came forward with a flat and indifferent face. His old face did not have its usual kindness.
But for some reason... the more Lian looked at him, the more uncomfortable he felt.
"Sorry if we caused a misunderstanding. But these days, the situation around the village is not good at all." The old man put his hands behind his back.
Then he looked toward the distant forests.
"The number of monsters is increasing. Much more than before."
"If you go out and those creatures track you, they might come straight here."
"Then all the village people will be in danger."
A short silence followed. Lian looked into the old man’s eyes. His words were logical. There was no problem with them.

They had indeed killed a large number of monsters on their way. There was a chance that more monsters would be attracted. Especially because that Fallen Wolf was dead and other monsters were no longer afraid of being suppressed by it. More monsters would come to this area.
But still, that unpleasant feeling did not go away. The old man, as the village elder, was just protecting his people. There was nothing wrong with that.
But why did he not feel good about this? Too much paranoia?
"I understand." In the end, he just nodded.

"Thank you for your cooperation. I just want to protect the village people. If you want to leave and not come back, that is fine. But I cannot let you leave and then come back. That is dangerous." Aldric smiled.
Then the old man left with the guards. Lian and Seris stared at his back for a while until he was out of sight.
"He is lying." Seris was the first to speak. Her tone was completely emotionless.
"Do you have proof? I don’t feel good about him either, but his reasoning was not wrong." Lian glanced at her.
"No. I just feel it." Then the silver-haired girl turned and walked toward their accommodation.
Lian followed her. When they returned to the house, Aria almost jumped up from her chair.
"What happened? Weren’t you going hunting?"
Alisa and Ryan also looked at them with curiosity.
Lian explained what had happened. About the guards and being surrounded, about Aldric, and about the restriction on leaving.
After he finished explaining, Ryan was the first to react.
"Well... to be honest, what they said makes sense."
Lian raised an eyebrow.
"You remember how many monsters attacked us?" Ryan continued.
"If there really are more and they follow you, what then? The whole village could be destroyed."
"I think so too. After all, these people helped us. We shouldn’t cause trouble for them." Aria also nodded and agreed.
"That’s right. This place is the safest for now. You shouldn’t ruin our safety here." Alisa also agreed and said in a blunt and honest tone, but it was a bit too blunt.
"Well, what my sister means is, why don’t you just wait a little? After all, we might have to leave sooner or later anyway." Aria then interrupted and tried to correct her sister’s harsh tone.
Lian said nothing. He just glanced at Seris. The girl was sitting by the window. Her face was calm, but her eyes seemed colder than ever.
She did not even take part in the discussion. She just stared outside. It was clear she was angry and did not want to talk to any of them.
"I guess that is the best option." Lian did not say much and did not object. He went back to his room. He needed to organize his thoughts.
The others watched him leave and sighed. Then Aria and Ryan returned to their sweet talking.
A few hours later, the weather became strangely cold. Colder than it should be. Colder than was normal.
Even Lian, who was now an Awakened, felt the bone-chilling cold. The window glass slowly became covered with a thin layer of ice.
The sound of the wind howling could be heard through the wooden cracks of the house.
At that moment, Mira entered the house. She was carrying a large tray. The smell of food filled the room.

"I brought dinner." She smiled. But when her gaze fell on Seris, her smile trembled for a fraction of a second. Very short, very faint. She felt like Seris was so angry that she wanted to tear her apart.
But Lian saw it. Mira quickly turned her gaze away. She placed the food tray in front of them. Like last night, she had brought them meat soup.

"Meat soup is good for your bodies and speeds up recovery. I also put some herbal medicine in it. With this, you should be fully healed within a week." She then said with a big, innocent smile on her face.
"Wow! It smells so good. I always hated soup. How do you make soup like this? You have to teach me!" Aria felt like she was intoxicated by the smell of dinner.
"Well, sure." Mira laughed.
"Don’t you want to have dinner with us?" Lian also sat at the table and looked at her.
"I already ate. And I have to go back to my family. My mother has not been feeling well lately. I need to take care of her." Then she said goodbye and left.
After she left, they ate their dinner quietly. They planned to go to their bedrooms. But after dinner, the weather became even colder.
Their rooms had become so cold that they were not livable or suitable for sleeping.
In the end, they decided to gather around the fireplace. Lian went to the toolbox by the wall.
"Where are the matches?"
But before he could find them, Ryan raised his hand. A small flame appeared on his fingers. Then he threw it toward the wood. The flames immediately blazed up.
A pleasant warmth filled the room.
"I didn’t know you were a Mage." Lian gave him a short look.
"You didn’t ask." Ryan shrugged.
"Fair." He also sat by the fire. But he still looked at this Mage.
Mages are one of the six basic classes and one of the most powerful classes. Of course, their power also depends on their talent and innate skills.
And since this boy could use fire, his talent was probably related to elements, or only the fire element.
’Four-element or more Mages are rare. So he probably only has the fire element ability.’
He became a little curious about how many stars Ryan’s class had. Unfortunately, he had no information about him to base any reasoning or guess on. Asking such a question could also be rude.
’Now that I think about it, I never saw him in battle either. And yesterday on the battlefield, there was no sign of fire being used.’ He frowned a little.
Even though they were in a chaotic situation yesterday, he did not remember seeing any trace of fire being used there.
His gaze fell on Ryan. He saw Aria asking about Ryan’s fire abilities with excited eyes. It seemed that girl was also amazed by seeing those flames.
’Am I thinking too much about him?’
They all sat around the fire. The two sisters sat together. Alisa was holding her sister’s arm. Seris sat a little farther away, as cold and emotionless as ever.
Ryan also sat next to Aria.
For a while, no one spoke. As if no one knew what to talk about.
Until Aria suddenly whispered.
"Do you think we will go back?" Her voice trembled.
"I miss my family..."
The sound of burning wood and the wind outside the window replaced her voice.
Alisa held her sister’s arm tighter. She was scared too, but she tried to look stronger and not be a burden on her sister.
Ryan reached out his hand and gently took Aria’s hand.
"We will go back. We will definitely find a way."
Aria’s face immediately turned red. But she did not pull her hand back. She just lowered her head. A warm and sweet feeling spread through her being. Suddenly, that bone-chilling cold disappeared.
Seeing that scene, Lian sighed.
These two were still children. The two sisters had not even had their awakening ceremony yet. But now they were trapped in the middle of the most dangerous ruined realm.
He was quiet for a while.
"We will get out of here." He then said.
Everyone looked at him.
"Maybe not today. Maybe not tomorrow either. But sooner or later, we will get out of this hell."
His voice was calm but firm. There was a strange confidence in his words.
But the effect of his firm tone was clear. Aria became calmer. Alisa breathed a sigh of relief. Even Seris took her gaze away from the window for a moment.
"That’s right. As long as we are together, we will definitely find a way." Aria also said with shining eyes.
Time passed. The flames became smaller. One by one, everyone fell asleep. The sound of their quiet breathing filled the room.

But Lian could not sleep. No matter how hard he tried, he could not. The feeling of danger and that unpleasant feeling still boiled inside him. He had lost the sense of security he had in this village.
Finally, he got up from his spot and went to the window. He looked outside. The village was covered in darkness.
But suddenly, something came to his mind. Those ruined houses and the forbidden area and that stench of blood came back to him.
As if even from this distance, he could still smell it.
Besides, Mira’s fear... everything fell into place in his mind again.
He made his decision. If there was a secret in this village... that secret was hidden there.
Lian looked behind him. Everyone was asleep. Even Seris, or at least that is how it seemed.
He quietly opened the door without making any sound. The freezing night wind hit his face. Then he stepped into the darkness, heading toward the abandoned houses.
