chapters.title: Chapter 17: The Slaughterhouse
paragraphs: Lian opened the door and went out without making any sound. The sky of the realm was still spread above him. He looked around to make sure no one was nearby.
With his senses, he could hear even the smallest sound within a 20-meter radius. But luckily, there was no sound.
He pulled up the collar of his shirt and moved toward the end of the village. The further he went, the colder the air became. Much colder. Breathing had become harder.
And the smell that he could barely sense at noon was now completely clear.
The smell of blood. Old blood and rotten blood. The ruined houses slowly became visible. Worn-out buildings that looked like they had been abandoned for years.
But it was strange. Very strange. No one was guarding them. No guards were there. No fence could be seen.
As if they had been deliberately left alone.
Lian checked the area for a few moments. No one was there. Then he went toward the nearest building.
Before entering, just to be safe, he looked around again. He was entering a place that was practically forbidden.
"If the villagers find out, it will definitely cause trouble." He thought for a moment and chuckled. He did not know what he would find inside.
He just hoped that whatever it was, it would be worth getting into trouble for. But he was also prepared for the possibility that there was nothing inside.
He pushed the rotten wooden door quietly.
Creek...
The door opened. Absolute darkness faced him. Lian took a step inside. And at that moment... a sound came from behind him.
"Why did you come here?"
Every muscle in his body tightened. His heart almost jumped out of his chest. He immediately turned around. But when he saw the face of the person, he let out his breath.
"Damn it..."
Seris was standing there. She was looking at him with the same emotionless face as always.
"You could have appeared a little quieter." Lian rubbed his face.
"No."
Of course not. Lian did not even know why he asked. He was still surprised that he had not gotten used to this girl’s personality.
"What are you doing here?"
Seris shrugged.
"I followed you."
"Since when?"
"Since you got up from bed."
Lian was quiet for a moment, then sighed. It seemed this girl could still hide from his senses. But since she was stronger than him, that was normal.
"Okay." He looked around.
"Something has been wrong since we entered this village."
"I know." Seris nodded.
"This is the forbidden area. Mira told me I cannot come here."
"So because she told you that you cannot come here, you came here?
"Yes. And I smell blood coming from here."
"Now that we are close... I really do smell blood." For the first time, Seris wrinkled her nose a little and noticed the stench of blood.
Of course, she had sensed it earlier too, but she thought she was wrong. After all, what reason could there be for blood to be coming from here?
Lian moved forward without another word. Inside, the building was completely intact, unlike its outside appearance. A long hallway stretched in front of them.
Stone walls and torches that were burning quietly. And silence. A silence that became more uncomfortable by the moment.
They walked forward for a few minutes, but the hallway did not end. It seemed too long. It looked more like the entrance to an underground temple or monastery, not a village house.
Why should such a place be abandoned? Besides, if it was really abandoned, why were there torches here? This did not make sense.
And then... they found stairs. Stairs that went down into the depths of the earth.
Lian looked at Seris.
"Let’s go." Seris just said.
And both went down. With every step they took, the smell of blood became stronger.
Stronger.
Stronger.
Until breathing became hard just because of that stench.
And then... they reached the bottom of the stairs. Lian took the last step. His gaze went forward.
And at that moment, his body froze. His eyes widened. For a moment, he felt his stomach twist.
He felt like he was going to throw up, but he forced himself to hold it in.
Next to him, Seris suddenly stopped. For the first time since they had met, the girl’s face color changed. Her eyes opened wide with disbelief.
"This..." she said, and for the first time, her voice had a slight tremble.
She turned her head. Seeing that damn scene was very hard even for her!
Not just for her, but for any human. Seeing that scene was scary, terrible, and sickening.
"What the hell is this?!" His voice echoed in the huge underground space.
"What the fuck is this?!"
In front of them was a huge pit. A lake of blood. Really blood. And a lot of blood. At least hundreds of thousands of liters of blood!
The surface of the blood rippled slowly. And above it... hundreds of bodies were hanging.
Humans. Men, women, old people, young people. All hanging from the ceiling.
Their stomachs were cut open. Their chests were opened. Their bodies were dried out. As if all their blood had been drained. Drops of blood slowly dripped from their bodies.
Drip...
A drop fell into the lake of blood.
Drip...
Another drop.
The sound of each drop falling was strangely clear in that hellish silence.
Lian stared at one of the bodies. Suddenly, he noticed something.
There was no heart. The chest was empty. He looked at the next body.
And the next.
And the next.
None of them had hearts. All the hearts had been removed.
"Why don’t they have hearts?" Seris also noticed this.
Lian frowned. He had no answer for this damn question, all their other organs were in place.
Only the hearts were missing!
Then his gaze fixed on one of the faces. He stopped breathing. He recognized that face.
A little farther, another body was hanging. Again familiar. And another, and another. Lian felt the blood in his veins freeze.
They were villagers. The people he had seen every day. And then he saw a face that made his heart sink.
Mira.
The kind girl who had taken care of them. She was hanging there. Dried out and dead!
Her heart had been torn out.
And at the end of the hall, the body of old man Aldric could be seen. The village elder. He was also dead.
"If these are the real ones..." Lian swallowed hard.
"Then who are the people outside?" Seris also continued with disbelief and wide eyes.
Neither had an answer. For the first time since entering this realm, they felt real fear.
Fear of something they did not even understand.
Thousands of different possibilities and arguments came to their minds. But each one seemed more terrifying and horrible than the last. No matter how they thought about it, this was not right.
They were in a killing ground! They were in a slaughterhouse. A place where humans, each with their own lives, memories, friends, and loved ones, had been butchered and hung like sheep.
What could have done such a thing to them?
"We have to go." Lian stepped back. His voice was dry and hard.
"Right now."
"I agree." Seris immediately nodded.
"We have to take the others and get out of this damn village." They did not want to spend even one more second in this cursed, damned village.
Both turned back without delay. They ran up the stairs. They went through the hallway. They headed toward the exit. But just when they opened the door...
Both stopped.
At the entrance of the building, a girl was standing. A familiar face in white clothes.
Mira.
But something about her was wrong. Very wrong. Her eyes were no longer warm. No longer kind. They were cold, soulless, and inhuman. Like the eyes of a monster!
She looked at them quietly. Not angry. Not upset. Just looking at them.
Then her lips moved.
"You should not have come here."

sentences.text: Lian opened the door and went out without making any sound.
The sky of the realm was still spread above him.
He looked around to make sure no one was nearby.
With his senses, he could hear even the smallest sound within a 20-meter radius.
But luckily, there was no sound.
He pulled up the collar of his shirt and moved toward the end of the village.
The further he went, the colder the air became.
Much colder.
Breathing had become harder.
And the smell that he could barely sense at noon was now completely clear.
The smell of blood.
Old blood and rotten blood.
The ruined houses slowly became visible.
Worn-out buildings that looked like they had been abandoned for years.
But it was strange.
Very strange.
No one was guarding them.
No guards were there.
No fence could be seen.
As if they had been deliberately left alone.
Lian checked the area for a few moments.
No one was there.
Then he went toward the nearest building.
Before entering, just to be safe, he looked around again.
He was entering a place that was practically forbidden.
"If the villagers find out, it will definitely cause trouble." He thought for a moment and chuckled.
He did not know what he would find inside.
He just hoped that whatever it was, it would be worth getting into trouble for.
But he was also prepared for the possibility that there was nothing inside.
He pushed the rotten wooden door quietly.
Creek...
The door opened.
Absolute darkness faced him.
Lian took a step inside.
And at that moment... a sound came from behind him.
"Why did you come here?"
Every muscle in his body tightened.
His heart almost jumped out of his chest.
He immediately turned around.
But when he saw the face of the person, he let out his breath.
"Damn it..."
Seris was standing there.
She was looking at him with the same emotionless face as always.
"You could have appeared a little quieter." Lian rubbed his face.
"No."
Of course not.
Lian did not even know why he asked.
He was still surprised that he had not gotten used to this girl’s personality.
"What are you doing here?"
Seris shrugged.
"I followed you."
"Since when?"
"Since you got up from bed."
Lian was quiet for a moment, then sighed.
It seemed this girl could still hide from his senses.
But since she was stronger than him, that was normal.
"Okay." He looked around.
"Something has been wrong since we entered this village."
"I know." Seris nodded.
"This is the forbidden area.
Mira told me I cannot come here."
"So because she told you that you cannot come here, you came here?
"Yes.
And I smell blood coming from here."
"Now that we are close...
I really do smell blood." For the first time, Seris wrinkled her nose a little and noticed the stench of blood.
Of course, she had sensed it earlier too, but she thought she was wrong.
After all, what reason could there be for blood to be coming from here?
Lian moved forward without another word.
Inside, the building was completely intact, unlike its outside appearance.
A long hallway stretched in front of them.
Stone walls and torches that were burning quietly.
And silence.
A silence that became more uncomfortable by the moment.
They walked forward for a few minutes, but the hallway did not end.
It seemed too long.
It looked more like the entrance to an underground temple or monastery, not a village house.
Why should such a place be abandoned?
Besides, if it was really abandoned, why were there torches here?
This did not make sense.
And then... they found stairs.
Stairs that went down into the depths of the earth.
Lian looked at Seris.
"Let’s go." Seris just said.
And both went down.
With every step they took, the smell of blood became stronger.
Stronger.
Stronger.
Until breathing became hard just because of that stench.
And then... they reached the bottom of the stairs.
Lian took the last step.
His gaze went forward.
And at that moment, his body froze.
His eyes widened.
For a moment, he felt his stomach twist.
He felt like he was going to throw up, but he forced himself to hold it in.
Next to him, Seris suddenly stopped.
For the first time since they had met, the girl’s face color changed.
Her eyes opened wide with disbelief.
"This..." she said, and for the first time, her voice had a slight tremble.
She turned her head.
Seeing that damn scene was very hard even for her!
Not just for her, but for any human.
Seeing that scene was scary, terrible, and sickening.
"What the hell is this?!" His voice echoed in the huge underground space.
"What the fuck is this?!"
In front of them was a huge pit.
A lake of blood.
Really blood.
And a lot of blood.
At least hundreds of thousands of liters of blood!
The surface of the blood rippled slowly.
And above it... hundreds of bodies were hanging.
Humans.
Men, women, old people, young people.
All hanging from the ceiling.
Their stomachs were cut open.
Their chests were opened.
Their bodies were dried out.
As if all their blood had been drained.
Drops of blood slowly dripped from their bodies.
Drip...
A drop fell into the lake of blood.
Drip...
Another drop.
The sound of each drop falling was strangely clear in that hellish silence.
Lian stared at one of the bodies.
Suddenly, he noticed something.
There was no heart.
The chest was empty.
He looked at the next body.
And the next.
And the next.
None of them had hearts.
All the hearts had been removed.
"Why don’t they have hearts?" Seris also noticed this.
Lian frowned.
He had no answer for this damn question, all their other organs were in place.
Only the hearts were missing!
Then his gaze fixed on one of the faces.
He stopped breathing.
He recognized that face.
A little farther, another body was hanging.
Again familiar.
And another, and another.
Lian felt the blood in his veins freeze.
They were villagers.
The people he had seen every day.
And then he saw a face that made his heart sink.
Mira.
The kind girl who had taken care of them.
She was hanging there.
Dried out and dead!
Her heart had been torn out.
And at the end of the hall, the body of old man Aldric could be seen.
The village elder.
He was also dead.
"If these are the real ones..." Lian swallowed hard.
"Then who are the people outside?" Seris also continued with disbelief and wide eyes.
Neither had an answer.
For the first time since entering this realm, they felt real fear.
Fear of something they did not even understand.
Thousands of different possibilities and arguments came to their minds.
But each one seemed more terrifying and horrible than the last.

At the entrance of the building, a girl was standing.
A familiar face in white clothes.
Mira.
But something about her was wrong.
Very wrong.
Her eyes were no longer warm.
No longer kind.
They were cold, soulless, and inhuman.
Like the eyes of a monster!
She looked at them quietly.
Not angry.
Not upset.
Just looking at them.
Then her lips moved.
"You should not have come here."

chapters.title: Chapter 18: The Fragments
paragraphs: The cold of the night had become worse than before.
The wind howled through the abandoned buildings, and its sound echoed through the empty streets of the village.
Lian and Seris stood right in front of the exit of the abandoned house. But neither dared to move.
Because what stood in front of them, what they had once looked at with human eyes, but now? They doubted that thing was anywhere close to being human.
Mira stood quietly in front of the door. Her eyes... those eyes no longer belonged to a human. No emotion could be seen in them.
No warmth, no fear, no anger or joy. Only coldness. Absolute coldness shone in her eyes.
Lian stared at her with a frown. His heart was still pounding hard because of that underground slaughterhouse. The images of those hundreds of dried bodies were still in front of his eyes.
Drops of blood slowly falling into that huge lake of blood. And the hearts that had been pulled out of every victim’s body.
"What are you?" He tried to stay calm and asked.
Mira showed no reaction. She just kept that same cold look.
"You should not have come here." Then her lips moved and she answered.
Lian’s frown deepened.
"We should not have come?" His voice became louder.
"Down there is a slaughterhouse!" He pointed to the building behind him.
"Hundreds of humans were butchered like sheep! They were hanging from the ceiling! All their hearts were torn out!"
"And you tell me we should not have come? So you could hide such a horrible secret from us? So you could do the same thing to us?" For the first time, anger could be heard in his voice.
But Mira just looked at him. As if all those events did not matter. As if they had nothing to do with her.
"Talking to her is useless." Seris let out a cold sigh.
She did not like wasting time. Especially since she was worried that the other guards of this village might also notice and come here.
It was better to defeat this one as soon as possible and leave the village.
The sound of metal echoed in the air. Her sword came out of its sheath. Without any further warning, she charged forward.
BOOM!
The ground under her foot cracked. The ten-meter distance between them disappeared in a fraction of a second. The blade of her sword went straight toward Mira’s neck.
But... what happened made even Lian shocked.
Mira’s body suddenly dissolved. No blood sprayed. No flesh was cut. Her body turned into mist. Seris’s sword passed through the mist.
"What?!"
At that same moment, the mist gathered behind Seris. Suddenly, dozens of black branches shot out from inside it.
Branches covered in thorns. Branches that looked like living creatures.
Seris’s face changed. She tried to dodge, but it was too late. The branches hit her body like huge snakes.
CRAAACK!
The sound of breaking bones echoed in the night. Blood sprayed in the air. Seris’s body shot back like a bullet.
She was thrown dozens of meters back and hit the wall of a building with great force.
BOOM!
The wall collapsed.
For a moment, Lian froze. He had seen Seris’s power. A girl who had alone killed dozens of mammoth bears and had even managed to wound a Fallen Wolf to near death.
But now she had not even been able to land a single hit.

"Damn it..." He tried to look at that girl’s information. He had not done this before because he thought Mira was human, and you cannot see other humans’ information. But for monsters, it might be possible.
[Race: Unknown]
[Level: ???]
"How is this possible?" He frowned. How could the system not identify Mira’s race? Did that even make sense?
Was there a race that The Will could not identify? Or was it because this was a new ruined realm and the system had not yet been able to get all the information about it?
But he had never heard of such a thing before.
"She is at least 10 levels above me." He whispered to himself. The fact that the system could not identify the enemy’s level meant the enemy was at least ten levels above him.
"No choice." He entered the fight without hesitation. If Seris alone could not defeat her, then both of them would attack together.
His body moved like a shadow. He charged straight toward Mira. His fist went toward the girl’s face. But just before impact, a branch shot out from the ground.
CRACK!
A terrible pain went through his side. Lian felt something inside his body break.
Then the second hit came.
And the third.
And the fourth.
Each time, before he could even react, his body was thrown like a rag doll among the branches.
Blood spilled from his mouth. The ground under his feet broke. But he could not land a single hit on the enemy.
There was no chance. No hope. No way to win. This was no longer a fight. It was a hunt. And they were the prey.
If they could not even wound this one, then what chance did they have against the whole village?
Lian’s eyes went to Seris. The girl was breathing with difficulty. Blood covered all her clothes. If this continued... she would die.
Lian clenched his teeth.
[Wolf Speed Activated]
"Not enough!" He immediately opened his panel.
[Stat Points: 41]
Without any hesitation, he put 30 points into Speed.
Suddenly, a wave of energy exploded inside his body. He went to Seris, put her on his shoulder, turned, and ran.
That was the only option left. The enemy was so strong that fighting was stupid. Besides, this was only Mira. What if the other villagers suddenly appeared?
If each of them had even half of Mira’s power, they would be killed without any chance.
"Running is foolish." Mira quietly watched them.
Dozens of branches rushed toward them again.
Lian thought he could escape. But before he realized it, those branches had suddenly reached him. They tried to hit him, but he was lucky enough to dodge.
He cursed and put the remaining fifteen points into Speed as well.
[Speed: 66]
The world around him blurred.
BOOM!
The ground under his foot exploded. He shot out of the village like a bullet.
But even this was not enough.
Mira disappeared. She moved through the shadows. Through the trees, on the roofs of houses, through the darkness. She was still chasing them.
Lian forced his breath out. His damn speed had reached 66 points! It was unlikely that even a level 15 Awakened had such speed.
And he should not forget that he was using Wolf Speed, which brought his speed to 100 points! A speed that no Awakened below level 20 had!
Then how was this monster chasing them so easily? At this rate, they would definitely be caught.
"How could I forget them?" Then suddenly he remembered something. Fragments.
He immediately opened his panel.
[Fragments: 6]
Fragments were a kind of mechanism. You could use them to upgrade skills. Fragments could be obtained very randomly after killing monsters.
Of course, it was very random. You might kill dozens of monsters and not get a single fragment. Or you might kill one monster and suddenly get 5 of them.
Exactly like him. After killing the Fallen Wolf, he had gotten 5 fragments. And another one after killing all those mammoth bears.
He clicked on his skill.
[Wolf Speed]
[Rank: Common (+)]
The upgrade option appeared.
[To evolve Wolf Speed, 5 Fragments are needed.]
[Do you confirm?]
"Confirm."
[Confirmed]
[Wolf Speed has been upgraded]
[Fallen Wolf Speed]
[Rank: Great (+)]
[Increases your Speed by 60 points for 15 minutes and greatly enhances all senses]
Suddenly, a wave of energy exploded inside his body. He felt the world become slower. Much slower. He could hear his own heartbeat.
Even the sound of blood moving through his own veins.
And then he ran. This time he really ran. Faster than any speed a human could run. Mira slowly fell behind. The chasing shadows disappeared.
The village was lost in the darkness. The golden mountain faded behind them.
But Lian did not stop.
One hour.
Two hours.
Three hours...
Maybe more. He did not know. His skill had run out a long time ago.
But he just kept running.
Until there was nothing left in his body. Until snow started to fall. Until the cold was breaking his bones.
And finally, he stopped.
He put Seris on the ground. He himself fell onto the snow.
He was breathing heavily. His whole body was burning. But they were alive. Luckily, they were alive.
A few minutes later, Seris slowly opened her eyes.
"What... happened?"
"Where are we?"
Lian took a heavy breath.
"I don’t know."
Then for the first time, he raised his head and looked around. And at that moment, he froze. They were no longer in a normal forest.
Snow was falling everywhere. Terrible snow that looked like it wanted to swallow everything.
And in the distance, behind the blizzard, something could be seen. A city. But not a normal city. Huge ice towers and shining ice walls.
[Hidden area discovered]
[Frostheart, The Fallen City]

chapters.title: Chapter 19: Explorers of the Lost City
paragraphs: A cold wind that passed through the blizzard was dragging across Lian’s skin like an icy blade. His breaths had become heavy, and his lungs were burning.
His legs no longer had any feeling. From the moment they had escaped that damned village, he had just run.
Without stopping. Without even looking behind him once. And finally, his knees bent.
He dropped Seris onto the snow, and he himself fell to the ground with a muffled sound.
The cold snow touched his face.
But for the first time in the last few hours, he felt like he was still alive.
"Damn it..."
His chest rose and fell. His whole body hurt. Even after all the increases he had gotten from the system. Even after all those stats he had absorbed.
The fight with Mira was not a fight at all. It was a massacre. Even if he and Seris had been three times stronger, it would not have made a difference.

That creature, whatever it was, was not a normal monster. Now that his brain was finally not in a stressful, emotional state and he could think calmly, the image of the moment when the system could not identify that monster’s race appeared in his mind.
In a normal situation, such a thing is impossible. Unless The Will had not yet been able to fully identify the new ruined realm and gather all its information.
But is that possible? He doubted it. Actually, there was a more logical possibility. Those monsters were no longer what they used to be. They might have evolved and turned into a new kind of monster.
This could explain the missing hearts in those bodies. And if they had mutated, that would explain everything. Because they were monsters that had never existed before.

And for this reason, the system could not identify them. The more he thought, the more sure he became of his reasoning. But the question was, how had they actually mutated? And what exactly were they now?
Next to him, Seris slowly opened her eyes. She stared at the gray sky for a few seconds.
Then she frowned.
"What happened?" Her voice was weaker than ever.
"Where are we?"
Lian was quiet for a few moments, then shook his head.
"I don’t know."
For the first time, he looked around. The blizzard was still continuing. A white, endless world of snow and ice. Huge rocks and frozen valleys.
And silence.
But suddenly, something in the distance caught his attention. In the middle of the blizzard, behind the white curtains of snow, there was a massive shadow.
Lian blinked. Then he sat up higher, and his eyes widened.
"That..."
Next to him, Seris also noticed. In the distance, there was a city. A massive city, but not made of stone. Made of ice. Towers that stretched to the sky. Walls that shone like crystal.
[Hidden area discovered]
[Frostheart, The Fallen City]
[First discoverer of the area: Lian Vonhelm, Seris Pendragon]
[Reward received]
[10 Fragments]
[20 Stat Points]
[New title received]
[Explorer of the Lost City]
Lian stared at the notifications. His eyes shone with surprise. He had not expected to discover a hidden area!
Hidden areas are very attractive. The people who find them first become rich. Aside from the amazing rewards they get from The Will, these areas are always full of valuable items and objects.
Hidden areas are places that show the remains of civilizations from ruined realms. Civilizations that once had passion and life.
And aside from all the wealth that might exist in that fallen city, he had gotten 20 stat points and ten fragments. Plus a title! With this title, he now had two titles.
But that was not the only thing that caught his attention. It was Seris’s family name. Pendragon! The family name of one of the six founders of the modern era.
Actually, one of the first ten Awakened and a member of the group that had cleared the first ruined realm by themselves and saved the world from that apocalypse.
"So you are a Vonhelm." Seris also stared at him with a cold tone. Her tone was colder than usual.
"And you are a Pendragon." Lian also frowned. The relationship between their families... was not very good.
"But you don’t act like one of them."
"But I guess you really do seem like one."
The atmosphere between the two became a little suffocating. The tension rose higher and higher with each moment. As if they might attack each other at any moment.
But in the end, Seris sighed and leaned against a rock. As if she was too lazy to care about such things.
Her wounds had not fully healed yet, but her condition was much better than before.
"My family’s problems are none of my concern." Then she thought for a moment and said in a more normal tone. Her words made the tension disappear.
"I guess we are both in the same boat." Lian laughed quietly. He also sat down and leaned against a rock. He was considered an exile. He had no interest in caring about his family problems.
"What exactly happened?"

"After you got hurt in the fight with that monster and passed out, I attacked her. But as you can imagine, I could not do much..." Then Lian explained how they had been forced to make a strategic retreat and leave that village.
"I lost?" Seris looked at her fists. Her sword was nowhere to be seen. Unfortunately, in all that chaos, her sword had been left behind.
"Don’t blame yourself. That bastard was way too strong."
"So what about the others?"
"Oh." Lian suddenly realized he had completely forgotten about the twins and Ryan. Of course, in that chaos, there was nothing he could do anyway.
He had barely saved himself and Seris, let alone them.
"They are probably dead by now." Seris said with a cold tone. But not as cold and indifferent as usual. After all, they had spent some time together.
For a while, silence formed between them. Neither could speak. Until she herself broke the silence.
"What should we do now?"
"We need to get stronger and go back to that village. There is no other choice. The key is there. And I doubt finding another one would be that easy." Lian thought for a moment and then answered.
Seris slowly stood up and looked at that city in the distance.
"If we want to get stronger, that place is our only chance." She then said quietly.
Lian also stood up and nodded. A hidden area could be a huge help. If they could also find and hunt monsters nearby, that would be even better.
"But I don’t have a good feeling about that city." Seris suddenly said.
"Since when have you ever had a good feeling about anything?" Lian laughed.
"Never." Seris’s answer was immediate, but her gaze was still fixed on the city.
"A hidden area is definitely dangerous. These areas are unknown. Along with all their opportunities, they can also be deadly. But right now, it is our best option."
Suddenly, the blizzard parted for a moment. For a fraction of a second, Lian saw something on one of the ice towers.
A shape that looked like a human. Standing on the edge of the tower, motionless, just watching. But much larger than a human. And it seemed to have horns?
But in the blink of an eye, the shape disappeared.
"Did you see it?" Seris suddenly asked.
"Yes." He quietly nodded.
Both were silent for a few seconds. So it was not just his imagination. Seris had seen it too. Something was there. Of course, that was not unusual. Such a city would certainly not be empty.
But was that not even better? Instead of fear, both of them felt excitement. Excitement to grow and become stronger.
The wind blew again. A strange howling sound rose from the ice city.
"Shall we go?"
Lian stared at the city for a few moments. At the ice towers. At the blue light. At the deadly feeling that came from there.
Then he gave a bitter smile.
"We always make the worst possible decision, don’t we?"
"We are still alive." Seris shrugged.
"That’s right."
Lian stood up from the snow. The wind blew again. The city of Frostheart was waiting for them in the middle of the blizzard.

chapters.title: Chapter 20: The Frozen City
paragraphs: A cold wind that passed through the frozen streets of Frostheart made a sound like a distant moan.

Lian and Seris slowly walked through the city’s massive gate. Neither of them spoke. Their senses were fully focused on their surroundings to make sure they would not be surrounded again, attacked secretly, or trapped in a snare.
Frostheart was much larger than it had seemed from a distance. Huge ice buildings stood on both sides of the streets.
Blue crystal pillars rose from the ground. Towers that reached hundreds of meters high were lost in the blizzard.
At the same time, a suffocating silence had taken over the entire city. Apart from the sound of the wind, there was no noise. As if the whole city had died centuries ago.
"I don’t like this place." Lian said quietly.
"Me neither." Seris answered without looking around.
She almost never liked anything. But this time, even she was cautious.
Hidden areas can be a big opportunity, but at the same time they can be deadly. God knows what dangers are hidden in there.
If they are not careful, they might die without a grave.
They continued moving. After a few minutes, Lian suddenly stopped. His gaze fixed on the snow.
"Wait."
Seris also looked down.
Footprints.
Huge footprints, as big as a large plate. As if a multi-ton creature had passed through.
But these were not the only footprints. A few meters ahead, another footprint could be seen. This one did not look like a claw. It looked more like the footprint of a giant reptile.
And a little farther... six parallel tracks could be seen on the ground.
As if a six-legged creature had passed through.
Seris frowned.
"These do not belong to one creature."
"Obviously." Lian bent down. The footprints were not completely fresh, but they did not look old either.
And stranger than anything, all of them were moving in one direction. Toward the center of the city. According to his observations, they were not far from the city center.
And these footprints showed that several different types of monsters had passed through here and gone toward the city center. But why would all of them go in that direction?
He examined the area for a few minutes. Then his frown deepened.
"No footprints lead out of the city."
Seris also noticed. All the footprints had entered the city. None had left. As if all the creatures that entered Frostheart...
Disappeared inside it.
A cold wind blew. They continued on their path. Sometimes they entered houses. Sometimes they examined buildings.
And the more they saw, the worse they felt. In one house, the dinner table was still set.
The plates were in their places. Even a frozen piece of bread was on the table. In another house, an open book could be seen on a desk, as if its owner had only left for a few minutes.
But the layers of ice on them showed that centuries had passed since that time.
"It’s as if time stopped." Lian whispered this sentence quietly.
Seris did not answer. She had no explanation for what she was seeing either. There was no sign of human bodies. Either they had been completely destroyed, or they had managed to escape this city.
But even if they had managed to escape the city, how far could they have gone?
They continued moving. After a while, they reached a large square. Lian’s eyes widened a little.
In the center of the square stood massive statues. Armored warriors. Mages with giant staffs. Knights riding unknown creatures.
All made of ice. Lian checked twice to make sure whether these were frozen humans or actual statues.
And the result did not surprise him much.
"They were real humans once, but now they are completely frozen." Lian sighed. These were probably the guardians of this city.
Guardians who wanted to protect this city from something... but this was what happened to all of them.
"But they are all looking at one point." Seris, who had noticed something, added.
The strange thing was that all the statues were looking at one point. Toward the center of the city. Toward a castle.
A massive castle that was taller than all the other buildings in the city. Its towers were lost in the blizzard. A faint blue light shone from its ice windows.
Seris was the first to break the silence.
"We go there."
Lian nodded. He was thinking the same thing. If any place was going to have information or treasure, it would definitely be there.
They continued on their path toward the city center. The closer they got, the more footprints appeared.
Bigger. Stranger. And of course, more terrifying. On some walls, claw marks several meters long could be seen.
Some buildings looked like they had been cut in half with a single blow. But despite all this, there were no corpses. They did not even see any more frozen guardians.
There were no monster corpses either that would show a fight between monsters.
After a while, they reached the central square. And then... both stopped.
In the middle of the square, something stood. At first glance, it looked like an ice hill. But when they got closer... they realized they were wrong.
This was a creature.
A monster. An ice giant. Over fifteen meters tall. Its body was like a mountain of blue crystal and ice.
Two massive horns stuck out from its head. Its hands looked like the claws of an ancient giant. And on its chest, dozens of broken ice spears were embedded.
As if an entire army had once fought to stop it, but had failed.
Lian swallowed.
A panel immediately appeared in front of him.
[Frostfallen Titan]
[Rank: Fallen]
[Level: ???]
His eyes narrowed. A Fallen monster! This creature was on the same bloodline and status level as that Fallen Wolf!

And worse than that, this monster’s level was at least ten levels above him! That meant it was many times stronger than that Fallen Wolf. This monster had power equal to a normal rank level 30 or even 35 monster.
And this was not good news at all.
"Can you see its level?" He looked at Seris. This girl had a higher level than him. She might be able to see this monster’s level.
"Yes. Level 19." Seris nodded, but a small frown could also be seen on her face.
Lian also frowned. Level 19. That was 12 levels above him. And it was a Fallen monster. This was a big problem.
"Can you defeat it?"
"I don’t think so." Seris thought for a moment and then said in a normal tone. But her answer did not make the situation much better.
Lian stared at the ice giant for a few seconds. No movement could be seen. No breath. No sound. Just a massive pile of ice.
"Do you think it is alive?" He added.
"I don’t think so."
But at that very moment, a sound was heard.
Crack...
A weak sound, like ice cracking. Both immediately fell silent. Their eyes locked onto the ice giant.
A few seconds passed.
Nothing happened. Then again.
Crack...
This time clearer. One of the layers of ice on the creature’s chest cracked. The silence of the square suddenly became heavier.
Neither spoke.
But both understood one thing. Whatever was in front of them was not completely dead. And it might wake up soon.

chapters.title: Chapter 21: Hunters Become the Hunted
paragraphs: Crack.
The sound of ice cracking was heard from the center of the square for the second time. Lian did not hesitate for even a moment.
His gaze fixed on that massive ice monster frozen in the middle of the square. Then he said in a completely serious tone.
"If that thing wakes up, we cannot defeat it."
For the first time, Seris did not disagree. The silver-haired girl just stared at the frozen ice monster for a few seconds, then shook her head.
"I think so too."
And that alone was enough. Seris was not the kind of person who was afraid of anything. If she herself had decided to retreat, it meant that creature was truly dangerous.
A level 19 Fallen monster is not something they can handle. This monster is so powerful that it could kill that Fallen Wolf with a single hit.
They were not stupid enough to fight such a monster.
Both of them left the square silently. The massive monster remained motionless.
The city was still submerged in silence. Snow quietly settled on the frozen streets. Massive crystal buildings stood on both sides of the path.
Statues of unknown warriors could be seen in different corners of the city.
Everything was frozen. Everything was dead. But the further they went into the city, the stranger they felt.
"Footprints."
Lian suddenly stopped. Seris also looked down. On the fresh snow, there were footprints. But these footprints did not belong to just one creature.
Some looked like wolves. Some looked like reptiles. Some were so strange that they could not even be identified.
And more interestingly, the footprints were fresh. Very fresh.
"We are heading toward where the monsters probably are." Lian frowned.
"Stronger than that Titan?" Seris asked.
"I am not sure, but I doubt it." He thought for a moment and then answered. It is unlikely that a monster stronger than that Fallen monster is near here.
"But that is not the important question. The important thing is, what does that castle have that makes all the monsters go toward it?" Lian added.
Monsters do not go toward one point for no reason.
They continued on their path. Through narrow streets, past collapsed buildings, past squares that were probably once the center of life in this city.
But no creature could be seen. No sound, no movement, no sign of life. The only thing that existed were the many footprints.
Footprints that increased more and more the further they went. As if hundreds of different creatures lived in this city.
But none of them could be seen. And that was even scarier.
A few minutes later, they saw the castle. In the distance, in the heart of Frostheart, a massive castle made of ice and crystal. Its towers were hundreds of meters high.
Walls that shone even through the blizzard. And a blue light that shone from the highest tower up to the sky.
"If there is anything valuable in this city, it is there."
"Probably." Seris agreed.
So they continued on their path toward the castle. But at that moment, the footprints suddenly ended.
As if the creatures of the city did not dare to go further from this point. Lian noticed this.
And that made him feel bad. But before he had time to think... a sound was heard from behind them.
Crunch.
Crunch.
Crunch.
The sound of footsteps on snow. A lot of them. Very close.
Seris immediately turned around. Her eyes narrowed.
"We are getting visitors."
Shadows dropped down from the icy roofs.
One.
Two.
Five.
Ten.
Fifteen.
Within a few seconds, the street around them was filled. Lian stared at the creatures in front of him.
Bodies that were almost human. About two and a half meters tall. White skin covered in frozen fur. Massive horns like a deer’s. Hands with long, deadly claws.
But the worst part was their faces. Faces that looked human but were not complete. As if something had tried to imitate a human and failed.
[Frosthorn Stalker]
[Rank: Normal]
[Level 10]
[Frosthorn Stalker]
[Rank: Normal]
[Level 11]
[Frosthorn Stalker]
[Rank: Normal]
[Level 10]
"Fifteen monsters, but instead of being a threat, they look like a reward." Lian chuckled.
They needed to increase their power somehow. And what better way than these monsters? They were like free prey walking into the lion’s mouth.
Seris smiled a little. But her eyes shone. Finally, she could fight again and release her anger on these poor creatures.
And then the monsters attacked.
Everything exploded. The monsters charged from all four sides with terrible speed.
Lian moved.
BOOM!
His fist hit the first monster’s face directly. The sound of bones crushing echoed in the street. The monster was thrown several meters back.
But before it could hit the ground, Lian appeared in front of it.
Second hit.
Its neck broke. The corpse fell on the snow.
[You have killed a level 10 Frosthorn Stalker]
[4 Stat Points gained]
[Congratulations, you have obtained a Talent]
But there was no time to stop. A claw came toward his neck from behind. He ducked, turned, and drove his elbow into the monster’s chest.
Bones crushed. Icy blood sprayed on the snow.
[You have killed a level 10 Frosthorn Stalker]
On the other side.
Seris moved like a crazy storm. She had no sword, but her body itself was a weapon.
Fist.
Knee.
Elbow.
Each hit put one of the monsters on the ground. But their number was high.
Too high.
The monsters attacked nonstop. The more time passed, the more wounds they had.
But it did not matter how many there were. Unfortunately for them, they had run into monsters among humans. The creatures that thought they were hunters had now become the hunted.
And as expected, the monsters realized what a mistake they had made. They thought they had found easy prey.
But they did not know that they had run into butchers.

Seris was also standing a few meters away. She was breathing heavily, but a small smile could still be seen on her face.
System notifications appeared.

But there were so many that they could completely surround them.

[Frostfang Alpha Wolf]
[Rank: Normal]
[Level 15]

[Frostfang Wolf]
[Rank: Normal]
[Level 14]
[Frostfang Wolf]
[Rank: Normal]
[Level 14]
[Frostfang Wolf]
[Rank: Normal]
[Level 13]

There was no way to escape.
But was there even any need to worry?

Lian did not hesitate for even a moment.
His gaze fixed on that massive ice monster frozen in the middle of the square.

chapters.title: Chapter 22: Inside The Castle
paragraphs: The sound of the wolves’ howls still echoed through all of Frostheart. The frozen winds passed through the crystal towers, creating a sound like the moaning of ghosts.
Lian and Seris stood in front of the massive castle gate. Behind them was the ice city. From the distant streets, the sounds of howls, roars, and heavy footsteps could be heard.
And in front of them were more than twenty ice wolves, most of them above level 13.
Among them also stood a level 15 wolf. Its bright blue eyes burned like two icy flames in the darkness.
They had no way back and no way forward. But neither of their faces looked worried. Even though the enemy had a significant advantage in numbers, in raw power, it was not the same.
Seris had alone been able to slaughter a Fallen Wolf, and that wolf was stronger than each of these wolves. And Lian? With his current power, he could also easily handle each of them.
No one spoke. Then the strongest wolf roared, and the whole pack started moving.
The frozen ground shook.
"You handle the left side." Lian said quietly.
The first wolf attacked him from the right. Its massive claw split the air.
Lian ducked. The claw passed over his head. For Lian, who now had speed several times that of a normal human, speed that at least none of these monsters had, the speed of this attack seemed too slow.
Then he gathered all his power into his right fist.
BOOM!
His fist hit the wolf’s jaw directly. The sound of breaking bones echoed in the air. The wolf was lifted off the ground like a bullet and hit an ice wall several meters away.
[Frostfang Wolf level 12 killed]
[You have gained 4 stat points]
[Skill obtained]
[Blood Hunt]
[Rank: Common (+)]
[Passively enhances all of the user’s senses by two times. Hunting instincts become stronger. Tracking monsters becomes easier. Can identify different blood smells.]
But he did not have a chance to look at the notification. Three other wolves attacked him from both sides.
At the same time, Seris also entered the fight. Even though she had lost her sword, she still fought like a humanoid monster.
She jumped onto the head of one of the wolves and slammed her knee onto the monster’s skull. The sound of crushing bone was loud.
Then she grabbed the monster’s body and threw it directly at another wolf. The two monsters rolled on the ground. Seris charged toward them without stopping.
Meanwhile, Lian was in his own fight. A claw scratched his arm. Blood sprayed on the snow, but he did not even frown.
His speed had now reached a level where the normal wolves could barely touch him. He slid under the attack of one wolf.
He stood up and drove his fist into the monster’s throat.
CRACK!
The neck’s spine broke. The monster fell to the ground.
[Frostfang Wolf level 12 killed]
More monsters attacked. But as time passed, Lian became more adapted to his new power and more skilled in fighting these monsters.
He was no longer that weak young man who had to fight a deadly battle to kill one mammoth bear. Now his physical power had reached a level where his fists were truly deadly.
A few minutes later, the body of the fifth wolf fell to the ground.
[Frostfang Wolf level 12 killed]
[You have gained 4 stat points]
[Skill Acquired]
[Frost Claw]
[Rank: Common (+)]
[Effects: Focuses mana on the user’s hands and turns the nails and fingers into ice blades for 10 seconds.
Effect: +15 penetration power. Wounds caused are hard to heal. Consumes 0.1 mana per Minute of activation.]

Lian’s eyes lit up. An offensive skill. Exactly what he needed in this environment. But he still did not have a chance to examine it further. Aside from this, he had also obtained a Talent and another skill.
But he was not in a situation to look at any of them.
On the other side of the field, the fourth wolf also died under Seris’s blows. The young girl was breathing heavily. Her silver hair was soaked in blood.
Her left arm was wounded, but her gaze remained cold and emotionless.
However... the situation was not as good as they thought it was. Nine wolves had been killed, but the remaining wolves were still many.
And more importantly, behind them, another pack of monsters was hidden, waiting for a chance to attack and hunt the two.
Seris and Lian came together and stood back to back, staring at their surroundings. The monsters had become more cautious around them. They showed their sharp teeth but did not attack directly.
"They have become cautious about attacking. Maybe we can use this chance and do a burst attack." Lian thought and then said.
"Burst attack?" Apparently, Seris was not familiar with this word.
"We charge at full speed toward a group of them and try to deal the most damage in one attack."
But before they could agree on doing it, a strange sound was heard.
All the wolves suddenly stopped. Even the alpha wolf. Then they let out a short roar and stepped back a few steps.
Lian and Seris looked at each other in surprise.
What had happened?
Creak...
Another sound came. This time from behind the castle gate. The massive ice door opened slightly. Just a few centimeters. But that amount was enough for all the wolves to suddenly show panic.
Even the alpha wolf.
The monster that moments ago was ready to tear them apart stepped back one step, then another step, and then the whole pack retreated.
Lian had no intention of asking questions.
"Go!"
Seris did not need an explanation either. Both ran toward the gate at the same time. At the last moment, Lian also put two wolf corpses into his storage space.
Maybe they would be useful later. They could only handle hunger for two weeks. If a situation came where they needed food, this would be helpful.
Then both passed through the crack in the gate. At that moment, the door closed behind them.
BOOM!
Silence. Just silence. For a few seconds, neither spoke. Then they looked around.
And their frowns deepened. Inside the castle, there were human bodies. Several bodies. Of course, calling them bodies was wrong. They were all frozen.
But the problem was not that they were frozen. The problem was that they were leaning against the walls, and their bodies looked very bony.
Their faces were intact, but it seemed like they had not eaten for a long time before freezing. The eyes of some of them had completely decayed.
They sat at a significant distance from each other. They were in a defensive position relative to each other. Next to each one, there was a weapon.
Lian quietly approached one of the bodies. He examined its clothes. Then suddenly, his eyes narrowed.
On the chest of the clothes, there was a symbol. A familiar flag. Very familiar. The same design, the same pattern. The same symbol he had seen on the clothes of the village guards.
"This..." Seris also noticed.
"It’s the same symbol." Lian said quietly.
Silence followed. His mind worked quickly. It was clear that this was the same symbol he had seen in the village. This symbol was also on the painting in the village elder’s room.
This symbol was made based on the golden mountain. And this meant one thing. This city and that village were connected.

"We did not find any frozen bodies in the city except for those guardians. Either the rest of the city’s people were eaten by monsters, or they escaped. And if it’s the second, then the people of that village might be the same people from this city." Lian expressed his reasoning.
If these people were the same people from the village, how had they managed to escape? And what had happened to them?
And more importantly, what had happened to Frostheart?
"How far are we from that village?" Seris suddenly asked.
"I don’t know. Maybe a few hundred kilometers. But not more than a thousand kilometers." He thought for a moment and answered.
At that time, he had run for hours. Even he himself did not know how far they had gotten from the village.
Seris was silent. It was clear that she also had questions about how the people of this city were connected to that village and that mountain.
But for now, there were no answers. They continued moving. A large part of the castle was buried under dozens of meters of ice.
Hallways were blocked. Stairs had collapsed. Many rooms were completely unreachable. Almost a large part of the castle was frozen.

However, the further they went, Lian noticed something. The cold bothered him less. Looking at Seris, it was clear her body was shivering from the cold. As if the further they went, the colder the air became.
But strangely, he did not feel anything.
Could it be related to the new Talent he had received?
Even breathing had become easier.
"Something is strange." A few minutes later, Seris suddenly said.
"What?"
"Those wolves."
Lian looked at her.
"If they wanted to enter, they could have. Their number was too high." Seris continued.
"That’s right."
"Then why were they just waiting outside?"
Lian thought for a few moments.
"Probably something is here. Something that stops monsters from entering and advancing." He then said quietly.
Seris said nothing. But both of them were thinking about exactly the same thing. Unfortunately, they had no information to base any reasoning on.
Finally, they reached the end of one of the main hallways. There, a massive door stood.
Bigger than any door they had seen before. Its entire surface was covered in ice. Seris stepped forward and raised her fist.
And she hit.
BOOM!
Just a small scratch.
"Damn it."
Then Lian stepped forward. They looked at each other and attacked at the same time.
BOOM!
BOOM!
BOOM!
The sound of their hits echoed in the castle. After several consecutive hits...
CRAAAAAACK!
The door finally broke. Pieces of ice were thrown around. The path was opened. They entered.
Inside was a massive royal hall. The ceiling was dozens of meters high. Giant ice pillars filled both sides of the hall.
And at the end of it, there was a royal throne. On the throne sat a human skeleton.
Lian quietly walked forward. He looked at the bones. The size of the skeleton was relatively delicate.
"Probably a woman."
Seris shrugged.
But at that moment, something under the bones caught Lian’s attention. A small object.
He bent down and pulled it out. Its surface was frozen, but it was still usable.
A notebook. An old leather cover.
Lian and Seris looked at each other. Then they opened the notebook. The first page slowly turned. And they understood what they had in their hands.
"This is a diary!"

Pieces of ice were thrown around.
The path was opened.
They entered.
Inside was a massive royal hall.
The ceiling was dozens of meters high.
Giant ice pillars filled both sides of the hall.
And at the end of it, there was a royal throne.
On the throne sat a human skeleton.
Lian quietly walked forward.
He looked at the bones.
The size of the skeleton was relatively delicate.
"Probably a woman."
Seris shrugged.
But at that moment, something under the bones caught Lian’s attention.
A small object.
He bent down and pulled it out.
Its surface was frozen, but it was still usable.
A notebook.
An old leather cover.
Lian and Seris looked at each other.
Then they opened the notebook.
The first page slowly turned.
And they understood what they had in their hands.
"This is a diary!"

chapters.title: Chapter 23: A Princess’ Diary
paragraphs: Lian stared at the notebook for a few seconds. A heavy silence had taken over the frozen hall.
Seris stood next to him, looking at the notebook.
This was a diary. A diary written by one of the residents of this city. A diary that might answer some of their questions.
"Can you read it?"
"Yes." Lian nodded.
He drew his finger across the first page. The writing was in a completely unknown language. Not like the language of their world, and not like any language he had seen before.
But at that moment, a notification appeared.
[The Will’s translation ability activated]
[Language identified]
[Automatic translation started]
Lian’s eyes widened a little. As expected, The Will had shown its strange ability again.
He could read the text without any problem.
He slowly turned the first page.
First day of winter.
Today, snow started to fall. Father says this winter will be a little harder, but the people are not worried.
The city of Frostheart has always survived harsh winters.
Lian flipped ahead a few pages. The writing had slowly changed.
Week three.
The snow is still continuing. Mother says this is not normal. Some of the surrounding farms are completely buried under snow.
Month two.
The snow does not stop. The people of the city are slowly becoming worried.
Month six.
We can no longer go far from the city walls. Everything is white. No animals remain. No plants can be seen.
"This is no normal winter. Could this winter be the reason for the city’s destruction?" Seris said quietly.
Lian said nothing. He just opened the next page. There was no need to answer. Naturally, the further they went, the more answers they would get.
And the further he went, the darker the diary’s atmosphere became.
First year.
Today, five people died from the cold. No one laughs anymore. No one is happy because of the snowfall. The snow that once brought life to the city... is now causing death and destruction.
Second year.
Many houses have become empty. Some families go to sleep at night and do not wake up in the morning.
Third year.
I turned eighteen today. But there is no celebration. No one celebrates anymore.
Lian paused for a moment. Three years. Three years of nonstop snow. Even imagining it was hard, especially in such a remote city that had no access to anywhere.
Such snow would cause animals to die or flee. That meant there would be no food or supplies left for the people. They could go to distant places to hunt.
But how far? And who knew if distant places would be safe?
He continued.
The city council decided that we should leave Frostheart. If we stay, we will all die.
Our only hope is the Mountain God. The golden mountain. The symbol of our city. Father says it is still sacred there.
Maybe we can start a new life.
Lian and Seris looked at each other at the same time. The golden mountain. The same mountain. The same mountain where the village was built at its base, and where the key is located.
Lian’s heart became a little heavy. So the people of this city clearly knew the golden mountain. The place where the key was. The item that could let them leave the ruined realm.
He went to the next page.
People left the city in groups. Each group took some of the supplies with them.
Wood, stone, tools, food, everything. They wanted to build a new city. New homes. A new life. New hope.
This group was led by my brother. They headed toward the Mountain God.
A few pages later, the princess’s handwriting had become more shaky.
Only the last group remains.
Father, me, the servants, the guards, and some of the remaining people. We will leave in another week.
Then...
The text suddenly changed.
Today, the snow stopped! For the first time in three years, I cried. Everyone cried.
We thought we were saved. We thought it was over.
But we were wrong.
They came. From every direction. Through the snow. Through the blizzard.
Monsters. Hundreds of monsters. Strange wolves that did not look like normal wolves at all. Ice giants. Creatures we had never seen before.
But the scariest ones were not them.
That being. That monster. That king.
Even on paper, it seemed the writer was afraid to write its name. The handwriting was messy.
No one knew what it was. No one knew where it came from. But all the monsters were afraid of it. Even the monsters did not look at it.
But it ruled over that army of monsters like a king.
It was huge and terrifying.
"That same Fallen one." Seris said quietly.
"Probably." Lian nodded.
He remembered the image of that frozen giant in the center of the city. That massive creature. That monster that was terrifying even while sleeping.
In this entire city, they had not seen any other monster as powerful as that one. A monster that was only one level away from its first evolution.
Just like humans, monsters can evolve every twenty levels.
Then he continued and turned to the next page.
The battle began. Father personally took command of the defense. The guards fought.
The knights fought. Everyone fought. But it was useless.
I saw father get killed. I saw my friends get torn apart.
I saw people running. I saw children crying. I saw my city dying.
Ink had spread on part of the page, as if drops of tears had fallen on the paper.
I just stood there. I could not do anything. I was weak. I was not like my brother. I could not defend anyone.
I wish my brother was here. If he was here, could everything have gone differently?
We retreated to the castle. Only a few remained alive.
Me, some servants, some guards, and some ordinary people along with my father’s chief advisor. We were barely twenty people. More than forty had been killed.
The chief advisor... he was a great mage. The last great mage of this land.
He sacrificed himself. I did not understand what he did. I just saw light. Golden light. And then everything stopped.
The monsters could no longer enter the castle. We were saved.
At least for a while.
"So that is why the wolves could not enter." Seris looked around.
Lian nodded and confirmed. That mage had probably performed some kind of defensive magic mechanism by sacrificing himself, protecting the castle and the survivors.
Six months passed.
We are still alive. Still waiting for my brother to come and save us. He will surely understand that something is wrong. He will surely come to save us.
Ten months.
Food has become low. And my brother still has not come... why? Why has he not come? Could something have happened to them too?
One year.
The monsters are still outside. But that massive monster is asleep.
I looked at it from the top of the tower.
It was asleep. And that same day, the snow started again. I think its sleep is the reason for the snowfall.
Lian’s eyes narrowed. So the reason for that endless snowfall and that this whole area was covered in snow was the sleep of that Fallen monster?
Such power is truly catastrophic. It could destroy entire generations.
"The only way for them to survive was to kill that Fallen monster." Seris added with a frown.
"But that was not possible for them. Aside from the power of that Fallen one itself, an army was also protecting it."
Then Lian reached the last pages. At that moment, he frowned. The princess’s handwriting was no longer neat. It was shaky. Torn. As if the writer was breaking down.
Food is gone.
We have not eaten for three days.
Today, one of the servants disappeared. I did not know what happened.
But another week passed, and another servant disappeared.
And again, a week later, another person disappeared... but this time it was one of the ordinary people.
I think I know what happened. But I do not want to believe it.
May God forgive us.
May God forgive us.
May God forgive us.
Lian felt the hair on the back of his neck stand up. Seris also frowned and was not in a better state. She felt nauseous and wanted to vomit.
Both of them knew where the rest of the story was going. But neither wanted to hear it.
"How could they do such a thing?"
"Hunger can drive a person insane." Lian sighed. He slowly opened the last readable page.
And he saw a sentence that made him stay completely silent for a few seconds.
I thought monsters were my greatest fear. But they were not. Even the cold was not the greatest fear.
The greatest fear... was hungry humans.

chapters.title: Chapter 24: Child Of Winter
paragraphs: The royal hall had fallen into a heavy silence. The sound of the wind passing through the frozen cracks of the castle echoed like the moaning of lost ghosts in the dark space.
Lian closed the diary. For a few moments, he did not say anything.
Even Seris had become quiet.
The atmosphere around them was suffocating. Not because of the cold, but because of what they had just understood.
Lian quietly looked at the bones on the royal throne. Then he turned his gaze toward the broken door of the hall.
"Now I understand."
"What?" Seris raised her head.
Lian sighed.
"Those bodies we saw outside, the ones sitting by the walls in the entrance hall."
He was quiet for a few seconds.
"Do you remember how they were not close to each other? Each one sat at a distance from the others. Their weapons were also next to them."
Seris’s eyes slowly narrowed. Then she suddenly understood.
"You mean..."
"Yes."
Lian did not take his gaze off the bones.
"Hunger. They were afraid of each other. Afraid of one another."
"After the food ran out, they started eating each other."
Seris did not say anything, but her face had clearly changed.
Lian continued.
"The princess probably realized the situation was getting out of control. That is why she ran away. She locked herself inside this hall."
"She closed the door from the inside and hoped the others could not get in."
Then he pointed to the bones on the throne.
"She survived for a while, but in the end, she either died of hunger or from the cold."
Seris clenched her fists.
"That is inhuman."
Lian looked at her for a moment.
"You are wrong. That is completely human. When you take everything away from a person... civilization, morals, hope, food... what remains is the animal nature of a human."
For a few seconds, neither of them spoke.
Then Seris asked:
"So what happened to the rest of the people?"
"If this city fell, why did her brother not come to help them?"
Lian thought for a moment, then slowly shook his head.
"I don’t know."
"But the people of that village are definitely connected to this city. The flags were the same. The symbols were the same."
"They were probably the survivors of this city, or at least the next generation of them." But he immediately frowned.
"But there is a problem."
Seris looked at him.
"The bodies here are only bones. But the bodies under the village still had flesh and skin. They seemed much newer."
"So either these events happened at two different times... or we still do not know a large part of the truth."

Lian had doubts about this matter and did not understand what had happened in this part. Because if nothing had happened to the survivors who went to the village back then, then why did they not come to help?
First of all, he needed to know exactly how many years had passed since this event. But there was no evidence that could tell him that.
Seris frowned. It was clear she did not like these mysteries. She was more a person of the sword than of thinking.
Finally, she stood up.
"I want to look around the castle. The air here is suffocating me." Today she had faced something beyond her understanding and perception of humans, and her worldview had changed.
Lian nodded.
"Okay, but be careful. There should be no monsters inside the castle. But if something happens, shout."
Seris said nothing. She just left the hall. The sound of her footsteps slowly faded away.
And the silence returned. Lian sat on one of the frozen chairs. For the first time in hours, he had a chance to breathe.
And more importantly, a chance to examine himself.
"Status panel."
A blue window appeared in front of his eyes.
[Name: Lian Vonhelm]
[Level: 8]
[Race: Human]
[Class: Monster]
[Talents: Dormant Monster (SSS), Child Of Winter (C)]
[Innate Skills: Glutton, Bloodlust, Butcher, Winter Skin, Frost Dominion]
[Skills: Fallen Wolf Speed, Iron hide, Blood Hunt, Frost Claw
[Titles: Explorer of the Lost City, Wolf Slayer]
[Stats: Click to see]
[Fragments: 21/100]
Lian’s eyes stayed on his level. Level eight. After all those fights, he had only increased by one level.
This itself showed that leveling up becomes harder the further you go. But what caught his attention more was his new talent.
Winter Child.
He tapped on it.
[ Child Of Winter]
[Rank: C (+)]
Description: You have been accepted by the energy of the ice element. Natural resistance to cold increases. Limited control of the ice element in icy environments may be possible.
Power of frost-based skills increases. Overall body performance increases in icy environments.]
Lian’s eyes lit up.
"So that’s why..." Ever since entering Frostheart, he had noticed that the cold of this area affected him less.
Now he knew the reason. But that was not the only change. His gaze fell on the new innate skills.
Winter Skin.
[Winter Skin]
[Description: Your body gains more resistance against cold, freezing, and damage or attacks caused by frost attacks or monsters.]
Lian gave a small smile. A simple skill, but very useful. Besides, when he goes through his first evolution, this skill will definitely become even stronger.
In general, talents and innate skills can only be upgraded through evolutions, increasing their rank and abilities.
And of course, not every talent and innate skill can be upgraded. Only those that have a (+) can be upgraded.
Then he clicked on the last one.
Frost Dominion.
[Frost Dominion]
[Description: Ability to have limited control over Frost present in the environment. At lower levels, creating ice is not possible. Uses 0.2 mana per Minute of use.]
Lian raised his eyebrow. Currently, his mana was very low. But this innate skill could become something terrifying in the future.
If he got his first evolution, if the rank of this talent increased, then he might be able to create ice from nothing.
But something else occupied his mind.
Fragments.
Twenty-one.
He frowned.
"Wait..." Before entering the city, he only had one fragment. He had gotten ten more from discovering Frostheart.
So where had the ten extra fragments come from? There was no way he could have gotten that many fragments by killing that many monsters.
Something came to his mind. He looked at his old title.
Wolf Slayer.
He opened its description.
[Wolf Slayer]
[You are the first person to have slaughtered a Fallen Wolf. From now on, for every wolf you kill: +2 Fragments.]
For a moment, Lian’s eyes widened. Then a smile appeared on his face.
"So that is the reason."
He had killed five frost wolves. So that was why he had gotten ten fragments. Everything fell into place.
And more importantly, outside the castle, there were more than twenty other wolves. If he killed all of them, the amount of fragments he would get would be insane.
That way, his number of fragments would reach more than 60. Would it not be possible to easily upgrade all his skills like that?
Then he clicked on Stats to take a look at them.
[Strength: 78]
[Spirit: 5]
[Speed: 66 ]
[Mana: 3]
[Resistance: 32]
[Stat Points: 68 ]
68 Stats Points!.
A number that surprised even himself.
He had earned 20 points from discovering the city, 28 points from killing 7 Frost Stalker monsters (each kill gave 4 points), and then another 20 from killing wolves (each again giving 4 points).
He had also realized that the system rounds the points, for example, if a monster’s stat is actually 466 percent, his talent only gives him 4 points for it.
His strength and speed were insanely high, but he also had clear weaknesses.
Mana, soul, and resistance were all low. If he faced a creature like Mira again, these weaknesses could be deadly.
Especially for using his new innate skill and his other offensive skill, he needed mana.
Lian leaned back on the chair and stared at his stats pointes
His finger hovered over the floating window. Now was the time to choose. A choice that could determine the outcome of future battles.
A small smile appeared on his lips.
"The best way to use these points..."
At that moment, a heavy sound was heard from deep inside the castle. The sound of something very large being hit.
Lian immediately stood up. His eyes narrowed.
"Seris...?" He was sure that girl had done something again.
