But at that moment, Aria’s face lost its color, as if she had seen a ghost.
Ryan also froze.
Alisa started to tremble.
Suddenly, all three backed away in horror, as if an enemy was standing in front of them, not a rescuer.
Lian frowned.
"What’s wrong?" Lian frowned and could not understand the reason for their behavior.
"Stay away!" Aria shouted with a trembling voice.
"You are monsters!"
Lian and Seris both stopped.
A few moments of silence passed.
Ryan threw himself in front of the two girls, and despite his legs shaking, despite his obvious fear, he still stood.
"I won’t let you hurt them!"
Lian was confused.
"What do you mean?" What was happening here?
Did they look like ghosts that these three were so terrified?
"You thought we didn’t see?!" Aria’s eyes filled with tears.
"You killed all the village children!"
Lian completely froze.
"What?
When did we do that?
"Don’t lie!" Tears fell down Aria’s face.
"We saw everything!" Images of that night appeared in front of her eyes.
Children.
Screams.
Blood.
Corpses.
And two monsters that were Lian and Seris.
Lian suddenly remembered something.
The children.
All those children.
When he had fought the villagers, there were no children.
Not even one.
They had completely disappeared.
And now he realized that he had not seen any children in the village.
Of course, he was sure those children were actually monsters, not real humans.
But regardless, they were not there.
"Brainwashed?" Seris whispered quietly.
Lian was thinking the same thing, and if not, what other answer could there be?
But the question is, why would they brainwash these three?
He even thought that these three should have been dead by now, and that they are still alive is a surprise in itself to him.
He could not understand, what is this final mutation?
Why are these three being kept for it?
And why were they in these cocoons?
What is this cocoon?
But before he could answer, a sound echoed in the cave.
Grrrrrrrrrrrr...
All four turned toward the sound.
At the end of the cave, the massive stone door began to open.
The ground shook.
A golden light shone from the crack in the door.
And then the sound of footsteps was heard.
Tak.
Tak.
Then a familiar voice was heard.
"Is the ceremony finally over?"
Lian’s eyes suddenly narrowed.
He knew this voice.
Very well.
The light moved aside, and a man came out from behind the door.
A calm smile was on his face.
The same usual smile, the same friendly smile.
The village chief!
He glanced at the torn cocoons, then his gaze slid over Aria and the others, and finally fixed on Lian and Seris.
His smile deepened.
"Oh?
So you two came back."
At that moment, a new notification appeared in front of Lian’s eyes.
[Dreadmaw]
[Rank: Mutated]
[Level: 20]
He glanced briefly at the notification.
Fortunately, they were not facing a Fallen one; the monster in front of them was a level 20 Mutated.
The village chief smiled, looking at them for a long time.
"It’s good that you came back, because with you, the ceremony will go better." He then said quietly.

chapters.title: Chapter 35: The Dreadmaw Sovereign
paragraphs: "Come, let’s go. The god wants to see you." The village chief looked at the twins and Ryan, then without paying any attention to Lian and Seris, he turned and went inside.
Excitement appeared in the eyes of the twins. They had heard many things about the Mountain God, and finally they could see him with their own eyes.
Aria took Ryan’s hand, and then all three went inside behind the old man.
"Should we go too?" Seris looked at Lian. She herself did not feel good and preferred not to do this.
"Don’t worry." He did not want to retreat now. He wanted to see this monster with his own eyes.
The girl nodded, and they also entered. But when they entered, they froze in their place and stared at the creature sitting on a black stone throne at the end of the hall.
For a few seconds, neither could speak. As if the air itself had become heavier. As if every breath had become a painful effort.
Lian felt his heart beating with unnatural intensity. Not from fear of a strong enemy, not from the excitement of battle, but from a primitive instinct.
An instinct that screamed:
Run.
Run right now.
In front of his eyes, a system notification appeared.
[Dreadmaw Sovereign]
[Level 20]
[Rank: Unholy]
That was it.
No other explanation was needed. It was not necessary. These three lines were enough for any sane person to turn around and run with all their power and speed.
This made Lian’s frown even deeper.
"So this is the Mountain God?" Seris whispered quietly. She also had no interest in fighting such a monster.
Lian did not answer.
His eyes were fixed on the monster. At least three meters tall. Red skin. Horns twisted like tree branches. A long smile that looked more like a permanent scar on its face than a real mouth.
But suddenly, something else caught Lian’s attention.
Around the creature’s neck, there was a golden key. A key that, unlike the dark atmosphere of the hall, emitted a bright and calm aura.
Lian’s eyes widened a little.
That was it. Without a doubt, the exit key. The key they had been looking for since the beginning of entering this realm.
But now it hung around the neck of a creature that seemed difficult to even look at directly.
At that moment, the village chief stepped forward and with absolute respect, the words came out of his mouth.
"My god." His voice echoed quietly in the hall.
"As you wished, I have brought them."
The Dreadmaw Sovereign raised its head a little. Its dark eyes slid over the three teenagers.
"Are they ready?" It said with a deep voice, completely devoid of any emotion, as if it looked down on all creatures from above.
"I think we are about to find out." The village chief smiled.
Aria was confused. She looked between the old man and the creature on the throne.
"Village chief..." Her voice trembled.
"What is happening here?"
Alisa also turned pale.

"You said this place was sacred. You said the god protects us... You said he could help us go back home..." Aria added with fear. The creature in front of them looked more like a demonic god than a mountain god.
But the village chief looked at them playfully. His face was still calm, but the usual kindness was no longer in his gaze.
As if the mask he had worn for years had finally fallen off.
"Naive children. Still haven’t you understood? You were never going to be saved?"
"What...?" The faces of Aria and Alisa lost their color.
"You are just sacrifices."
A heavy silence filled the hall. As if even the wind had stopped moving.
Aria’s eyes filled with disbelief. Alisa stepped back.
"Stop joking." Ryan also frowned.
"Joking?" But the village chief just laughed.
"Especially you. You are going to be the god’s sacrifice." Then his gaze fixed on Aria.
Aria froze.
"Me...?" Aria froze, feeling a bone-chilling cold in her spine. Her body started to tremble from fear.
"Yes." Suddenly, the old man raised his hand, grabbed the girl’s neck tightly, and her body slowly lifted off the ground.
Fear slowly formed in the young girl’s eyes. She tried with all her might to free herself from those hands.
She was trying to breathe, but it was useless. Every moment, breathing became harder, and less air entered her lungs.
Her eyes turned red. She could feel death. She could feel that this was her end.
She was truly scared!
"Let my sister go!" Alisa stepped forward, begging and pleading for the old man to release her sister.
Ryan also stood between them, trying to separate the village chief’s hands from Aria’s neck.
"Bastard, let her go!" He shouted and tried to save his love. But his efforts were useless.
He felt like he was trying to move a mountain. Simply impossible.
But the village chief did not even look at them. His eyes were only on Aria, like a hunter who had finally found his desired prey.
"Please... let my sister go... anything you want... I’ll do anything..." Alisa cried from the bottom of her heart and begged.
"Really? Anything I want?" The village chief gave a sadistic smile and looked at her.
"Yes... please... just let her go..."
The old man released Aria and threw her to the ground, causing her to start gasping and coughing.
Then a sword appeared in the old man’s hands, and he threw it in front of Alisa.
"Kill him." He then pointed at Ryan.
His words caused absolute silence in the space. No one else knew what to say.
"What...?" Alisa felt she had heard wrong.
"I won’t repeat myself. You have 30 seconds. Either you kill him, or I kill your sister."
A sword lay on the ground. Tears flowed down Alisa’s face. She sobbed. She did not know what to do.
She had never hurt even an ant in her life. How could she kill a human?
But she did not dare say anything to the village chief. She was terrified.
Ryan clenched his fists. It seemed he had made his decision. He sighed.
He stepped forward, looked at the crying girl, and said calmly,
"Pick up the sword. I won’t resist."
Alisa heard those words and felt her heart hurt even more. Because of the crying, she could barely see.
"Only ten seconds left." The old man reminded.
Alisa looked at the sword with determination. She picked it up and pointed it at Ryan. She could not let her sister die! She would save her at any cost.
But before she could move it forward, Aria struggled to get up and stood between them. She could still barely breathe.
But she could not witness such a thing. It was as if her whole world was collapsing.
"No! You can’t do this!"
"Sister?" Alisa whispered in disbelief.
Aria said nothing. Then she suddenly gave a bitter smile. She looked at Ryan, her eyes trembling.
But her voice was calm.
"I don’t want you to die..."
Ryan remained silent.
"Ever since we came to this damned realm... you have been by my side..." A tear slid down from the corner of Aria’s eye.
"When I was scared, you were by my side... When I cried, you were by my side..."
"When I thought everything was over and I was going to die... you were still by my side."
Alisa lowered her head. She understood. Her sister had really fallen in love. Her stupid sister had really fallen in love...
Ryan still gave no answer. Aria gave a trembling smile.
"I..." Her voice broke.
"I love you..."
Suddenly, silence took over everything because of that confession. No one expected such a last-minute confession.
No one spoke.
But at that moment, Aria turned and looked at the old man.
"If you want to sacrifice someone, kill me. Leave them alone." It seemed she had made her decision and was determined.
But at that same time, Lian suddenly frowned. His enhanced senses had felt something. Something was wrong. Very wrong.
His eyes fixed on Ryan, and for the first time, he noticed. The boy’s eyes were no longer completely human. A strange darkness waved deep in his pupils.
As if something inside him had died long ago.
"Wait!" Lian suddenly shouted.
But it was too late. Everything happened in an instant.
Aria looked at her chest in disbelief... A large hole had been made there, and blood was pouring out.
And she saw a hand. A hand holding her heart.
She turned and looked at Ryan. With disbelief in her eyes, at his cold gaze, at his silence.
Her lips trembled. A tear fell from her face.
"Why...?" She asked with a weak, broken voice.

chapters.title: Chapter 36: The Truth I
paragraphs: Aria’s body fell to the ground with a muffled sound, and blood slowly flowed from under her body, spreading on the cracked floor.
Her eyes were still open, disbelief still visible in them, but there was no light in them anymore.
For a few seconds, no one spoke. As if even time had stopped.
Then a sound broke. A sound that was more like a moan than crying.
"Si... sister...?" Alisa fell to her knees, her hands trembling.
Her eyes were fixed on her sister’s lifeless body.
"Sister...?" There was no answer.
"Sister... get up..." Her voice trembled.
"Please get up..." She threw herself onto Aria’s body, took her bloody hands, and shook her.
Once more.
And once more.
But nothing happened.
"Please..." Her tears dripped onto her sister’s face.
"Please... enough joking..." Her breath broke.
"Sister..." And then she broke down. Her crying no longer sounded like a normal human’s cry. It was more like the scream of a creature that had lost its entire world.
"Sister!"
"Sister!"
"Sistereeee!" Her voice echoed through the entire hall, but there was no answer. No miracle happened. No salvation came.
Aria was dead. Completely dead.
Ryan, however, just watched. No emotion could be seen on his face. No sadness, no regret, no hesitation.
As if he had not just pulled a human’s heart out of her body moments before.
"Why...?" Seris whispered in disbelief. She still could not believe what she had seen.
Everything had happened too suddenly. A few seconds ago, Aria was alive. A few seconds ago, she was ready to sacrifice herself so Ryan could live.
And now... she was dead.
Lian was also staring at Ryan. His eyes narrowed, and his mind was putting the pieces of the puzzle together at a crazy speed.
"Now I understand..." He then said quietly.
Seris looked at him.
"What?"
Without taking his eyes off Ryan, Lian answered.
"Now I understand why he always avoided answering personal questions."
Seris frowned.
"What do you mean?"
"He does not belong to our world at all. He belongs to this one." Lian said quietly.
"But he is human." Seris was shocked and added in disbelief.
Lian nodded.
"That’s right."
Ryan really was a human. He had just tried to see Ryan’s information, and the system showed nothing.
All the monsters he had seen until that moment had information. Level, rank, and race.
But the system showed nothing for Ryan, exactly like other Awakened humans.
That meant the system did not recognize him as a monster, and he really was not a monster. He was just thinking, how long had this bastard monster been plotting against them?
From the time Ryan had found the twins? Or even before that? All this time, they had been like puppets under this bastard’s control?
At that moment, Ryan started moving. In his hands was still Aria’s heart, a heart that was still beating slowly even though it should have stopped.
He walked with slow steps toward the massive stone throne, toward the creature sitting at the head of the hall, toward the Dreadmaw Sovereign.
Then he knelt in front of the monster, lowered his head, and offered the heart with both hands.
"My lord."
The Dreadmaw Sovereign reached out its massive hand and took the heart.
For a moment, it held it in front of its face, then smelled it. Its black eyes narrowed a little.
"A heart..." Its voice was like the roar of breaking ice.
"With very strong emotions." A terrifying smile formed on its face.
"Perhaps this one will work."
"I did my best, my lord. I hope you are satisfied with the result." The village chief immediately bowed his head.
"We will see." The monster answered, and then its gaze slowly turned around the hall.
And stopped on Lian.
A feeling of danger immediately exploded throughout Lian’s being. As if an ancient predator had chosen him.
The monster’s smile deepened.
"And you..." Its claw pointed toward Lian.
"You can be my new skin."
Lian’s eyes turned cold. Now he understood almost everything, or at least a large part of the truth.
"Now I understand."
"What?" Seris felt like her brain was about to explode right now, and this boy still kept his calm?
Lian did not take his eyes off the monster.
"What has been happening here all this time. These aren’t even real monsters." He then added, pointing to the village chief.
Seris frowned.
"What do you mean?" Seris frowned. This old man and those bastards in the village that they killed were definitely monsters. What did he mean they weren’t real monsters?
"They are parasites. Parasites that can take over the bodies of other creatures."
Seris immediately answered.
"But we saw the villagers’ bodies. They hadn’t taken over anyone’s body. Their hearts had been removed."
Lian nodded.
"That’s right. Because they have mutated." He thought about the monster corpses they had killed outside.
About the human hearts he had found inside the disgusting bodies of those creatures. Everything now made sense.
"This is their new path of evolution. The hearts have become their source of power. They become one with the hearts of the creatures they hunt."
Seris remained silent. She felt like this information was too much for her.
Lian continued.
"Body, abilities, talents, even skills. They take everything from the heart’s owner." His eyes became playful.
"Probably in the past, they could only control bodies, but they could not use the real power of the victim. Now they have found a new way. A way that lets them steal everything."
Seris looked at the Dreadmaw Sovereign.
"So before the mutation... they were very weak?"
"Naturally." Lian answered.
"After all, they were only low-level normal monsters. But by swallowing hearts, they mutated and became something completely different."
"Of course, I think it’s not just about stealing the abilities of the body’s owners. Probably, they can also gain the power and skills of any human they kill and turn into their shape."
"When they possessed a body, they could neither use their own abilities nor use the abilities of that body."
"But when they swallowed the hearts, they no longer possess someone. They can just turn into that shape, so they can even use all their own abilities."
"The shape they have now is probably something they feel more comfortable in."
"So that one is also one of these parasites?" Seris looked at the massive creature on the throne.
For the first time, Lian paused, then slowly shook his head.
"No. The parasites are its children. That one is different."
A short silence followed.

"This is its real body. It has probably been looking for a way to get a human body for a long time while also keeping its own abilities and power, but it has not succeeded. That is why it created these parasites."
"Like experiments. Like tools, to find a way to achieve its goal."
"And it found a way. The hearts. With the help of hearts, instead of taking over a shell, it can turn into that shell and also keep its powers."
"Of course, it might want to completely take over a body and still keep its powers through the heart. That is why it probably needs a special heart."
"But why? Why would such a monster want a human body?" Seris still did not understand.
"I don’t know either." Lian said quietly, and continued.
"But I know it wants the hearts for transferring power. To build a new shell. A shell that can carry all its abilities."
His gaze fell on Aria’s heart.
"But why Aria’s heart? Why not any other human’s heart? I don’t understand this part either." He himself did not know the answer to this question.
A heavy silence ruled the hall.
Then the sound of quiet laughter was heard. Laughter that made the hair on the body stand up. The Dreadmaw Sovereign was laughing.
Its black eyes were fixed on Lian.
"Interesting. Truly interesting." The monster leaned forward a little, and its massive shadow fell on the ground.
And then, with a calm but terrifying tone, it said.
"I did not think such an interesting human could exist."

Then he knelt in front of the monster, lowered his head, and offered the heart with both hands.
"My lord."
The Dreadmaw Sovereign reached out its massive hand and took the heart.
For a moment, it held it in front of its face, then smelled it.
Its black eyes narrowed a little.
"A heart..." Its voice was like the roar of breaking ice.
"With very strong emotions." A terrifying smile formed on its face.
"Perhaps this one will work."
"I did my best, my lord.
I hope you are satisfied with the result." The village chief immediately bowed his head.
"We will see." The monster answered, and then its gaze slowly turned around the hall.
And stopped on Lian.
A feeling of danger immediately exploded throughout Lian’s being.
As if an ancient predator had chosen him.
The monster’s smile deepened.
"And you..." Its claw pointed toward Lian.
"You can be my new skin."
Lian’s eyes turned cold.
Now he understood almost everything, or at least a large part of the truth.
"Now I understand."
"What?" Seris felt like her brain was about to explode right now, and this boy still kept his calm?
Lian did not take his eyes off the monster.
"What has been happening here all this time.
These aren’t even real monsters." He then added, pointing to the village chief.
Seris frowned.
"What do you mean?" Seris frowned.
This old man and those bastards in the village that they killed were definitely monsters.
What did he mean they weren’t real monsters?
"They are parasites.
Parasites that can take over the bodies of other creatures."
Seris immediately answered.
"But we saw the villagers’ bodies.
They hadn’t taken over anyone’s body.
Their hearts had been removed."
Lian nodded.
"That’s right.
Because they have mutated." He thought about the monster corpses they had killed outside.
About the human hearts he had found inside the disgusting bodies of those creatures.
Everything now made sense.
"This is their new path of evolution.
The hearts have become their source of power.
They become one with the hearts of the creatures they hunt."
Seris remained silent.
She felt like this information was too much for her.
Lian continued.
"Body, abilities, talents, even skills.
They take everything from the heart’s owner." His eyes became playful.
"Probably in the past, they could only control bodies, but they could not use the real power of the victim.
Now they have found a new way.
A way that lets them steal everything."
Seris looked at the Dreadmaw Sovereign.
"So before the mutation... they were very weak?"
"Naturally." Lian answered.
"After all, they were only low-level normal monsters.
But by swallowing hearts, they mutated and became something completely different."
"Of course, I think it’s not just about stealing the abilities of the body’s owners.
Probably, they can also gain the power and skills of any human they kill and turn into their shape."
"When they possessed a body, they could neither use their own abilities nor use the abilities of that body."
"But when they swallowed the hearts, they no longer possess someone.
They can just turn into that shape, so they can even use all their own abilities."
"The shape they have now is probably something they feel more comfortable in."
"So that one is also one of these parasites?" Seris looked at the massive creature on the throne.
For the first time, Lian paused, then slowly shook his head.
"No.
The parasites are its children.
That one is different."
A short silence followed.
"This is its real body.
It has probably been looking for a way to get a human body for a long time while also keeping its own abilities and power, but it has not succeeded.
That is why it created these parasites."
"Like experiments.
Like tools, to find a way to achieve its goal."
"And it found a way.
The hearts.
With the help of hearts, instead of taking over a shell, it can turn into that shell and also keep its powers."
"Of course, it might want to completely take over a body and still keep its powers through the heart.
That is why it probably needs a special heart."
"But why?
Why would such a monster want a human body?" Seris still did not understand.
"I don’t know either." Lian said quietly, and continued.
"But I know it wants the hearts for transferring power.
To build a new shell.
A shell that can carry all its abilities."
His gaze fell on Aria’s heart.
"But why Aria’s heart?
Why not any other human’s heart?
I don’t understand this part either." He himself did not know the answer to this question.
A heavy silence ruled the hall.
Then the sound of quiet laughter was heard.
Laughter that made the hair on the body stand up.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign was laughing.
Its black eyes were fixed on Lian.
"Interesting.
Truly interesting." The monster leaned forward a little, and its massive shadow fell on the ground.
And then, with a calm but terrifying tone, it said.
"I did not think such an interesting human could exist."

chapters.title: Chapter 37: The Truth II
paragraphs: "Am I wrong?" Lian gave a cold smile and said.
"No." The monster said with a deep, cold voice, and its black eyes narrowed.
"A large part of what you said is correct."
The village chief lowered his head. Ryan also stood still, as if waiting for his master’s permission.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign raised Aria’s bloody heart, smelled it with strange pleasure, and then a terrifying smile appeared on its face.
"For years, I have been looking for a way to get a human body, but at the same time keep my powers."
"My children succeeded."
"But I... am much more powerful than them. Much more powerful." Its long nails scratched the heart.
"And to withstand my power, a normal heart is not enough."
"A powerful heart? What makes a heart powerful?" Seris frowned. From her perspective, all hearts were the same.
The monster laughed. A laugh that made the hair on the back of Seris’s neck stand up.
"Hearts do not become powerful with mana. They do not become powerful with energy. They do not become powerful through training." It put its hand on its own chest.
"Emotions. Emotions are what make a heart powerful."
"Love, hatred, sorrow, regret, hope."
"The stronger the emotions... the stronger the heart will be." Its eyes fell on Aria’s body.
"And this girl... had an extraordinary heart. Deep love for that boy, deep love for her sister, and in the final moments..." Its smile grew larger.
"When she was killed by the love of her life, a great hatred also formed in her heart."
"Love and hatred combined in one moment are a perfect mix."
Seris clenched her teeth. She felt disgust towards this bastard monster. This monster only saw humans as dolls and playthings for its own goals.
"So that is why you did not kill them." Lian, however, remained calm.
"That is correct." The Dreadmaw Sovereign’s eyes turned toward him.
"All this time, you have been cultivating Aria’s emotions. Friendship, attachment, love, hope, so that in the end, you could build a heart that can withstand your power." Lian continued.
"Exactly. And I succeeded." The monster laughed, and its laugh filled the cave.
"This heart can be the foundation of my evolution. The foundation of my rebirth."
Lian paused for a moment.
"Then why do you want a human body?" He then asked.
For the first time, real hatred appeared in the Dreadmaw Sovereign’s eyes. Hatred so deep that it made the air even colder.
"For revenge. For revenge against humans.
"Against those wild creatures that slaughtered my race." Its eyes shone with killing intent.
"I want to kill all of them. All of them. Entering the seven regions is not easy."
Lian paused in his mind.
Seven regions? Probably the remaining shelters of humanity. The last strongholds of humans. But if his guess was correct, then this ruined realm could be different from all the previous ones.
"But if I have a human body, entering there will be possible. And then..." Its smile grew wider.
"The slaughter will begin."
Lian said nothing. He had nothing to say. This monster had been planning for years just to find a way to take over a human body.
And this really made him understand how astonishing the intelligence of an Unholy is. Then how smart and terrifying are Demons and above them Supremes?
But now was not the time to think about that, because the monster had fixed its gaze on him again.
"And among all the humans I have seen, your body is the best option." It pointed its finger at Lian.
"At first, I wanted to use this trash." It pointed to Ryan.
"But you... have more talent, a stronger body, more potential."
"If I take your skin, taking revenge will become much easier."
Lian’s eyes turned cold, but instead of answering, he asked another question.
"When did your plan start?"
"Why do you want to know? What difference does it make to you?" The monster was quiet for a moment.
"At least before I die, let my curiosity be satisfied." Lian shrugged.
The monster laughed.
"You are an interesting human." Then it leaned back on its massive stone throne.
"About thirty years ago, humans came to this mountain. They wanted to live here, build homes, form a village." Its eyes narrowed.
"So I killed them. How could such lowly creatures dare to enter my sacred territory?"
Lian stayed silent. It was what he had guessed. So the real village people who were killed were the same people from Frostheart who had left because of the snow and blizzard.

"After that, my children took over their bodies. They lived in those bodies for years. And for years, I tried to find a way for my children to use both their own abilities and the abilities of those humans while inside their bodies."
"But I did not succeed. At least until I discovered the secret of hearts." Its claw tightened on Aria’s heart.
"Then we removed their hearts. My children absorbed those hearts and evolved. But none of them were enough for me."
"I did not want to just absorb that heart and turn into the shape of those lowly humans. I wanted to completely take over the body of my target and at the same time keep my powers."
"The best way was to find a heart that could withstand my power, place that heart inside the human body I wanted, and use the heart as a channel."
Then it continued.
"Only two hearts could withstand part of my power. One was a mother who died with her child. The other was a father who had to watch his child die."
Even Lian felt disgust for a moment. The monster spoke of these tragedies with pride, as if talking about a scientific achievement.
And this monster was more savage and bastardly than any other monster he had seen. It practically used humans as laboratory mice.
"Those two hearts could withstand a little of my power before being destroyed. And that was when I understood what I needed."
"You are a crazy monster." Seris stepped forward, her eyes burning with anger.
The monster just laughed.
"No. Just an idiot." Lian said mockingly.
All eyes turned to him. Even Seris.
Lian gave a mocking smile.

"Years of experiments, years of killing, years of wasting time, and you still haven’t been able to complete your first evolution. You tried for thirty years, and you are still here. What a pathetic failure."
For the first time, the smile disappeared from the Dreadmaw Sovereign’s face, and its black eyes froze.
The air suddenly became heavier. An invisible pressure filled the hall.
"Human." Its voice was no longer calm.
"You are too brave. This is not good."
"Enough talking."
"Now surrender and die, or I will kill you and take your corpse for myself."
Seris gripped her sword tighter. Lian took a quiet deep breath, and then without taking his eyes off the monster, he said,
"Sorry, but I have no plan to die here." He glanced at Seris.
"Get ready."
"I don’t think we can defeat it." Seris raised the Frostfang sword. Even though she really wanted to tear this monster apart, she was not stupid.
Lian nodded.
"We are not going to defeat it. We just need to take the key."
His gaze fixed on the golden key around the monster’s neck. The only way out. Their only hope.
Seris understood what he meant.
"Okay. Then we take the key." She said quietly.
At that moment, the Dreadmaw Sovereign looked at the village chief and Ryan. A cold smile appeared on its face.
"You two. Bring me the dead body of that boy."

chapters.title: Chapter 38: Revenge For Her Sister
paragraphs: "Bring me the dead body of that boy." Its endless black eyes were emotionless, as if all creatures were nothing but tools to achieve its goals.
Hearing the monster’s command, Ryan immediately bowed his head.
"Yes, my lord."
At the same time, the village chef also gave a cold smile.
"It is my honor."
The next moment, both moved. Ryan toward Lian, and the village elder toward Seris.
BOOM!
The ground under their feet cracked. Lian moved forward almost at the same time as Ryan, his eyes fixed on the floating notification in front of him.
He did not know how powerful Ryan was, but he felt no danger from him. Based on the aura and pressure he felt, Ryan should not be above level 13.
Compared to the monsters he had killed in Frostheart, Ryan was no longer a serious threat.
But what was dangerous was probably his fire element.
WOOSH!
Red flames erupted around Ryan’s hands. The frozen air of the hall became warm in an instant.
"For my lord, you must die!"
BANG!
His flaming fist came straight toward Lian’s face. But Lian just tilted his head slightly, and the fist passed by his face.
At that moment, his ice claw activated.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
The sharp sound of tearing echoed in the air, and blue claws emerged from his fingers.
Ryan’s eyes widened. It was too fast. Much faster than he remembered.
SLASH!
Three deep marks appeared on his chest. Blood sprayed around, and Ryan stepped back several meters.
His face twisted in pain.
"Impossible..." But Lian did not even give him a chance to breathe.
BANG!
The ground under Lian’s feet exploded, and in a fraction of a second, he appeared in front of Ryan. The ice claw moved from bottom to top.
SLASH!
Ryan’s skin and flesh tore like paper, and blood fell on the ground. Ryan screamed and released more flames.
A massive column of fire rushed toward Lian, but Lian walked straight into it.
His resistance was now at a level where such flames had no effect on him.
SLASH!
Another hit.
SLASH!
Another hit. In less than a few seconds, Ryan’s body was covered in wounds.
On the other side of the hall, Seris’s fight had also begun.
BANG!
The village chef’s fist collided with Seris’s sword. The shockwave shook the hall.
Seris frowned.
This old man’s physical power was truly unnatural. But even so, she was not very surprised. After all, this monster was level 20, and dealing with it would not be easy.
This was the first time she was fighting a level 20 monster. A monster that was practically one step away from its first evolution.
And she was lucky that this monster had not done its first evolution. If it had, she would have had no chance against it.
The first evolution is very important for monsters and Awakened. Because that is where the main difference in power between geniuses and normal people becomes clear.
Five-star classes would peak after their first evolution and shine like stars, while one-star classes would begin their downfall.
The same was true for monsters. They would finally form their second core and gain two sources of power.
Two power cores, two sources of power for monsters. And this matter was even more terrifying for Fallen monsters because they could form four cores!
Unholy ones could form 8 cores, and Demons could form 16 power cores. And Supremes? They could gain 28 cores just in their first evolution.
This was where the biggest reason for monster ranking and the superiority of higher ranks became clear.
The monster smiled, and suddenly his right hand turned black.
[Bone Breaker]
BANG!
His fist hit the ground, and hundreds of cracks appeared on the hall floor. Seris jumped back, but at that moment, the village chef raised his other hand.
[Blood Surge]
The blood that had spilled on the ground came alive. Like red snakes, they attacked Seris. Seris spun her sword.
WOOSH!
She cut all of them into pieces. But the third attack came immediately.
[Frenzied Burst]
The village elder’s muscles swelled. His speed suddenly doubled.
BANG!
His fist hit Seris’s stomach, and Seris stepped back several meters.
But that was all. She had also increased her resistance and would not take internal damage that easily. More importantly, her new armor was completely intact and could defend against such attacks.
She pressed her foot on the ground, raised the Frostfang sword, her eyes turned cold, and she suddenly disappeared.
SLASH!
The first wound appeared on the village chef’s shoulder.
SLASH!
The second wound.
SLASH!
The third wound.
The monster’s smile slowly faded, and for the first time, it understood that things were not going as it had expected.
"It seems you have improved a lot during this time." It said coldly. The first day this girl came to the village, she was not that powerful.
If it had finished her off that day, it would not have such trouble now. But even now, it did not think it would lose. In the presence of its god, it never lost.
Meanwhile, Ryan had fallen to his knees. His whole body was bloody. His breaths came out in gasps. Lian slowly walked toward him.
The ice claws were still extended from his hands. Ryan barely raised his head.
"I... for my lord..."
SLASH!
The ice claw tore his throat. The unfinished sentence remained, and his body fell to the ground.
But he was still alive. Still struggling. Killing an Awakened was not that simple.
Lian stared at him for a few moments, then turned his gaze to the corner of the hall.
To Alisa, the girl who was still kneeling beside her sister’s body. Her shoulders were shaking from crying. Her eyes were red.
Empty, broken, but deep inside, a burning hatred was blazing.
Lian looked at Ryan, then at Alisa. He could not let this girl stay like this.
"Do you want to do it yourself?" He said quietly.
Alisa raised her head. Her gaze fell on Ryan. On the same boy who was once everything to her sister. On the same boy who had pulled Aria’s heart out of her chest.
Her hands trembled. She struggled to stand up. Her steps were unsteady.
But she did not stop. She went to the sword that lay on the ground, bent down, and picked it up. Ryan lay half-dead on the ground, and his eyes slowly fell on her.
"Alisa..."
The girl said nothing. She just looked at him. Then...
SLASH!
She drove the sword into his stomach. Ryan’s eyes widened in pain, and blood spilled from his mouth.
The sword was pulled out.
But it was not over.
SLASH!
The second time.
SLASH!
The third time.
SLASH!
The fourth time.
Tears flowed down Alisa’s face, but her hand did not stop.
SLASH!
"Die, you bastard..."
SLASH!
SLASH!
"Die, you trash..."
SLASH!
"Die..." Her scream echoed through the entire hall.
"Die, you bastard!"
Blood had sprayed everywhere. Ryan no longer moved. But Alisa still raised and lowered the sword, as if she wanted to release all her pain, anger, and hatred with each strike.
And at the top of the hall... the Dreadmaw Sovereign silently watched this scene.
A calm and terrifying smile had formed on its face.

She pressed her foot on the ground, raised the Frostfang sword, her eyes turned cold, and she suddenly disappeared.
SLASH!
The first wound appeared on the village chef’s shoulder.
SLASH!
The second wound.
SLASH!
The third wound.
The monster’s smile slowly faded, and for the first time, it understood that things were not going as it had expected.
"It seems you have improved a lot during this time." It said coldly.
The first day this girl came to the village, she was not that powerful.
If it had finished her off that day, it would not have such trouble now.
But even now, it did not think it would lose.
In the presence of its god, it never lost.
Meanwhile, Ryan had fallen to his knees.
His whole body was bloody.
His breaths came out in gasps.
Lian slowly walked toward him.
The ice claws were still extended from his hands.
Ryan barely raised his head.
"I... for my lord..."
SLASH!
The ice claw tore his throat.
The unfinished sentence remained, and his body fell to the ground.
But he was still alive.
Still struggling.
Killing an Awakened was not that simple.
Lian stared at him for a few moments, then turned his gaze to the corner of the hall.
To Alisa, the girl who was still kneeling beside her sister’s body.
Her shoulders were shaking from crying.
Her eyes were red.
Empty, broken, but deep inside, a burning hatred was blazing.
Lian looked at Ryan, then at Alisa.
He could not let this girl stay like this.
"Do you want to do it yourself?" He said quietly.
Alisa raised her head.
Her gaze fell on Ryan.
On the same boy who was once everything to her sister.
On the same boy who had pulled Aria’s heart out of her chest.
Her hands trembled.
She struggled to stand up.
Her steps were unsteady.
But she did not stop.
She went to the sword that lay on the ground, bent down, and picked it up.
Ryan lay half-dead on the ground, and his eyes slowly fell on her.
"Alisa..."
The girl said nothing.
She just looked at him.
Then...
SLASH!
She drove the sword into his stomach.
Ryan’s eyes widened in pain, and blood spilled from his mouth.
The sword was pulled out.
But it was not over.
SLASH!
The second time.
SLASH!
The third time.
SLASH!
The fourth time.
Tears flowed down Alisa’s face, but her hand did not stop.
SLASH!
"Die, you bastard..."
SLASH!
SLASH!
"Die, you trash..."
SLASH!
"Die..." Her scream echoed through the entire hall.
"Die, you bastard!"
Blood had sprayed everywhere.
Ryan no longer moved.
But Alisa still raised and lowered the sword, as if she wanted to release all her pain, anger, and hatred with each strike.
And at the top of the hall... the Dreadmaw Sovereign silently watched this scene.
A calm and terrifying smile had formed on its face.

chapters.title: Chapter 39: Feeling Hopeless
paragraphs: The sound of the sword sinking into flesh still echoed in the stone hall of the cave.
Blood slowly flowed from Ryan’s body onto the ground and spread into the stone cracks.
Alisa stood in front of him. Her hands were trembling, and her tears were flowing down her face without stopping.
But her eyes no longer looked like they used to. Only hatred was waving in them.
Deep hatred. Hatred that had come from the depths of her broken heart. She pulled the sword out of Ryan’s stomach, and then the sword fell from her hand.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign also watched for a moment, as if watching an entertaining show.
Alisa could not stand anymore. She fell to her knees. The sword slipped from her fingers. She hid her face in her hands, and the sound of her crying echoed in the hall.
"Sister, I avenged you," she whispered to herself, and the look in her eyes calmed down a little.
At that moment, Lian and Seris’s attention moved away from the bodies. The village chief was also dead. Even though he was powerful, he had no chance against Seris from the beginning.
Both of them looked toward the massive stone throne, toward the real monster, toward the creature from which this whole nightmare had started.
The Dreadmaw Sovereign.
The monster sat quietly on the throne, as if it had only been watching a boring show all this time.
Its dark eyes slid over the bodies of Ryan and the village chief.
"I did not expect those two to be so worthless." It then said with indifference.
Its voice made the air around tremble.
"It is not their fault. We are too strong." A crooked smile appeared on its face.
The monster laughed. A heavy, deep laugh. A laugh that seemed to come from several different throats at the same time, and its sound echoed throughout the hall.
"Then why don’t you come yourself?" Lian then added.
Then the monster raised its finger in response. Just one finger. No spell was chanted, no magic circle appeared.
But suddenly, a red light formed at the tip of its finger, and a moment later...
BOOM!
A massive beam of energy split the hall. The ground melted, the stones vaporized, and the terrible pressure of the explosion covered everything.
Lian’s eye widened.
"Alisa!"
Without thinking, he jumped forward, grabbed the girl, and used all his power to dodge. At the same time, Seris also moved out of the attack’s path.
But even this was not enough. The shockwave reached them, and the explosion swallowed the hall.
Blood dripped from Lian’s face. He struggled to get up from the ground. His breathing was heavy. The entire left side of his face was burned.
And worse than everything, his left eye was gone. A bloody hole had taken its place.
His right arm was also hanging, almost useless.
A bit farther away... Seris had landed on one knee. Blood was flowing from her mouth. Her left leg was bent at an unnatural angle.
Several ribs were broken, but she was still alive.

And that was the most terrifying part of it. All this damage had come from just a simple finger gesture. Not from a final skill, not even from a serious attack. Just a finger gesture. For the first time, Lian felt his scalp tingle.
The distance between them and this monster was even greater than he had imagined.
Seris suddenly stood up. Blood was flowing on her chin, but her eyes were still cold.
"Damn it..." She raised the Frostfang sword, and mana erupted around her.
The air split, and an invisible wave moved toward the Dreadmaw. A heavy pressure settled on the monster’s body. But that was not the end.
[King’s Breaker]
All her remaining mana flowed into the sword, and the blade began to tremble. Then...
BOOM!
Seris shot forward like a released arrow. The sword hit the monster’s chest directly, and the sound of metal hitting metal echoed in the hall.
But no scratch was made. The monster did not even lower its head. It just moved its hand, like swatting a fly.
BANG!
Seris was thrown back like a cannonball and finally hit the cave wall with great force. The sound of bones breaking was heard.
She fell like a dead person. When she tried to move her muscles, she felt terrible pain. Pain so terrible that she could barely control her scream.
Lian frowned. This was no longer a fight. This was a one-sided slaughter. He put Alisa on the ground and then opened his status panel.
[Stat Points: 96]
His eyes stayed on the number. He had gotten this number naturally from the monsters he had killed in the village.
But even with all this number, he knew he had no chance of defeating the monster. But maybe he could at least get the key.
A moment later...
[+30 Speed]
And then he went to the skills.
[Steelhide]
[Storm Tyrant Fang]
Sparks of lightning appeared on his body. And then...
[Fallen Wolf Speed]
Activated. In an instant, he disappeared. Even the air around did not have time to react. Only a trace of lightning and snow remained in the hall.
A moment later, Lian appeared next to the stone throne. He was only a few centimeters away from the golden key. His hand reached forward.
But the monster had been watching him from the beginning, as if it had seen all his movements beforehand. Its massive hand came up and grabbed Lian’s neck.

Tight. Very tight. Lian’s remaining eye widened. He felt that his end had come. Just one more... if this monster applied pressure just a little more, his skull would be crushed, and nothing would remain of him.
"For such a weak insect, you talk too much."
A moment later...
BOOM!
His body was slammed to the ground. The entire floor of the hall collapsed, and blood erupted from his mouth.
"Oh, I think I have damaged my future body a bit too much, haven’t I?" The Dreadmaw’s voice was calm and mocking.
Lian struggled to get up. Every bone in his body hurt. He looked at Seris. Her condition was also terrible.
For the first time, a thought formed in his mind. Maybe they should run.
Maybe the key was not worth it. But if they ran, what then? If this monster evolved, what then? At that time, their chance of getting the key would become absolute zero.
Would it not be better to forget this key and look for another one? But what if the next key was months away?
That would mean they would have to live here for months?
And more importantly... would they even be allowed to run? This monster wanted his body. Under no circumstances would it let him escape.
His eyes narrowed, and then his gaze fell on the status panel.
Fragments, stat points, skills, and suddenly... a crazy idea formed in his mind.
He did not know if it would work, but if it succeeded, they could get the key.
A moment later, he appeared next to Seris. Seris was still on the ground, her whole face bloody.
"Are you okay?" Lian asked.
"What do you think?" Seris said with difficulty.
Lian looked at the monster.
"We have no chance of defeating it."
"Obviously." The girl agreed.
"But maybe we can take the key."
"How?" Seris frowned.
"That skill of yours... the one that puts pressure on monsters." Lian said quietly.
"It does not work on it." Seris said without hesitation. That skill had no effect on this monster. This monster was too powerful.
"Even one second would be enough."
Seris looked at him, but her answer was the same. Not even one second would work.
"Do you have fragments?"
"Yes."
"Then upgrade it. This is our only chance."
A few seconds of silence passed, and then Seris slowly nodded. They were going to die anyway. She had lost all hope of escape.
At least before dying, she would make one last attempt.
Lian turned back to the monster. This time, he gathered all his remaining power, and snow and ice coiled around his left hand.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
At the same time, blue lightning erupted around his arm.
[Storm Tyrant Fang]
But he knew this was not enough. So with the help of his talent, he made his ice claws even more powerful, and he started consuming mana much faster.
A massive pressure formed in the hall. The ground under his feet cracked, and then he charged forward with all his power.
His fist shot directly toward the monster’s face.
But...
The Dreadmaw Sovereign only smiled.
A calm, mocking smile. Just before impact, its hand came up and caught Lian’s fist. Completely stopped. No explosion happened.
No damage was done. All of Lian’s power was extinguished between the monster’s fingers.
The monster looked at him as if looking at a walking corpse. In its eyes, the game was over. It was time to kill this insect and then use its body as a shell.
"Now!" But Lian suddenly shouted.

chapters.title: Chapter 40: Berserk State
paragraphs: The Dreadmaw Sovereign’s mocking smile spread through the darkness of the hall. Its massive hand still held Lian’s fist inside its grip.
All the power Lian had gathered, all the mana he had spent, all the speed he had gained from stat points, all seemed useless.
The monster did not even frown. Not a scratch had been made on its skin.
The Dreadmaw’s black eyes stayed fixed on Lian’s bloody face. Then slowly, very slowly... it started to squeeze his fist.
CRACK!
The sound of bones crushing echoed in the hall. The veins on Lian’s neck bulged. A savage pain ran from his fingers to his shoulder.
But he did not even scream. He just clenched his teeth. Blood flowed from the corner of his mouth.
The Dreadmaw smiled.
"Did you really think you could wound me?"
And a moment later...
BOOM!
Its hand came down. Lian’s body was slammed to the ground like a red meteor. The stones on the floor exploded, and cracks spread for dozens of meters.
The shockwave shook the entire cave. Blood sprayed from Lian’s mouth. For a few moments, he could not even breathe.
His whole body screamed in pain.
But at that moment, on the other side of the hall, Seris was quietly watching everything that was happening. Seeing that her time was coming, she got ready.
A blue light formed around her body, and a panel appeared in front of her eyes.
[Upgrade Complete]
[King’s Pressure → Tyrant’s Fall (+)]
[Rank: Great]
[Effect: Applies overwhelming pressure to enemies. Reduces resistance. Duration increases against targets with similar levels. Against powerful targets, effect lasts only moments.]
Blue light flowed into the Frostfang sword. She was ready, just waiting for the signal to activate her skill.

In the center of the hall, Lian struggled out of the massive crater. His whole body was covered in blood. His arm was almost destroyed. Of course, the word "almost" was wrong; that arm was no longer usable.
His breathing had become heavy, but he still stood. He still had not fallen. He was still alive. That itself was a miracle—that he had managed to stay alive against such a monster.
Of course, one of the main reasons he was still alive was that the monster was playing with them like toys instead of killing them.
All this time, the monster had not even gotten up from its spot and had not used any skill. But it had almost killed both of them.
The Dreadmaw looked at him and laughed.
A quiet laugh that filled the entire cave. But suddenly, a shout was heard.
"Now!"
Seris raised her sword. All her remaining mana was released. A blue light covered the hall.
"Tyrant’s Fall!
WHOOOOM!
It was as if the whole world became heavy for a moment. The air around collapsed. The ground shook. The cave walls cracked. For the first time, the Dreadmaw’s smile disappeared.
Its eyes narrowed. Its body stopped for a fraction of a second. Just one second. Just one short moment. But that was enough.
Lian moved. Not toward the key. Not toward the monster’s neck. Not toward the escape route. But straight toward the heart. Aria’s heart.
The heart that was still in the Dreadmaw’s hand. The heart it had been planning for all these years.
The heart that was supposed to be the foundation of its evolution. And at that moment, for the first time, fear appeared on the monster’s face.
"No!" Its roar shook the entire cave.
"Human!" Its red eyes widened.
"Stay away!"
And at that moment, Lian became sure. His guess was right. The monster’s entire plan was built on that heart. Maybe he could not kill this monster.
True, he could not inflict physical damage on this monster. But at least he would make that bastard suffer.
In the middle of his charge, the status panel appeared again.
[Fragments: 71]
Their number was far beyond what he had expected. He had to look at his notifications to understand what was happening.
And then he saw that the reason was killing the Mutated ones. The Mutated were a new race, and for each Mutated he had killed, he had gained 2 Fragments.
This was probably the reward for helping The Will add a completely new race to its data. If he had known this would happen, he would have killed the rest of the Mutated himself.
Lian chose without hesitation.
[Upgrade Storm Tyrant Fang?]
[Required: 16 Fragments]
[Yes / No]
"Yes."
WHOOOOM!
Blue lightning exploded around his body, and a new notification appeared.
[Storm Tyrant Fang → Thunder Calamity]
[Rank: Divine]
[Description: The destructive power of lightning is greatly increased, and each spark can create a massive explosion. Lightning can be summoned to destroy targets. Consumes 0.5 mana per minute.]
New power flowed through his veins. He felt stronger. He could feel that the power of the lightning surrounding his body had at least tripled.
And more importantly, he realized that this was the peak of this skill. It could no longer be upgraded.
But that did not matter. He released all of it.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
[Thunder Calamity]
Ice and lightning gathered into one fist. Lian’s hand turned into a monster of ice and electricity. The pressure from it caused the surrounding stones to collapse.
Blood was flowing from his mouth. His body was on the verge of collapse, but he moved forward. Faster and faster until his fist hit the heart.
BANG!
A massive explosion occurred.
Blue and white light swallowed the entire hall. The shockwave threw everyone back. The cave cracked. And then... the sound of something breaking was heard.
CRAAAAACK!
Aria’s heart shattered inside the Dreadmaw’s grip. With a little look, it was clear that even the monster’s hand had finally been damaged.
Silence.
For a moment, everything was quiet.
Then a terrible roar came from the monster’s throat. A roar that sounded like nothing else. As if thousands of creatures were screaming at the same time.
The cave shook.
Cracks appeared on the Dreadmaw’s red skin. Black veins appeared on its body. A red light shone from the cracks.
A system notification appeared.
[Warning]
[Dreadmaw Sovereign has entered Berserk State]
Lian lay on the ground. His body could no longer move. On the other side of the hall... Seris barely stood on her feet. She had leaned her sword on the ground to keep from falling.
Alisa was still sitting by the wall. Her eyes were wide with terror. She had lost all hope of surviving.
She knew that today would be the day she died. She looked at her sister’s body, nothing left of her, destroyed during the exchange of blows.
"Sister... I will join you soon."
And in front of them... the Dreadmaw Sovereign slowly raised its head.
Its skin was still cracking. Black blood oozed from the cracks in its body. Its eyes were no longer black. They had become completely red.
Redder than blood. Redder than fire. It looked slowly at Lian, then at Seris.
And finally, a terrifying smile appeared on its face. A smile that opened its mouth almost to its ears.
"I..." The entire cave shook.
"Will..." Stone pillars collapsed one after another.
"Tear you apart."

True, he could not inflict physical damage on this monster.
But at least he would make that bastard suffer.
In the middle of his charge, the status panel appeared again.
[Fragments: 71]
Their number was far beyond what he had expected.
He had to look at his notifications to understand what was happening.
And then he saw that the reason was killing the Mutated ones.
The Mutated were a new race, and for each Mutated he had killed, he had gained 2 Fragments.
This was probably the reward for helping The Will add a completely new race to its data.
If he had known this would happen, he would have killed the rest of the Mutated himself.
Lian chose without hesitation.
[Upgrade Storm Tyrant Fang?]
[Required: 16 Fragments]
[Yes / No]
"Yes."
WHOOOOM!
Blue lightning exploded around his body, and a new notification appeared.
[Storm Tyrant Fang → Thunder Calamity]
[Rank: Divine]
[Description: The destructive power of lightning is greatly increased, and each spark can create a massive explosion.
Lightning can be summoned to destroy targets.
Consumes 0.5 mana per minute.]
New power flowed through his veins.
He felt stronger.
He could feel that the power of the lightning surrounding his body had at least tripled.
And more importantly, he realized that this was the peak of this skill.
It could no longer be upgraded.
But that did not matter.
He released all of it.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
[Thunder Calamity]
Ice and lightning gathered into one fist.
Lian’s hand turned into a monster of ice and electricity.
The pressure from it caused the surrounding stones to collapse.
Blood was flowing from his mouth.
His body was on the verge of collapse, but he moved forward.
Faster and faster until his fist hit the heart.
BANG!
A massive explosion occurred.
Blue and white light swallowed the entire hall.
The shockwave threw everyone back.
The cave cracked.
And then... the sound of something breaking was heard.
CRAAAAACK!
Aria’s heart shattered inside the Dreadmaw’s grip.
With a little look, it was clear that even the monster’s hand had finally been damaged.
Silence.
For a moment, everything was quiet.
Then a terrible roar came from the monster’s throat.
A roar that sounded like nothing else.
As if thousands of creatures were screaming at the same time.
The cave shook.
Cracks appeared on the Dreadmaw’s red skin.
Black veins appeared on its body.
A red light shone from the cracks.
A system notification appeared.
[Warning]
[Dreadmaw Sovereign has entered Berserk State]
Lian lay on the ground.
His body could no longer move.
On the other side of the hall...
Seris barely stood on her feet.
She had leaned her sword on the ground to keep from falling.
Alisa was still sitting by the wall.
Her eyes were wide with terror.
She had lost all hope of surviving.
She knew that today would be the day she died.
She looked at her sister’s body, nothing left of her, destroyed during the exchange of blows.
"Sister...
I will join you soon."
And in front of them... the Dreadmaw Sovereign slowly raised its head.
Its skin was still cracking.
Black blood oozed from the cracks in its body.
Its eyes were no longer black.
They had become completely red.
Redder than blood.
Redder than fire.
It looked slowly at Lian, then at Seris.
And finally, a terrifying smile appeared on its face.
A smile that opened its mouth almost to its ears.
"I..." The entire cave shook.
"Will..." Stone pillars collapsed one after another.
"Tear you apart."

chapters.title: Chapter 41: Eternal Frozen Apocalypse
paragraphs: The monster’s roar echoed through the cave like a death bell.
"I... will tear you apart."
At that moment, the entire atmosphere of the cave changed.
If a few seconds ago the Dreadmaw Sovereign seemed like a calm and confident creature, now it looked like the embodiment of rage and madness.
Black cracks spread across its red skin. Traces of dark energy flowed through those fissures.
The ceiling of the cave began to shake. Massive stones fell one after another. The air around became heavier and heavier.
It was truly angry. Angrier than anything. The plan it had worked on for years. The heart it had waited years to nurture.
All its efforts to finally obtain a human body. All its efforts for the day it could take revenge for its race.
And all the efforts it had made to start its evolution were ruined because of these lowly humans.
Lian felt his breathing become hard. As if an entire mountain had been placed on his shoulders.
Even Seris, for the first time since they entered this realm, fell to one knee on the ground. Cold sweat was on her forehead. Her eyes were locked on the monster.
Then the Dreadmaw disappeared. So fast that it seemed like it was never there. Lian’s eyes widened. His instincts screamed wildly.
But it was too late.
BOOM!
The monster’s massive fist hit him directly in the stomach. The sound of the explosion echoed through the hall. Lian felt all his internal organs crush.
His body shot back like a cannonball. The ground under him split. Stones shattered. He was dragged dozens of meters on the ground, finally hitting a massive stone pillar.
The sound of breaking bones echoed in the cave. Blood sprayed from his mouth. The ribs on his left side were almost completely crushed.
But before he could even get up...
BOOM!
Seris also charged at the monster. She understood that if she did not do something now, Lian would certainly die.
The Frostfang sword flashed in the air. But the Dreadmaw did not even look at her. It just flicked the back of its hand.
That was it.
A hit that meant nothing to it sent Seris flying like a rag doll. The young girl hit the cave wall directly.
The sound of more bones breaking was heard. The sword fell from her hand. Blood sprayed on the stones.
The Dreadmaw calmly walked toward Lian.
Its steps were slow, but each step made the cave shake, as if an ancient king was walking through its domain.
It stopped in front of Lian, then placed its massive foot on his chest.
CRACK!
The sound of bones crushing was heard. Lian coughed up blood, but his gaze was still fixed on the monster’s neck.
On the key.
Only the key.
The Dreadmaw smiled.
"No human has ever made me this angry. Even those savages who killed my race. But congratulations, you succeeded."
"Is this all you had?" It pressed its foot harder.
"This pathetic creature ruined my thirty-year plan?"
Blood flowed from the corner of Lian’s mouth, but a faint smile appeared on his face. This made a frown appear on the monster’s face.
On the other side of the hall, Seris was breathing with difficulty. Her whole body screamed in pain, but she raised her hand.
The system panel appeared, and without any hesitation, she spent all her remaining fragments.
A silver light formed around her body.
[Tyrant’s Fall upgraded]
[Sovereign’s Judgment (+)]
[Rank: Divine]
Not just one upgrade, but two upgrades! All her fragments were used, but it did not matter. Now it was a matter of life and death.
If she did nothing, both of them would die.
A royal aura formed around her body. Even the Dreadmaw turned its gaze toward her for a moment.
But at that same time, Lian also opened his panel. His eyes fixed on the Frozen Cataclysm skill.
There was no hesitation.
[Are you sure you want to upgrade Frozen Cataclysm?]
[Confirmed. 20 Fragments used.]
[Frozen Cataclysm upgraded]
But Lian did not stop there. He immediately clicked on the next upgrade. One upgrade was not enough. He had to upgrade it again so the skill could at least inflict damage on this bastard monster.
[35 Fragments used]
[Fragments: 0]
[Eternal Frozen Apocalypse]
[Rank: Divine]
[Description: An apocalypse of snow and blizzard descends, covering a radius of one kilometer and freezing everything. The more mana used, the stronger it will be.]
Still not enough. He looked at his stat points.
[Stat Points: 66]
Just a few seconds of silence, then without any pause, he put them all into Mana. Now he only needed Mana to use this skill at full power.
Maybe then they would have a chance.
A massive energy flowed through his body. For the first time, the Dreadmaw frowned.
It sensed danger. Not from power, but from something else. From determination. From madness. From the fact that these two humans had still not given up.
Why? Why could it still see hope in their eyes? What else did they have that they had not used yet?
Seris struggled to stand. Her whole body was soaked in blood, but she picked up her sword again.
Then she shouted.
"Right now!"
The entire cave exploded.
Sovereign’s Judgment activated.
Thousands of cracks appeared on the ground. An invisible pressure descended from the sky onto the monster’s body.
And the Dreadmaw stopped. Just one second. Again, one second. But in this second, unlike the previous time, the monster could not even move its eyes or hold its thoughts.
It was as if time had completely stopped for it for one second.
But for Lian, that was enough. His eyes shone, and all his remaining mana erupted.
[Eternal Frozen Apocalypse]
[Thunder Calamity]
Both activated at the same time.
Ice and lightning energy exploded around his body. His skin began to crack. His veins tore one after another. Blood burst from his entire body.
Suddenly, the entire cave began to freeze. A terrifying blizzard covered everything.
Everything froze. Even the monster’s entire body was suddenly covered in ice. Seeing the situation, Seris dragged herself toward where Lian was to stay safe.
Seeing this, Alisa also understood and ran toward them.
And the ice covered the entire cave, then spread further to cover the whole mountain.
Lian’s body could no longer handle this amount of force, but he still did not stop. He charged straight at the Dreadmaw.
For the key. This was the only chance to get that damn key.
At that moment, the monster realized his real target and frowned deeply. It moved its body to break free from the ice.
But it was too late. Lian’s ice claw landed on the golden chain.
CRAAAAACK!
The sound of metal tearing echoed in the hall. The chain broke. The key was freed.
At that same moment, the monster also broke free from the ice, and the Dreadmaw’s fist hit Lian’s body.
A massive explosion shook the hall. Almost all the bones in his body were crushed. Nothing remained. His body was thrown into the distance like a bloody meteor.
It passed through pillars, broke through several stone walls, and finally fell to the ground.
The force of the fist was so strong that the ice covering the hall cracked.
The golden key shone in Lian’s bloody hand. A heavy silence ruled over the cave. Seris had fallen to one knee, unable even to stand.
Alisa was still where Lian had been. Her face had no color. The terrible cold made her whole body shake, and her lips had turned black.
And in the middle of that destruction... the Dreadmaw slowly raised its hand to its neck.
Nothing was there. The key was gone. It stayed motionless for a few seconds, then let out a roar that shook the entire mountain.
Stones collapsed. Walls cracked. The roar caused the ice to crumble, and the air around trembled from its fury.
Its red eyes locked onto Lian. They darkened with hatred. Hatred that seemed born from thirty years of waiting and failure.
Its voice echoed through the hall like the howl of a creature from hell.
"Give me back my key."
And while Lian lay half-dead on the ground with the key clutched in his fist...

chapters.title: Chapter 42: Out Of Hell
paragraphs: The roar of the Dreadmaw Sovereign still echoed through the cave.
"Give me back... my key." His voice no longer sounded like a living creature. It sounded more like a mountain that was collapsing.
All the walls of the cave were shaking. Massive stones were breaking off from the ceiling and falling one after another.
If it were not for the ice created by Lian’s skill acting as a protective layer for the cave, the whole cave would have collapsed.
His red eyes were locked on Lian, on the key that was still between his bloody fingers.
That key was very important to him. He did not know what the key was, but he knew that it attracted all the energy and acted like an endless source for his core.
As long as he had that key, his core would never run out of mana.
But he did not dare to take it by force. He was afraid this damned human would suddenly destroy it.
But Lian could no longer even move a finger. All his mana was empty. All the bones in his body were crushed.
The only thing that had kept him alive was a stubborn will that miraculously kept him from dying.
A few meters away, Seris had fallen to one knee. Her sword lay next to her, and her breaths were broken.

Even raising her head had become difficult for her. Between them, Alisa was still alive and perhaps in the best condition. But even she was dying from the cold. She was not an Awakened, and her resistance to cold was very low.
And now she was lying on the ice, and the cracked ice surrounded her. If she had not gone toward Lian at the last moment, she would have frozen too.
She crawled on the ground with trembling hands. Each movement caused pain to explode in her entire body. Tears and blood mixed on her cheeks.
Her knees dragged on the broken ice, but she did not stop. She crawled toward Lian, toward the key, toward the only hope remaining.
She did not know what the key was, but she knew that Lian had done everything to get it, and the monster wanted it too.
Maybe... just maybe... the key was the way out.
Luckily, she was not far from Lian. Before the monster could do anything, she finally reached him. Her trembling hands reached out and pulled the golden key from between Lian’s bloody fingers.
At that moment, a strange silence ruled the cave. The Dreadmaw looked at the key.
For the first time, something like worry appeared in its eyes.
"What do you want to do with that key?"
Alisa said nothing. She just looked at him with hatred.
The monster stepped forward.
"Give it back. If you give it back right now..."
It took a second step.
"I will let you live."
Lian, who was half-conscious, opened his eyes a little when he heard that. Even Seris noticed. This was the first time. The first time this creature was making an offer.
The first time it was begging for something. And that showed how important that key was to it.
Alisa barely raised her head. Her eyes were still red from crying, but she was no longer that scared, quiet girl. Something inside her had broken, and something much darker had taken its place.
She stared at the monster.
"You... are responsible for my sister’s death." Then she said with a rough, trembling voice.
Her hands tightened around the key.
"Sooner or later..." Tears flowed from her eyes.
"I will kill you with my own hands.
Then suddenly, a panel appeared in front of her eyes.
[Golden Exit Key Obtained]
[Would you like to activate it?]
[YES] [NO]
Alisa looked at the panel in disbelief. So this key was the way out?
She did not hesitate even for a moment. Her hand landed on the first option.
YES.
And suddenly, the key exploded. Golden light filled the entire cave, and a blinding shine swallowed everything.
For the first time, the Dreadmaw was truly terrified.
Its eyes widened.
"No!"
Its scream shook the entire mountain. It charged forward at full speed. The frozen ground under its feet shattered. Its claws reached toward Alisa.
But it was too late. Space split open right in front of the three. A massive crack of golden light, like a wound between two worlds. A strong pull came out of it.
Everyone was pulled toward the crack.
Lian’s half-dead body lifted off the ground. Seris was also lifted off the ground. Alisa was the last.
The Dreadmaw screamed.
"Come back!"
Its hand almost reached them, but the crack was faster. All three disappeared into the light. At that moment, the crack closed.
Silence took over the space. For a few seconds of absolute silence, the Dreadmaw stood motionless.
It looked at the empty space in front of it. At where the crack had been. At its own empty neck. At the destroyed heart. At the plan it had spent thirty years on.
And now it had also lost the endless energy source.
Then the mountain exploded. A terrible roar came from its mouth. The pillars of the cave collapsed. The walls shattered.
The ceiling began to fall. The whole mountain was shaking as if the apocalypse had come.
At the same time, in another world, the Academy.
In the student dorm, silence ruled. Kain was sitting on his bed, a phone in his hand. His face looked tired.
"Still no news from him?" A girl’s voice came from the other end of the call.
"No." Kain sighed.
Suddenly, silence filled the space until...
"What if he is dead?"
The other end of the line went quiet.
"He had no power. He had no chance of surviving inside the ruined realm." Kain continued.
"Shut your mouth!" Suddenly, the girl’s voice rose.
"Don’t talk about his death again. He must be fine." But even the girl herself did not believe her words.
"You know he is probably dead." Kain lowered his head.
Silence.
Then the sound of sobbing was heard from the phone.
"Damn me... that night I was happy because of the new realm’s appearance." He also sighed and clenched his fist.
"While Lian was summoned as one of the sacrifices."
"I should not have been cold with him that day... I wish I had talked to him..." The girl said with a broken voice.
"I wish I had told him I forgive him..."
And at that moment, golden light appeared in the room. Kain froze.
Space split open, right in the middle of the dorm.
His eyes widened.
"What... happened?" The girl on the phone noticed that something was wrong.
The crack opened wider, and suddenly a body was thrown out of it.
BOOM!
The body landed directly on the bed.
Kain looked and then froze. His mind did not accept it. He could not accept it. His face lost its color.
"Lian...?"
The bloody body on the bed moved a little. One of his eyes was gone. His clothes were torn to pieces. His whole body was soaked in blood.
He looked like someone who had been pulled out of hell.
The girl on the phone shouted.
"What happened?!"
Kain stared in disbelief.
"Lian is back!" Then he shouted.
And he ended the call. Without even a second of delay, he ran to the door. He had to get help.
Immediately.
At that moment, Lian barely opened his eyes. His gaze fell on the ceiling of the room.
It was not stone, not darkness, not the smell of blood. It was the familiar ceiling of the dorm.
Finally...
A very faint smile appeared on his lips.
And with his last bit of consciousness, he whispered.
"So... I finally got out of that hell..." Then his eyes slowly closed, and everything faded into darkness.
