Naturally, that was Lian.
In a normal situation, only his class level needed to be measured, and based on that, he would be sent to an elite or normal class.
But he had said he did not want to announce his class level, which is not illegal.
It does happen that Awakened want to hide their class rank.
And on the other hand, the professor wanted to personally evaluate his abilities because he felt that Lian was hiding many things.
A gentle wind blew through the stone walls around the field, moving Lian’s hair.
On the other side of the field, Professor Aldric Voss stood with his hands locked behind his back.
Several other professors were also present on the upper platforms.
Even a few curious students had gathered.
The news of the return of the only survivor of the tenth Ruined Realm had spread very quickly through the Academy.
Everyone wanted to see what abilities this first-year student, who had suddenly gone from a normal Analyzer to an Awakened, really had.
Among the crowd, two young boys were also present.
Both were members of Roderick’s group.
As someone with a four-star class, he was naturally considered somewhat of a leader among the first-years, with many subordinates.
When their gaze fell on Lian, they smirked.
"Isn’t that the same guy?" One of them said.
The other laughed.
"Yeah.
The famous talentless one who used to be Lady Elena’s fiancé."
But their words did not reach Lian, and even if they did, he would not care.
After what he had seen in the ruined realm, these people were not even worth paying attention to.
Aldric stepped forward.
"First test." He raised his hand.
A few moments later, a massive pillar rose from the ground.
A black pillar, with thousands of magical patterns carved on its surface.
Several students held their breath when they saw it.
"That’s a professional-level power measurement pillar..."
"Why are they using that for a first-year?"
"Are you kidding?
That device was made for real hunters."
"Gather all your power into one strike." Aldric said, ignoring the whispers.
"And don’t worry.
There are no limits."
Lian looked at the pillar.
He now understood why this man had not let them use the normal power meter for him.
Considering his current physical strength could match a level 20, it would not be wrong to say that the normal device might not handle his power.
But how much power should he show here?
All of it?
Power equal to a level 20 Awakened?
He shook his head and rejected that idea.
But he did not want to play the weak role either and hide his power completely.
Then he quietly clenched his fist.
The muscles in his arm tightened.
He took a deep breath.
And suddenly, he threw his fist forward.
BOOM!
The sound of an explosion echoed through the field.
The air around trembled for a moment.
The black pillar shook, and numbers lit up on its surface.
The number stopped.
Silence.
For a few seconds, no one spoke.
"Impossible..." One of the professors muttered.
The students stared at the pillar in disbelief.
The average power of first-year students was usually less than a thousand.
But Lian... had recorded more than double that.
One of Roderick’s men frowned.
"It’s just raw power.
Raw power isn’t always important."
His friend nodded.
"Exactly.
Maybe his class gives him high raw power.
That doesn’t mean anything." But even he did not sound very sure.
A fist power of 2000 was very high.
Aldric said nothing, as if he had at least expected this much.
He just kept his gaze on Lian.
"Second test."
With a movement of his finger, dozens of metal orbs appeared in the air.
Then their number increased.
Twenty.
Thirty.
Forty.
Fifty.
The orbs spread across the entire field.
"Destroy the targets.
Time: thirty seconds."
At that moment, the countdown began.
Three.
Two.
One.
Start.
At the moment it started, Lian’s body vanished.
The students only saw a gray shadow moving across the field.
BANG!
BANG!
BANG!
The orbs exploded one after another.
There was no pause.
No unnecessary movement.
Everything was precise and deadly.
He did not even use any skills because there was no need.
Twenty seconds later...
The last orb exploded.
Aldric looked at the results.
Forty-seven out of fifty targets.
A whisper spread through the crowd.
"Forty-seven?!"
"The first-year record was twenty-one!"
"This is insane!"
"The device must be broken." One of Roderick’s men said angrily.
But what could be wrong with this test?
This was a test that measured speed, and Lian’s speed was higher than all first-years.
First raw power, and now speed!
Both were at least double the records of first-years.
Silence.
Aldric slowly turned his head and his gaze fell on Roderick’s subordinate, as if the annoying sounds were bothering him.
That was it.
But the student’s face immediately lost its color.
He felt as if a mountain had been placed on his shoulders.
A few seconds later, he lowered his head and said nothing more.
The third test began.
This time, the ground of the field shook.
A metal creature rose from the earth.
A golem over three meters tall.
A body covered in black steel and red eyes.
Its power level was 12!
Several students unconsciously stepped back.
This was a level 12 golem!
For all of them, such a creature was beyond their reach and abilities.
Only second-years had the ability to defeat such a golem.
"Final test.
Real combat." Aldric said.
The golem roared and charged at Lian.
The ground under its feet cracked.
But Lian just looked at it.
Honestly, he felt like laughing that he had to fight such a weak thing, especially after all those battles inside the ruined realm.
Hearing his laugh, Aldric frowned, and the other students looked at him as if they were looking at a madman.
"Did this guy go crazy from fear of the golem?" The students whispered.
At that moment, the golem brought down its fist.
But Lian disappeared and appeared behind it.
[Glacial Reaper Claw] activated.
His right hand was covered in blue ice, and he struck.
CRACK!
Ice cracks covered the golem’s entire body.
A second later, the upper half of the golem exploded.
Metal fragments scattered in the air.
The battle was over.
In less than ten seconds.
No one spoke.
Everyone just stared at the field, at the remains of the golem, and at the eighteen-year-old boy standing calmly in the middle.
"Is this really a first-year?" One of Roderick’s men muttered.
They did not even think their leader could defeat this golem that fast.
No first-year could!
Even among second-years, only the best of the best had such ability.
His friend had no answer.
Aldric slowly walked toward Lian and studied him for a few moments.
"Now I understand why you came back alive." He then said.
Lian said nothing.
But Aldric continued.
"And that makes me even more suspicious of your story." His eyes narrowed.
"Such power does not match the story of a normal guardian.
A normal monster should not have been able to inflict those injuries."
For a moment, silence fell.
Lian preferred not to say anything, but he was sure that this man was not going to leave him alone anytime soon.
He would probably cause trouble until he fully understood what had happened in that realm.
"There is something else." Aldric then said.
Everyone fell silent.
His tone had suddenly become more serious.
"At the same time as the tenth Ruined Realm appeared, one of the country’s border cities fell."
A murmur spread among the students.
Several people lost color.
This was not news that would be heard on the news, because the government controls the narratives to keep people from panicking.
Aldric continued.
"We moved a large part of the population to shelters.
Parts of the city have also been secured again."
"But hundreds of monsters are still present in that area.
Fortunately, most of them are of lower ranks."
Then his gaze fixed on Lian.
"I am forming an elite team of Academy students.
Their mission will be to clear the remaining monsters and assist local forces."
Several students looked at each other with excitement.
For many of them, this would be their first real mission.
But Aldric’s next sentence surprised everyone.
"And you will be on that team."
Many eyes turned toward Lian.
Some were jealous, some were shocked, and some did not believe it.
Because to join such a team, students certainly had to have achieved many accomplishments to qualify.
And most likely, first-years would not even have the right to join.
But this boy had earned the right to join that mission so easily.
But Aldric was completely serious.
"We move in one week.
Be ready by then."
Then without further explanation, he turned and started walking away.
The wind blew across the field, and Lian silently watched the professor’s back.
His first official mission as an Awakened and a first-year at the National Academy of Awakened.
And this time... his enemies were not monsters inside the ruined realm, but monsters that had found their way into the real world.
Of course, there was no difference between them.
And somewhere deep in his mind... he felt that this mission would be much more complicated than it seemed.

chapters.title: Chapter 49: The Elite Classroom
paragraphs: The news of Lian’s test spread through the Academy much faster than he himself had expected.
In less than a few hours, almost all first-year students had heard his name. The talentless boy who had suddenly returned from the tenth Ruined Realm.
The talentless boy who was now considered a level ten Awakened. And such a thing was strange enough to shake the entire Academy.
The sun was slowly setting behind the Academy’s tall buildings.
The sky had turned a dark orange. Lian was walking through the main Academy grounds when suddenly a familiar voice came from behind him.
"Level ten?!"
Lian did not even need to turn around to know who the voice belonged to. It was Kain. When he turned, he saw his friend staring at him with wide eyes.
As if his mind still could not accept the truth.
"You were gone for only a week!"
"Only a week!"
"I am still stuck at level three!" Kain messed up his hair.
"This does not make any sense!"
"Don’t be jealous. It is not that strange." Lian gave a short laugh.
"No, don’t get me wrong." Kain pointed at him with his finger.
"You are taking this too calmly. Level ten means you are stronger than most first-year students! In fact, stronger than all current first-years!"
"Even some second-years have not reached level ten yet!"
Lian said nothing. In fact, he knew better than anyone what price he had paid to reach this power.
Reaching level 10 was not easy, and he knew that now that he had reached this level, his position would be among the best students at the Academy.
But it would not be easy either. The National Academy of Awakened had thousands of students, and he might find many rivals among them.
A few minutes later, Seraphina also arrived. The Vice President of the Student Council. The black-haired girl who these days was almost always busy with Academy work. She was a second-year student.
But as soon as she reached Lian, her steps slowed. She just looked at Lian for a few seconds.
A long look. A strange look.
"Were you really there for only a week?" She finally said.
Lian was silent.
"I’m serious. Since you came back... you’ve changed." Seraphina frowned a little.
"Changed?" Kain asked with surprise.
Seraphina quietly nodded.
"Yes. Before, when you looked at him, you just saw a normal boy who acted somewhat withdrawn."
"But now..." She did not finish her sentence.
Because she herself did not know how to explain it. Lian seemed to have suddenly grown several years older.
Not in appearance, but in his gaze, in his silence, and in the calmness that now existed within him. Even from a distance, she could feel absolute confidence from Lian.
Were these changes because he had become an Awakened? Or because of something else he had experienced in the ruined realm?
"Anyone who becomes that famous overnight naturally changes." Lian just gave a faint smile.
"I guess you are right. You are now level 10. Higher than all first-years and higher than half of the second-years as well." Seraphina nodded.
"Did you come to see me just to say that?"
"What else were you expecting?" She smirked and said with sarcasm.
"I thought maybe you came to check on me." Lian shrugged, which made Seraphina a little shy, and her face suddenly turned red.
But when she noticed Lian and Kain laughing, her face immediately turned cold.
"Hmph! Enough laziness. It is clear you are fully recovered! If you don’t attend classes from tomorrow, I will report you!" And without looking at them, she turned to leave.

She had just come to check on Lian and spend some time with him, but this bastard dared to laugh at her! Yes, she had forgiven him, but she needed to teach him a lesson so he would not dare to laugh at the Vice President of the Student Council.
"She seems angry again." Kain continued laughing.
"Ah, I can smell trouble." Lian sighed and walked toward his dorm.
"Hey! Wait for me!"
It did not take long for night to fall. The news had spread like fire throughout the Academy dorms.
In every hallway, in every room, the name Lian Vonhelm was heard.
"Did you hear he found a legendary treasure?"
"Nonsense. He was already awakened and just hid it."
"So you are saying he has been an Awakened for a long time and was getting stronger secretly? Then why was he hiding it?"
"Who knows? Maybe for revenge?"
Rumors were made one after another, and none were close to the truth.
That night.
For the first time in a long while, Lian was going to have a good night’s sleep. He lay on his dorm bed.
The room was quiet.
There was no sound of monster roars, no smell of blood and death, and no screams.
Just silence.
And he quietly closed his eyes. Tomorrow he had to go to his first class, and he needed to rest.
The next morning, after waking up, he checked his phone notifications.
An official Academy notification appeared on his communicator.
[Status Updated]
[Elite Student]
[Access Granted]
[Student Points: 0]
Lian stared at the screen for a few seconds. From today, he was no longer a normal student. He was an elite student.
He looked at his student points, which were zero. These points are like currency in the Academy, earned through achievements and completing various missions.
With them, you can buy all kinds of equipment, items, and information. You can even buy skill books or various treasures that can permanently increase stats.
An example of that is mana crystals, of which he had several. By absorbing each one, you can increase mana by 1 to 5 points depending on the crystal’s quality.
Naturally, there are special treasures for other stats as well, but they are expensive and valuable. Fortunately, he does not need such things.
He got up and went to the bathroom. After finishing, he put on his Academy uniform and headed to his class.
The elite class building was located in the northern part of the Academy. Unlike the normal buildings, this one was much larger and more modern.
Armed guards stood at the entrance.
Students with expensive equipment came and went. All of them were Awakened, and all of them were considered the top talents of their generation.
When Lian entered the building, several looks fell on him.
Some were indifferent, some curious, some hostile, and many did not even recognize his face and wondered why he had come to the elite building.
He entered the classroom without paying attention to them. Inside the class, about twenty students were present. Almost all were level five or six.
A few were level seven.
All elites, all proud, and at least elite classes, even some with four-star classes, were present.
When Lian entered, whispers began.
"Is that him?"
"The survivor of the tenth realm?"
"I heard he became level ten."
"Nonsense."
"Impossible."
The atmosphere immediately became heavy, but Lian ignored it and sat in one of the empty seats. There were only two empty seats, next to each other.
A few minutes later.
The classroom door opened. A tall man entered. Short gray hair, a cold face, sharp eyes, and a presence that made the entire class immediately fall silent.
Professor Valerius Kane.
One of the senior combat professors. A man who had gone through two evolutions.
"Good morning." He stood in front of the class without any introduction.
"It seems we have a new student. So let me introduce myself once again."
"I am Valerius Kane, professor of practical and theoretical combat. An Awakened at level 46 who has gone through two evolutions."
"I don’t care what family you are from. I don’t care how much money you have."
"And I don’t care who your father is." Complete silence ruled the class.
"If you are weak, you are weak. If you are strong, you are strong. Here, only results matter."
Then his gaze paused on Lian.
"And it seems today we have an interesting student." Several students turned toward Lian.
Valerius opened a folder.
"Since we have a new student today... I will explain the rules of the elite class again."
He began to walk.
"First, no one here gets respect because of their age or background. Respect must be earned."
"Second."
"Rankings change every month. If you are weak, you will drop, be expelled from the class, and return to the normal class."
"If you are strong, you move up."
"And third."
"Our classes are more practical than theoretical."
Valerius closed the folder.
A very faint smile appeared on his face. A smile that made several students unconsciously sit up straight, because they had learned in previous sessions that this smile was not a good sign.
"Good. So today we are not wasting time."
He moved toward the classroom door.
"Today we have a practical class. Everyone get ready." Then his gaze turned on the students one last time.
"We are going to the simulation ground."
And at that moment, the confident smiles of several elite students faded.
Because they all knew that in Professor Valerius’s classes, the simulation ground was not a place to go for fun.
It was a place where pride was crushed.
And for Lian, his first day in the elite class had just begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 50: The New Star
paragraphs: The massive doors of the simulation ground opened with a heavy sound.
Hundreds of meters underground, there was a hall that looked more like a real battlefield than a training class.
Giant metal walls, watchtowers, massive mana crystals, and dozens of combat rings scattered across the field.
As soon as the students entered, whispers rose. Even many elite students rarely got permission to use this place.
Professor Valerius stood in the center of the field, his hands locked behind his back, his cold eyes scanning the students.
"Today we are holding a practical test. I want to see how much each of you is really worth."
"A full team including a tank, a shooter, a healer, a warrior covers all of each other’s weaknesses and can show their best during battle."
"But what about alone? When all your teammates are dead and you have to fight alone to survive and continue the battle?"
"I want to see what you know so I can know what I need to teach you."
The atmosphere immediately became serious. No one was joking. No one was smiling. Everyone knew that Valerius’s tests were notoriously harsh.
A man who had crushed many arrogant students in front of everyone.
The crowd moved to the first field. In the center of the field was a red crystal. A crystal capable of creating simulated monsters.
Valerius explained.
"First test, combat power. Each person fights a monster alone. The monster’s rank is determined according to your power."
"Healers can stand aside and do not need to participate."
"You can use everything I have taught you this week. But in my view, the best teaching is experience. You won’t learn anything until you are put in that situation."
Some students smiled. This test was their specialty.
A few minutes later, the test began. The first student entered the field. A level three monster appeared.
The battle was short, but the student managed to win. Brief cheers were heard.
Second person.
Third person.
Fourth person.
Gradually, the results became clear. Most elite students were between level five and seven. Exactly what was expected.
For them, defeating normal level two and three monsters alone was not hard.
Then it was Lian’s turn.
As soon as his name was announced, everyone’s gaze turned toward him. The unknown boy who had suddenly become the hot topic of the entire Academy.
"The survivor of the tenth realm... I still don’t believe it." Darren Will laughed mockingly.
He was Roderick’s best friend in the elite class and also the number one among his subordinates. A true genius with a three-star warrior class.
In terms of overall power, he was among the top five students in the elite class.
Two of his friends laughed.
"He probably hid behind a rock until everyone else died." Darren continued.
A few others also smiled, but Lian did not even look at him, as if he had not heard anything.
This indifference made the vein on Darren’s forehead bulge.
Lian entered the field. Valerius looked at the control panel, and his eyes paused on Lian’s information for a moment.
Then, without any change in his expression, he entered a number.
The crystal began to shine. A moment later... a massive creature appeared.
The sound of several people’s breathing stopped.
"Level twelve?!"
"Damn!"
"Is the professor serious?!"
"A two-level difference?!"

A level twelve monster was no joke. Moreover, the student who was supposed to fight this monster was level ten! Yes, he had a higher level than his peers, but that did not mean he could fight such a monster.
To defeat such a monster, a full team is needed.
But Valerius just stood quietly.
The monster roared.
The ground shook.
Then it charged straight at Lian. Its speed was high, its power was high, and for a first-year student, it was almost certain death.
But... Lian just took one step. That was all. One step, and his body vanished like a shadow. The monster was still charging when suddenly, a deadly cold filled the field.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
The ice claw passed through the air.
Silence.
The monster took one more step.
Two steps.
Then its head slowly separated from its body. Its massive body fell to the ground.
BOOM!
The entire field shook. Complete silence ruled. No one spoke. Even the sound of some people’s breathing could be heard.
Darren was stunned. His eyes almost bulged out of their sockets.
A level twelve monster... killed with one hit.
On the other side, a girl with long golden hair looked at Lian with shining eyes and licked her lips, as if she had found new prey.
While another girl next to the golden-haired girl sighed and then her gaze also fell on Lian, but with a thoughtful look.
"Maybe he will be useful for our group," she whispered to herself.
Valerius said nothing, but a faint gleam appeared in his eyes. He had seen exactly what he expected.
"The first test is over. Fortunately, none of you did badly in this test, but there are points I need to mention after watching your battles."
"First, the monsters were weaker than you, yet you still took too long to win. That is not good. If the monster was stronger than you, what would you do?"
Everyone fell silent. If the monster was stronger than them? Could they even do anything?
"The answer is simple. You have to use your brain. Find the monster’s weakness, use the environment, try to confuse the monster and perform sneak attacks."

"If you face much stronger monsters where you naturally have no chance, you will simply die. But if the power difference can be compensated, use whatever is necessary to win, even if you lose your arms and legs, it doesn’t matter."
"Plan ahead and win."
Then the field changed shape again. Hundreds of traps, moving walls, mana blades, and various obstacles appeared.
"Speed test. Whoever crosses the path fastest gets the higher rank." Valerius announced.
Students entered one by one. The results were not bad. Some performed well, some were average, but no one could break the field’s record.
Then it was Lian’s turn.
He entered the path. Valerius gave the start command, and at that moment... for many students... Lian almost disappeared.
"What...?" One of the girls said unconsciously.
The only thing that could be seen was a faint shadow. The traps activated, but none could even get close to him.
Ten seconds later...
Lian appeared at the end of the path.
Silence.
Then a sound echoed through the field.
[New Record Achieved]
This time, even several elite students lost color.
Darren could no longer tolerate it. He clenched his fist and stood up.
"It’s a trick!" He shouted.
Everyone turned around.
Darren pointed directly at Lian.
"I don’t accept this! Someone who wasn’t even an Awakened until last week can’t do these things!"
No one said anything. Darren stepped forward.
"I want to fight him." If things continued like this, Lian would become the new star of the class, and he could not allow such a thing.
Several people held their breath. Valerius was quiet for a few seconds.
"Fine." He then said.
Darren smiled.
But the professor’s next sentence dried up his smile.
"But if you lose, you will be banned from the simulation ground for one month."
Darren clenched his teeth.
"Agreed."
A few minutes later, both stood in the field. Darren drew his sword. Mana gathered around his body.
"We have no hostility. So why do you want to fight?"
"Shut up! You are stealing Brother Roderick’s position. I cannot allow that." Darren said coldly, and his skill activated.
Red flames coiled around the blade. It was an impressive display. Even some students cheered for him.
But Lian just stood quietly. He even sighed inwardly. Roderick really was good at gathering loyal subordinates.
He looked around. Everyone’s gaze was on their battle, and he could even feel two strange looks on himself.
’Who are those two girls?’ He noticed two girls who were looking at him in different ways.
One looked as if she was looking at prey, and the other as if she had found a new target...?

He ignored them for now and focused his attention on Darren. He did not back down from this fight because he had a goal. He wanted to solidify his position in the elite class by decisively defeating this fool.
He still had not forgotten how Roderick had humiliated him, and he wanted to make sure that when he came back, he would have no place in this class.
His face at that time would be worth seeing, right?
And he would become the number one of the class.
"Start!"
Darren shouted and attacked. His sword split the air.
But... Lian just took one step. Then he punched. No skill, no flashy effects, no explosion. Just a simple punch.
BOOM!
Darren was lifted off the ground like a torn doll, flew several meters, and landed hard on the ground.
Absolute silence took over.
The fight had not even lasted three seconds.
Darren tried to get up but could not. His face was red from humiliation, while the entire class was looking at him.
Valerius finally smiled. A very small but genuine smile. He stepped into the field. The sound of his footsteps echoed.
Darren’s face turned white.
The professor stood in front of Lian. His eyes locked directly onto Lian’s.
"Good." Then he placed his hands behind his back.
"Darren, I don’t want to see you here for one month. Get out."
Darren wanted to say something, but in the middle of his words, he swallowed them. With humiliation and shame, he stood up and left the place.
The students’ gazes fell on him but quickly moved away and stared at Lian.
Had a new king appeared in their class?

"You are not bad in combat, but you don’t know how and when to use your skills. Your speed is not bad either, but you have poor intuition and fall into traps, and you use your power to escape when that is not the point." Valerius continued.
"The rest of the day’s training is set. I will assign specialized simulations for each of you to solve these problems."
"But before that, there is the final test. I want to see if you know what responsibility and decision-making are. Do you know what your duty is to the people and the nation?"
"Well, we will soon find out if you know or not."
